content_zh: 我在巴西是传教士, 我周围是教堂, 巴西有丰富的传教士历史,他们留下了现在向其他国家派遣传教士的教会遗产. 这提出了一个问题:我们是否应该派遣传教士到已经存在教堂的国家去? 我们不应该认为那些地区已经“到达”了, 这是一个公平的问题, 在回答之前, 有几个因素需要考虑: 记得PAUL的ExAMPLE吗? 对,保罗部相当一部分是教会的传教士。 但他并没有放弃这些被新建的教堂. 保罗也是一名加强教会的传教士. 他重新审视了所种植的教堂(第14:21-23;15:36;18:22-23号法案)。 他给这些教堂写了信,因为他需要更多的教他们(1 Thess 3:10). 他甚至派遣了自己的传教工人去他之前所到的地区:提奇丘斯去以弗所和克洛斯塞,提图斯去科林斯,克勒特去和达尔马提亚去,提摩西去以弗所等城市去. 令人惊讶的是,我们没有任何保罗派遣传教士前往未到达的地区的记录,而只是前往他已经到达的地区。 保罗为我们创造了有用的类别。 我们看到罗马人的15个先锋任务,但我们也看到14号行动加强教堂的任务。 我们是否应该派传教士到已经存在教堂的地方? 保罗向我们展示了一个圣经类的任务。 事实上,保罗做到了。 考虑中国的健康 这些年来,我训练了牧师,我遇到了令人震惊的情况:教会容忍不道德,牧师不理解简单的福音信息,教会领导人不知不觉地把异端归罪于他们的教会。 许多教会要么接受繁荣神学, 但当我们只考虑真正福音派教会时, 如果我们想把它进一步切入到健康的教堂里, 数字变得非常微弱。 考虑教会的健康。 如果我们忽视“接触”领域,我们就有可能在短短几代人中产生新的未接触人群。 理解政府基础设施的需要 因此,传教士在“传入”国家的作用是什么? 在大背景下考虑传教士对上帝在该国已经采取的行动的作用是有益的。 这是福音基础设施的特色 如此有帮助。 这样想:一个城市需要建立某些结构(如道路网、供水和能源网),以便它能够继续存在并在未来兴起。 同样地,大委员会要求的远远不止于最初的福音. 国家教会要发展和再生,就必须建立“神道基础设施”。 这开始于福音会,圣经翻译,并种植健康的教堂,但也包括了基督教文学,地方牧师培训,地方崇拜音乐,和神学院. 任务涉及国家教会需要的一切,因此他们可以继续为后代种植健康的教堂. 当派遣传教士前往已经拥有教堂的地区时,我们需要问传教士的礼物和全国教会的需求在哪里交叉. 例如,巴西可能不需要传教士来种植更多的教堂,但在神学院和地方牧师培训方面仍有巨大的需要. 任务 Churches已经存在 我们是否应该派传教士到已经存在教堂的地方? 根据保罗自己的例子,答案是肯定的。 我们应继续派遣大委员会的工人到任何需要健康教堂和福音基础设施的地方去。 愿我们愉快地服务于

title: How Ordinary Christians Can Help Others Follow Jesus
summary: Salvador Blanco-Perello shows how everyday activities can become opportunities to help others follow Jesus.
summary_zh: Salvador Blanco-Perello展示了日常活动如何成为帮助他人跟随耶稣的机会。
title_zh: 普通基督徒如何帮助他人跟随耶稣
content: Ask a handful of Christians to define “discipling,” and you’ll probably get a handful of different answers . Some may mention meeting with another follower of Jesus for an hour each week. Another might say it means attending the weekly Sunday school class on discipleship. Someone else says it involves teaching another Christian how to make disciples who disciple others . But ultimately, discipling others means giving someone access to your life. That’s how Jesus did it. Jesus’ whole life was a teaching moment for his disciples. Not only the miraculous parts of his life, but the ordinary ones too. The times in between: walking, talking, eating. This approach is often inconvenient, but it was the key ingredient to Jesus’ discipleship plan. I want to propose a simple principle for discipling: bring someone with you. Sure, there’s more to discipling, but you won’t disciple anyone if you don’t bring anyone along to what you’re already doing as a follower of Jesus. Call it discipling as double-duty. Imagine what it could look like. By doing something as simple as sitting in worship with someone, you may learn how to serve your own family better. Perhaps you’ll see how a young father serves his wife by taking the baby out so his wife can focus on the sermon or prayers. Perhaps you’ll be able to model your own worship habits. Corporate worship is a form of discipling. In fact, it’s the center from which all discipling flows . We learn to worship Jesus privately as we learn from other Christians publicly. Don’t miss on what you can teach or learn by observing Christians around you before, during, and after worship services. Or perhaps you can bring someone along to a community group to sing, pray, bear each other’s burdens, and apply the sermon more deeply to their lives. By bringing a person you’re discipling or being discipled by, perhaps you both learn new forms of hospitality . Maybe you learn how to disagree more lovingly and patiently. You learn to rejoice with those who rejoice and weep with those who weep. You could also bring someone along as you evangelize . Often, Christians don’t know how to evangelize because they’ve simply never seen another Christian do it. Does the person you disciple have a chance to see how you might share the gospel with someone? Even if you do all these things, someone you’re discipling must be able to see your walk with Jesus in order to replicate what they see in everyday life. The disciples didn’t just see Jesus preach the Sermon on the Mount . They saw the moments in between. They saw not only how he taught, but what he did after he taught. Jesus did say: “Therefore whoever relaxes one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven, but whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven” (Matt. 5:19). Discipling as double-duty will mean bringing someone along with you to the most ordinary moments of life. It will involve both teaching and doing what Christ commands. On the grocery run. The walk around the neighborhood. The car ride when you’d rather listen to music. As you bring other followers of Jesus with you into your existing rhythms of following Jesus, don’t underestimate what God might be teaching others. All of life following Jesus can be an opportunity to disciple others. Maybe the question shouldn’t be: “How can I make more time to disciple others?” But instead: “How can I use the time I have to disciple others?” Everybody does not have time for everybody, but everybody has time for somebody.
content_zh:
让少数基督徒定义“纪律”, 有些人可能提到每周会和另一个耶稣的追随者会面一小时. 另一种说法可能表示,这意味着参加每周一次的"周日"学校的门徒会. 有人说,这涉及到教另一个基督徒 如何使门徒谁门徒。
但归根结底,管教别人意味着 给别人进入你的生活。 耶稣就是这样做的。 耶稣一生都是他的门徒们的教诲时刻. 不仅是他生命中的奇迹 也是普通的 中间的时代:行走,说话,吃. 这种做法往往不方便,但它是耶稣的门徒计划的关键要素。
我想提出一个简单的纪律原则:带一个人来。 当然,还有更多的纪律约束,但如果你不把任何人带到你作为耶稣的追随者已经在做的事情上,你就不会门徒。 称其为"纪律"为"双重义务". 想象一下它会是什么样子。
通过做一些简单的事情, 和别人一起礼拜, 你可以学习如何更好地为自己的家庭服务。 可能你会看到年轻父亲如何为妻子服务, 或许你可以模仿自己的崇拜习惯。 企业崇拜是纪律约束的一种. 事实上,这是所有纪律都来自的中心。
我们在公开学习其他基督徒时,学会私下崇拜耶稣. 在礼拜活动之前、期间和之后, 或许你可以带一个人到一个社区团体去唱歌、祈祷、相互承担负担,
基督教徒通常不会传福音, 门徒们有没有机会 看看你如何和别人分享福音? 即使你做了这些事,你纪律严明的人 也必须能看到你和耶稣的行走, 以复制他们在日常生活中看到的。
门徒们不只看到耶稣在山上宣扬赛门教。 他们看到了中间的瞬间 他们不仅看到了他如何教书,还看到了他在教书后的所作所为.
耶稣确实说过:“因此,凡放松这些最最次要的诫命之一并教别人做同样的事情的人,在天国中称为最少的;凡这样做并教他们的人,在天国中称为伟大”(Matt. 5:19)。 分离为双重义务 将意味着带人 与你一起生活 最普通的时刻。
它既包括教学,也包括执行基督的命令。 在杂货跑。 绕行相邻. 你宁愿听音乐, 当你把其他的耶稣追随者带入你跟随耶稣的节奏时, 追随耶稣的所有生命都可以成为门徒他人的机会.
也许问题不应该是:我怎样才能让更多的时间给别人? 却取而代之:"我如何能用我的时间去门徒? 每个人都没有时间为每个人, 但每个人都有时间为某人。

title: The Importance of Non-Instrumental Activity
summary: The Secret Hobbies of Mike Tomlin (and Bryan Jarrell)   The post  The Importance of Non-Instrumental Activity  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
summary_zh: Mike Tomlin （和Bryan Jarrell ）的秘密爱好The post The Importance of Non-Instrumental Activity首次出现在Mockingbird上。
title_zh: 非仪器活动的重要性
content: Here’s something that retired Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin and I have in common: we both have secret hobbies that we don’t talk about. My hobby is houseplants. About two years ago, I decided I needed a hobby that was affordable, indoors, incapable of being monetized, offered zero status, and could be managed while raising two preschool-aged kids. The result was a half-priced money tree purchased off the clearance rack from Lowe’s. It was touch and go at first: two of the four “trunks” braided together on this money tree were dying of root rot, and it took me a while to figure out the right lighting and a good watering schedule. (Did you know that most houseplants don’t die from lack of water but from being overwatered? The more you know!) Once I figured all that out, my money tree stabilized, and a new hobby was born. About twelve years ago, the then head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers, Coach Tomlin, started playing Minecraft with his two preteen sons. For the unfamiliar, Minecraft is like a digital game of Legos, and while there are competition elements to the game, Coach Tomlin felt the draw of the game’s free-play mode, which allowed gamers to build their own creations out of the game’s various styles of bricks. Earlier this fall, having moved from coaching football to broadcasting, Tomlin disclosed his twelve-year Minecraft hobby to the world, offering a YouTube live stream tour of a city that he had spent more than a decade building from digital bricks. Both gamers and sports fans responded in mutual shock. If you’re not an NFL or sports fan, you might not know that Mike Tomlin is one of sport’s most respected head coaches, famously stringing together nineteen years of coaching without a single losing season. He won the Super Bowl in 2009 and kept the Steelers among football’s most winning franchises. One of his talents was keeping the sport’s most “diva” players in winning form. When top-flight players would leave the Steelers for other teams, many would go on to have public crashouts and exit the league in embarrassing failures. Players uniformly loved Tomlin, and many viewed him as a surrogate father figure. But when the Sunday Night Lights were off, and when the family was cared for, and when the man had some free time, the famous head coach was on his laptop playing Minecraft. This is as unusual as it is amazing. Professional sports of all stripes are marked by an “all-in” mentality. Everything is secondary to the game, whether it’s diet, exercise, sleep, even family and friendships. The money is just too much and the stakes are too high to be anything but 100% focused on preparing for the game ahead. And yet, Coach Tomlin achieved his incredible results while spending a lot of time hanging out in the land of the chicken jockey. Gamers have been just as shocked as the football fans. When Tomlin hosted his YouTube live stream of his city, it garnered universal appreciation from other Minecraft players. It was big, well designed, and orderly down to every last detail and accent. In the great divide between the nerds and the jocks, here was a jock who could keep up with the nerds. Arthur Brooks, the social science good-life guru, had lots to say about Tomlin’s hobby over at the Free Press . He confessed to being “gobsmacked” at the news and took the moment to reflect on his own lack of hobbies. Sparing you the requisite “here’s what a bunch of scholarly studies found about hobbies” bits that populate Brooks’ articles, here’s what stood out: A key element of a hobby that brings happiness is that the rewards must not be extrinsic. By this, I mean the hobby can’t run up your personal or professional scoreboard in terms of money, power, or prestige. The rewards must be intrinsic, involving personal growth, enjoyment, or drawing closer to others. Psychologists have long found a huge happiness difference between these two types of reward. 对于不熟悉的人来说,"Minecraft"就像一款"Legos"的数字游戏,虽然游戏中存在竞争元素,但主教练汤姆林感受到了游戏自由游戏模式的图画,这使得游戏者能够从游戏的各种花砖风格中打造出自己的创作.

今年秋天早些时候,汤姆林从教练足球转向广播,他向世界披露了自己十二年的"Minecraft"爱好,提供YouTube活溪游览一个他用数字砖建造了十多年的城市. 比赛双方球迷和体育迷均在相互冲击下响应.

当顶级飞行的球员会离开钢人队前往其他球队时,许多人会继续公开出场并因尴尬的失败而退出联赛. 玩家一致地爱戴了托姆林,许多人将他视为代父人物.

title: October 24-30
summary: Halloween's Sugar Fiction, New York Friction, the History of CrossFit, and Freud vs. Modern Pop Psychology   The post  October 24-30  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
summary_zh: 万圣节的糖果小说、纽约摩擦、CrossFit的历史和弗洛伊德与现代流行心理学10月24日至30日的帖子首次出现在知更鸟上。
content: 1. At his Substack, Tim Kreider eulogizes the model shops where he dithered in Covid times and the other quirky, abrasive, irreplaceable businesses that are ever more quickly dwindling in Manhattan. There are few things as authentic feeling as genuine indifference to your presence (or antagonism to it). Kreider describes what’s been lost in our frictionless contemporary world: You find the thing you want, you click on it; a day or two later, the thing you wanted arrives. It’s true you don’t have any discomfiting encounters with misanthropes or wackos, but you also don’t come home with any stories. […] The trip to the model shop, including the weird quirks of the owner, used to be as much a part of making a model as sanding or painting it. But for a lot of increasingly timid, introverted consumers, not having to interact with any human beings when they need something is the whole point of the internet. Which is why Jeff Bezos got to rent Venice for his wedding, and one reason people now seem so grotesquely maladjusted to interacting with each other, or living in a society. […] Look: I am as ambivalent as you about Other People. Other People are problematic, impossible. I don’t want to get too sentimentally nostalgic about the lost joys of real-life encounters with crazy, abrasive human beings. I did not enjoy being treated like a contemptible dilettante or a simpleton when all I wanted was to buy some glue. […] But we need the brush and abrasion of Other People, including — maybe even especially — annoying and difficult ones. Because look at the world we’ve constructed to avoid it. If it’s a choice between awkward conversations with eccentrics and cranks or this infinite blank impenetrable wall of corporate contempt we all now face daily — the constant, soul-eroding hassle of creating an account with a unique username and novel password including capital and lowercase letters plus at least one numeral and symbol for every single transaction or errand, scanning a QR code, downloading the app […] accidentally clicking on a popup and scrambling to close the blaring garish page it opens, being asked to take a moment to fill out a brief survey to rate your experience! and Let Them Know How They’re Doing, briefly explain your reason for cancelling, and having to delete one last “We’re Sorry to See You Go!” email — I know which world I choose. Shopping used to be one of the few things that forced us to engage with others, in ways that abrade us but also give to us. Give what? It’s intangible, but maybe just a sense for a reality beyond ourselves. I’m reminded of a quote from Thomas de Zengotita’s brilliantly prophetic Mediated , that “the opposite of real isn’t phony or illusional or fictional — it’s optional.” I think part of what he’s getting at is that anything optional is, once chosen, something that you constructed, something you are responsible for, whose existence depends on your own. What feels real is the thing that exists outside of you — that bracing feeling you get on a mountain or at McSorley’s that the world exists utterly apart from you and will go on existing apart from anything you do. It’s those sorts of encounters, given rather than constructed, arising naturally from a human soul rather than private equity market modeling and focus groups, that seem to get lost in today’s world. Maybe our 2027 NYC Conference will finally be my year for a platza. 2. On Tuesday, journalist Calum Marsh published a history of CrossFit , which seems like a gold mine for tracing the seculosity of fitness in our culture, at least if this week’s profile in UnHerd is anything to go by. Apparently CrossFit pioneered the model, common today, of pricey subscriptions to a high-intensity exercise program that function not just for health but as an arena in which one can pursue personal excellence. At the time, the metrics were revolutionary, and the idea that an adult would pay to be yelled at seemed fantastical. The eccentric visionary who star
content_zh: 1. 在他的Substack,Tim Kreider赞美了他在科维德时代抖动的模范店铺,以及曼哈顿日益迅速倒闭的其他奇特、粗糙和不可替代的企业。 很少有像真正漠不关心你的存在(或对你的敌意)那样真实的感觉。 Kreider描述了在当代世界失去的东西: 你找到你想要的东西,你点击它; 一两天后,你想要的东西到达。 确实,你没有遇到任何不愉快的人类或疯子, 模特店之行,包括店主的怪怪怪之行,曾是制作"模特"同"打砂"或"作画"一样的重要一环. 但对于许多越来越胆小的、内向的消费者来说, 当他们需要东西时, 不需要与任何人互动是互联网的整个点。 这就是为什么杰夫·贝佐斯不得不租给威尼斯参加他的婚礼, 这也是人们现在看起来如此怪异的不适应 彼此互动或生活在一个社会中的原因。 你看:我和你一样对别人充满矛盾。 其他人有问题,不可能 我并不想对现实生活中与疯狂而残忍的人类相遇所失去的欢乐怀念太多。 我并不喜欢被当做一个可鄙的二手货 或简单的人对待 当我只想买些胶水的时候 但我们需要其他人的刷子和磨擦,包括——也许甚至特别——烦人和困难的人。 因为看看我们所构建的世界, 如果在与古怪分子和曲柄的尴尬对话之间做出选择, 或者在这种无限空白的企业蔑视墙上, 我们每天都会面临这种不断的、令人心痛的麻烦, 让他们知道自己在做什么, 简单解释你取消的原因, 并删除最后一封“我们很遗憾看到你走!”电子邮件, 购物曾经是少数迫使我们与他人接触的事物之一,其方式使我们感到愤怒,但也给了我们。 给什么? 但也许只是对现实的感想, 我还记得托马斯·德·泽戈蒂塔(Thomas de Zengotita)辉煌地预言的“Mediated”的一篇文章,“与真实相反的不是虚构的、幻想的或虚构的,而是可选的。 ” 我认为,他得到的一部分是,任何可选的事物,一旦被选中,都是你构建的,你负责的,它的存在取决于你自己。 感觉真实的是你身外存在的东西 — — 吹嘘地感觉你在山上或在麦克索利的山上,世界的存在与你完全不同,并且会与你所做的一切相去甚远。 在今天的世界中,似乎迷路的是那些自然产生于人的灵魂而不是私人股权市场模型和焦点团体的交会。 也许我们2027年的纽约公会 终于能成为我的一年了 2. 记者Calum Marsh星期二发表了"CrossFit"(CrossFit)的历史, 显然,CrossFit开创了一种模式, 即今天常见的, 一个高强度的锻炼计划, 它不仅为健康运作, 并且是一个可以追求个人卓越的舞台。 当时的度量衡是革命性的,一个成年人会付出代价去被骂的想法看起来是奇幻的. 怪异的想象力谁的明星

title: The Shapelessness of Evil
summary: A Discussion of  Halloween  (2018)   The post  The Shapelessness of Evil  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
summary_zh: 万圣节讨论（ 2018 ）《邪恶的无形》一文首次出现在《知更鸟》上。
title_zh: 邪恶的无形
content: Happy Halloweek, boils and ghouls! Halloween is right around the corner, and so is Michael Myers, back to show everyone why he is the undisputed master slasher! Blaine Grimes, Blake Collier, Caleb Stallings, and I are in our Halloween best and invite you to join us in watching Halloween (2018). Ian : I picked this because it takes me back so vividly to October 2018 and seeing it with my wife, Kristin, and her sister, Anna. Weird as it may sound, this flick lights my heart up like a dozen M-80s in a jack-o’-lantern. I was excited for Michael Myers to return to the big screen and for a new generation to reckon with the horror of The Shape. Caleb : This was the first movie my wife, Aleece, and I ever saw together. Our second date! It’ll always be important to me for that reason alone, but it’s also important to me because it’s a good Halloween sequel! Blake : This movie will forever hold a dear place in my marriage as the first film I took my wife to that caused her to cry and to lose sleep. The first Halloween she watched, she didn’t even bat an eye. This one was just too much for her. Caleb : Wild that we all associate this, for good or for ill, with our wives! Blake : Except Blaine, who just saw it for the first time, right? Blaine : Yeah. I’ve only ever seen the OG and this one. Blake : That is WILD. Caleb : Do you think this one stands out more than others, Ian? Ian : In some significant ways, yes. Halloween (2018) resets the board by proceeding as if there had never been a sequel to the 1978 Halloween . Even titling this film Halloween shows how it positions itself as spiritual successor to the original, and it kind of implicitly announces that nothing with that word and a number after it matters. Caleb : I will admit, I am a sucker for all the various timelines and reboots. But I think this is far and away the best one. Ian : Don’t get me wrong, I enjoy certain sequels before this, but it’s largely in the same way I enjoy the Friday the 13th sequels: schlocky fun. Blake : I don’t hate any of the sequels. But this and its subsequent two films were the first time I felt giddy about being in Haddonfield again. Ian : Halloween (2018) definitely seeks to accomplish something amid its slasher spectacle. I think it wants to go back to basics in showcasing Michael as the evacuated site and vessel of evil: The Shape. Caleb : It’s fascinating how they have to cast the horror of Michael killing five people in 1978 against the larger horror of the subsequent 40 years in American society. Michael isn’t the most prolific serial killer. There have been worse threats than him, but still: he is an avatar of the shapeless Shape of evil. So I think Laurie gets it right later when she talks about how hard and dark the world is. All of us have to be prepared for it. The question is How can we be? Ian : You’re actually approaching something I’m sensing this time around. Although this film officially disavows forty years of sequels, it nevertheless assumes their lore, after a fashion, precisely because the Michael of Halloween (1978) murdered five people, but there’s a mythos to Michael here as though he had carried out everything in those sequels. Caleb : It definitely reckons with its own lore. Laurie’s granddaughter’s friends hear rumors that Laurie was Michael’s sister, which alludes to Halloween 2 (1981). But the truth is much scarier: he’s not related to Laurie at all. His stalking and tormenting her is utterly inscrutable; random. And I think a thesis of this movie is that the world is the same: full of random horror that we can’t ever truly parse out in this life. Michael just happens to be one personification of that. Ian : One of the most satisfying things to me was how the inmates at the asylum chitter and cry out when the mask is presented to Michael, like they sense a power drawing near. That shapeless evil seeks a vessel but also a shape. Michael is at the ready but seeks union with the mask. It’s an anti-wholeness: a complete evac
content_zh: 祝你们万事如意! 万圣节就在拐角处 迈克尔·迈尔斯也在这 向大家展示为什么他是无可争议的刀手! Blaine Grimes Blake Collier Caleb Stallings 我参加万圣节最佳演出 邀请你加入我们观看万圣节(2018年) 伊恩:我选这个是因为它让我生动地回到了2018年10月,并与我的妻子克莉丝汀和她的妹妹安娜一起看到了它. 这个闪光照亮了我的心, 我很兴奋迈克尔·迈尔斯回到大屏幕上 以及新一代人去考虑"形状"的恐怖 凯勒布: 这是我妻子艾莉丝的第一部电影 我曾经一起看过 我们的第二次约会! 但对我来说也很重要, 因为它是一部很好的万圣节续集。 布莱克: 这部电影将永远占据我婚姻中最珍贵的一席之地,作为我带我妻子去看的第一部电影,她因此哭泣并失眠. 她看的第一个万圣节, 这个对她来说太过分了 凯勒布:我们为了好,为了病,为了我们的妻子,把这件事联系起来,真是疯狂! 布莱克:除了布莱恩,谁刚刚第一次看到它,对不对? 对 我只见过OG和这个。 这是WILD。 你觉得这个比其他人更突出吗,伊恩? 伊恩: 在某些重要方面,是的。 万圣节(2018年)通过程序重放板子, 即使授权这部电影万圣节也展示了它如何将自己定位为原作的灵性接班人,它隐含地宣布了这个词和之后的数字都无关紧要. Caleb:我承认,我对各种时限和重回潮流都是个傻瓜。 但我认为这是最远的 Ian:别误会, 之前我还喜欢一些续集, Blake:我不讨厌任何续集。 但是,这及其之后的两部电影,是我第一次对再次出现在哈德顿菲尔德感到迷茫. Ian:万圣节(2018年)肯定在它的刀锋一现中寻求成就。 我认为它想回到基本点 展示迈克尔 被疏散的地点和邪恶的船:形状。 Caleb : 1978年迈克尔杀死了五个人,而美国社会随后的40年却发生了更大的恐怖。 迈克尔并不是最有实力的连环杀手。 曾经有比他更严重的威胁,但仍然:他是一个无形状的邪恶形状的造型. 所以,我想劳里得到它的权利 稍后,当她谈到 多么艰难和黑暗的世界是。 我们所有人都必须为此做好准备。 问题是,我们怎么能这样? (笑声) 伊恩:你实际上正在接近我这次所感知的东西。 虽然这部电影正式否定了40年的续集,但它仍然假定了他们的神话,在时尚化后,正是因为万圣节的迈克尔(1978年)谋杀了五个人,但迈克尔在这里有一个神话,好像他在那些续集中完成了一切。 凯勒布: 它肯定用它自己的神话来考虑 Laurie的孙女朋友听说Laurie是Michael的妹妹, 但事实更可怕:他与劳里根本不相干。 他跟踪和折磨她完全是不可理喻的,是随意的。 我认为这部电影的一个论点是世界是相同的:充满了随机的恐怖,而我们无法在这样的生活中真正地理解。 迈克尔恰好就是个人物 Ian:我最满意的一件事是 当面具被出示给Michael时, 精神病院的囚犯们哭喊着, 好像他们感觉到力量在接近。 这种无形的邪恶既寻求一种容器,也寻求一种形状。 迈克尔已经准备好了,但寻求与面具结合。 这是一个反整齐:一个完整的撤离
author: Ian Olson

title: Fear Itself
summary: Widow's Bay  and the Trolley Problem of Life   The post  Fear Itself  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
summary_zh: 寡妇湾和生活的手推车问题帖子Fear Itself首先出现在Mockingbird上。
title_zh: 恐惧自身
content: W hat is your biggest fear? Spiders? That’s a classic. Deranged clowns? Sure! Maybe you prefer the more existential variety? How about never fully realizing your potential or dying alone? All of the above? Similar to the What superpower would you choose? question, it is hard for me to select only one. I am a fearful person. I have a way of collecting fears as I go about my life. Alpha-gal, something I did not know existed until two days ago, is the flavor of the week. But my fear of dying alone is more like a longtime, trusted companion. The world is a scary place. At any moment, our identities could be hacked. Our phones could ring with dreadful news. Our brains could suffer an aneurysm. Swimming in a bottomless sea of insecurity, we are meagerly equipped with our basic survival instincts: fight, flight, freeze, and appease. These impulses may help keep us safe from spiders and clowns (answer for both: flight!), but what do we make of the dangers that are harder to pin down? What if the dangers are not only without but within? Leave it to this year’s hit TV series to explore these questions. If you’re looking for a spooky show to get into this weekend, it’s Widow’s Bay. The Emmy-sweeping, genre-bending, horror-comedic series is a triumph for a number of reasons. For starters, it muddles the black-and-white worlds Hollywood has created (e.g., horror movies without humor, comedies without any depth), reminding us that life can be both scary and funny. The show has all the irresistible horror tropes (the harbinger who warns everyone of impending doom, the suspenseful music, the jump scares) but, along with its crowd-pleasing antics, it dives deeper than surface-level fears. Its anthropology is refreshingly low. This is not a match between good people and evil monsters. Yes, sometimes the enemy is a chainsaw-wielding fiend. Much scarier, however, is when the enemy is yourself. Take Tom Loftis, for instance, the ambitious new mayor who wants to transform the cursed island town of Widow’s Bay into the next Martha’s Vineyard. He is, from every angle, a secular man. For Tom, God is no more real than ghosts. The only higher power that exists is the one you achieve by climbing the ladder. He resents how the locals tolerate the town’s haunted reputation. For too long, people have been resigned to the rumors that the hotel is haunted, the church is cursed, and the bay isn’t safe for a swim. For Tom, the only thing to fear is fear itself. Like any mayor with a messiah complex, he sets out to do something about it. As Loftis sees things, the real problem with the place is not that it is demonically possessed. The real problem is bad branding . In his eyes, Widow’s Bay is simply misunderstood. When visiting Widow’s Bay to write a piece for the New York Times travel section, a reporter asks Loftis about a framed article in the historical society titled “Cannibalism in God’s House.” Loftis tries to water it down. “These stories get so exaggerated over time,” he says. “Was there a deadly storm in 1786? Yes. Did a group of people get trapped inside a church? Apparently so. Did they immediately turn to cannibalism? No, that took four days !” See? That’s not so bad, right? Loftis’ PR campaign is like slapping new siding on a haunted mansion. He is convinced that the plight of Widow’s Bay can be solved by installing a proper cappuccino machine in the local coffee shop. Cappuccino machines are great at making a proper latte but pretty useless when up against the occult. Before long, Loftis’ denial of the curse over the island town is just as dangerous as the curse itself. The first step to keeping the forces at bay is to admit they exist. There is a scene in which Loftis speaks to another character about the Trolley Problem, an ethical thought experiment in which there is a runaway trolley barreling down the tracks toward a crowd of people. In this hypothetical setup, there is a lever that would switch the trolley to a different track with only one
content_zh: 帽子是你最大的恐惧? 蜘蛛吗? 这是经典。 疯狂的小丑? 当然! 也许你更喜欢生存的品种? 永远不能充分发挥你的潜力 或孤独地死去怎么样? 所有这一切? 类似于你选择的超级大国? 问,我很难只选一个 我是一个害怕的人。 我有办法收集恐惧 当我去我的生活。 Alpha -gal,我两天前才知道的东西 是这个星期的口味 但我害怕孤独地死去 更像是长期 值得信赖的同伴 世界是个可怕的地方。 我们的身份随时可能被黑入 我们的电话可能会传出可怕的消息 我们的大脑可能会有动脉瘤 在一个不安全的无底海中游来游去,我们装备了我们的基本生存本能:战斗、出逃、冻结和安抚。 这些冲动也许可以帮助我们远离蜘蛛和小丑(回答:飞行!),但我们如何应对那些更难消除的危险? 如果危险不仅是没有危险,而且是内部危险呢? 让今年的电视连续剧来探讨这些问题。 如果你想要一个恐怖的节目进入这个周末, "艾美扫地"(英語:Emmy-sweating, genre-bending),"恐怖喜剧"(英語:Description-comed)系列,由于多种原因,是一场胜利. 首先,它搅乱了好莱坞所创造的黑白世界(例如没有幽默感的恐怖电影,没有任何深度的喜剧),提醒我们生活既会恐怖又会搞笑. 该节目拥有所有不可抗拒的恐怖颤抖(预告会警告所有人即将来临的末日,悬疑的音乐,跳跃的惊吓等),但连同其人群取悦的焦虑,其潜入比地表恐惧更深. 它的人类学水平低得惊人 这不是好人和邪恶怪物的对决 是的,有时敌人是一个 链锯的恶魔。 然而,更可怕的是当敌人是你自己的时候。 以汤姆·洛夫蒂斯(Tom Loftis)为例, 他,从每个角度来说,都是世俗的人. 对汤姆来说,上帝不比鬼更真实. 唯一高的电能是通过攀登梯子实现的. 当地民众如何容忍镇上闹事的名声? 久而久之,人们对旅馆闹鬼、教堂被诅咒、海湾游泳不安全等谣言辞职。 对汤姆来说,唯一害怕的是恐惧本身. 像任何拥有救世主建筑群的市长一样,他开始对此有所行动. 正如洛夫提斯所见 这个地方真正的问题不是 它被恶魔附身 真正的问题是品牌不好 在他眼中,寡妇湾只是被误解了。 当一位记者访问寡妇湾为纽约时报旅行部写出一篇作品时,他问洛夫蒂斯关于历史社会中一篇被设定为“神殿中的食人狂”的文章。 洛夫提斯试图给它浇水 他说,“这些故事随着时间的推移变得如此夸张。” “1786年是否有致命的风暴? 对 一群人被困在教堂里了吗? 显然如此。 他们有没有立即转向吃人? 不,那需要四天时间!” 这还不算太糟吧? Loftis的公关活动就像在闹鬼的豪宅上再拍一拍。 他相信寡妇湾的困境可以通过在当地咖啡店安装适当的卡布奇诺机器来解决。 卡布奇诺机器很擅长做一个正宗的拿铁 但和神秘主义作对时却很没用 不久之后,洛夫蒂斯否认对岛屿城镇的诅咒,与诅咒本身同样危险。 阻止势力存在的第一步是承认它们的存在. 有个场景让洛夫蒂斯向另一个角色讲述了"特罗莱问题"(Trolley Problem),这是一场道德思想实验,其中有一个跑跑的推车管向一行人冲去. 在这个假想的设定中,有一个杠杆,可以把推车换到只有一跑道的另一跑道.

title: A Crazy Train Crying in the Wilderness
summary: Ozzy Osbourne's Plea to Be Heard   The post  A Crazy Train Crying in the Wilderness  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
summary_zh: Ozzy Osbourne的《Pleas to Be Heard》《A Crazy Train Crying in the Wilderness》一文首次出现在《知更鸟》上。
title_zh: 疯狂的火车在荒野中哭泣
content: No matter who won or lost the last big game you attended, chances are, Ozzy Osbourne was there in electronic chains, locked inside a brain-rattling sound system, unnoticed, unnamed, misunderstood, a voice crying in the wilderness of crowded rows of fans desperate for a win, cheering for their heroes while jeering at their opponents, paying too much for unnecessary carbs and calories, possibly on the sabbath day. When Ozzy cried, “All aboard!” you stood with hundreds or thousands of tangential warriors singing along with the fatalistic chorus, air guitaring with the riffs, nodding with the rhythm, but you weren’t there for music. You were there to shout, thump your chest, flex, thrust hands with fingers contorted into symbols of specific allegiance, or claim you’re #1, convinced that the song, the battle cry, and the power behind it all were on your side. The words didn’t matter. Your heroes were fighting for you, to give you hope. You’d fight for them if you could, if you had to, against whoever stands in your way, to win at all costs. But what if that’s not what Ozzy wanted? How do we know what he wanted? He screams, “You’ve got to listen to my words!” Below is a paraphrase of the “Crazy Train” lyrics: “It’s crazy, but it’s always been like this — we’re all living as enemies. But maybe it’s not too late to learn how to love and forget how to hate. We’ve all got mental wounds that aren’t healing. I’m losing it. I’ve listened to everyone — fools, preachers, anarchists. Nothing helps. There’s always a system run by someone who’s a product of the system and has been conditioned to run the system, which is sold to us by rich people who get richer by keeping the system alive. And we buy it, screaming in pain from our open mental wounds. It’s messed up. I’m messed up. We’re all messed up. We inherit each other’s trouble. We’re heirs of unresolved conflict. I keep saying it, but no one listens. You’ve got to listen to my words. I can’t figure out how to feel. The mental wounds don’t heal. I don’t know who to blame, but I know it’s not fair.” I wrote the above paraphrase to read to my senior literature class last Monday morning. Nearly half of the students in the class are varsity football starters chasing championships and full-rides. I prefaced the reading with a white lie, “I got this message from someone you all know over the weekend. I won’t tell you who it is, but I want you to help me think through how to respond.” The starting quarterback, worried, tried to interrupt me. I didn’t look up, held my hand out to pause questions, and continued reading. When I finished, there was a chorus of concern from several voices: That’s a cry for help! Is it from a boy or a girl? You said we know them? Who is it? Did they email you? What did you say? They need help. Who are you going to talk to? Still in character, I said, “I can’t tell you a name, but I’ll play this song.” A few seconds into “Crazy Train,” the students realized what was going on, looked relieved, but then became uncomfortable when I turned down the volume and read out the actual lyrics. In confused silence, their faces said, We weren’t listening . I felt bad. I smiled and apologized for manipulating their emotions, and the air lightened. Someone started singing the chorus, and we moved on. But I’m not sure we should have. “Crazy Train” is the most popular song from the most recognizable sex, drugs, and rock-n-roll villain to ever bite the head off a bat, but it’s also a cry for help from a struggling human admitting personal weakness and claiming no superiority. While suggesting that love is better than hate, he’s doing more than just asking us to love. He’s asking us to LEARN HOW TO. French philosopher and mystic, Simone Weil, who died during World War II in solidarity with residents of German-occupied France, didn’t write how-to books, but she couldn’t stop talking about attention. Her bumper sticker quote, “Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity,” is clippe
content_zh: 不管是谁赢了还是输了你参加的最后一场大赛 Ozzy Osbourne身处电子链中 被锁在脑震荡的音响系统里 无人注意 姓名不明 被误解 在一群挤满的粉丝的荒野中哭泣 渴望获胜 为他们的英雄欢呼 而嘲笑对手 付出了太多钱来换取不必要的卡布和卡路里 可能在安息日 Ozzy呼喊“所有人上船! ”你和数以百计或数以千计的勇士站在一起, 你在那里大叫,打起胸来,放出花花,用手指将手推入具体效忠的象征,或者说你是"一号",深信歌曲,战斗的叫声,以及背后的力量都站在你一边. 这些话并不重要。 你的英雄们为你而战 为了给你带来希望 如果你可以, 如果你不得不, 对抗阻碍你的人, 如果不是奥兹想要的呢? 我们怎么知道他想要什么? 他喊道:「你必须听我的话! 以下是“疯狂火车”歌词的句子:“这很疯狂, 但也许学会爱和忘记恨还不算太晚。 我们都有精神创伤, 我快输了。 我倾听了每个人的声音, 没什么用 总是有一个系统由某个人运行, 而这个人是这个系统的一个产品, 我们买下它, 在痛苦中尖叫 从我们开放的精神创伤。 情况很糟, 我搞砸了, 我们都搞砸了。 我们继承彼此的麻烦。 我们是未决冲突的继承人。 我一直这么说,但没人听 你必须听我的话。 我无法理解如何感受。 精神创伤无法愈合。 但我知道这不公平。 我写了上面的句子 上周一早上给我的高级文学班念 班上学生有近一半是 versity 足球起步者追逐冠军和全程. 我用一个白色的谎言在阅读前作了前言:“我收到了你们周末认识的人的这个信息。 但我希望你帮我思考如何回应。 开始的四分卫担心,想打断我 我并没有抬头, 我完成后,有多个声音关注的合唱: 这是求救的呼声! 是男孩还是女孩送的? 你说我们认识他们? 谁? 他们给你发邮件了吗? 你说什么? 他们需要帮助。 你要跟谁说话? 但我会演奏这首歌。 数秒钟后, 学生们意识到发生了什么, 他们的面孔模糊地沉默, 我觉得很糟。 我笑了起来,为操纵他们的情绪道歉,而空气也随之淡出. 有人开始唱合唱 我们继续 但我不确定我们是否应该这样做。 “疯狂列车”是最受欢迎的一首歌曲, 他不仅要求我们爱, 他要求我们如何学习。 法国哲学家和神秘主义者西蒙·魏尔(Simone Weil)在二战期间为声援被德意志占领的法国居民而死,她没有写如何写作的书,但她不停地谈论注意的问题. 她的保险杠贴纸引用了“注意是最罕见和最纯洁的慷慨形式”,

title: East Coker and the Cure for Human Inability
summary: "... to be restored, our sickness must grow worse."   The post  East Coker and the Cure for Human Inability  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
summary_zh: “......要恢复，我们的疾病必须变得更糟。“《East Coker and the Cure for Human Inability》一文首次出现在《知更鸟》上。
title_zh: East Coker和治疗人类残疾的方法
content: H ow strange that one can read the same poems countless times and discover new things with each visit, like a traveler coming home for Christmas only to find it slightly altered! It is the same for me revisiting T. S. Eliot’s Four Quartets : the end is different than I imagined in the beginning when I first read these words, imagined these places, and attempted to grasp the author’s meaning. Eliot had the same experience. The meaning of the Four Quartets was one thing when he originally envisioned them, another when he wrote them, and still another when the public began analyzing them. He never believed they would be forever linked with the world’s most destructive war. He had not even known there would be four. In the beginning, there was only “Burnt Norton,” written in 1936 and intended to be a one-off. It was generally well received by critics, and the whole business could have been over then. But three years passed, and Eliot found himself with that most common of authorly ailments: not knowing what to write or fearing that he no longer knew how to write properly. Specifically, he had gone for some time without constructing new poems. The world had changed since “Burnt Norton” was published. A growing menace once possible to ignore had exploded into a firestorm of destructive force sweeping through the nations of Europe, consuming all in its path. The bonds that had knit together what remained of Western Christian civilization were snapping with wild abandon, supplanted by ideologies of extermination. Faced with such a crisis, Eliot searched for the one fixed point amid the whirling chaos. He settled on the village of East Coker in Somerset, England. His ancestor Andrew Eliot had left there in 1669, abandoning the historic family home and immigrating to New England. Nearly three centuries later, Thomas Stearns Eliot had become the first member of the family to move back to the motherland, and the family connection held spiritual significance for him. In 1937, he visited St. Michael and All Angels’ Church in East Coker, where his ashes would one day be placed. I know something of Eliot’s experience. I too am the descendant of Englishmen and women whose bones lie buried in every corner of that land, some in tombs I have visited. I too was the first person in my family to return and live in England, if only for a year. It did feel in a sense like returning to my beginning, which is probably why I connect so strongly with the Four Quartets . The secret Eliot discovered at East Coker is one that has transformed my own life as well: we do not possess the power to redeem ourselves or the world and are utterly dependent on the gift of grace. Of all the Four Quartets , this is the most law and gospel poem. The Four Quartets are commonly associated with the four traditional elements of the physical world: air, earth, water, and fire. But as I have noted, Eliot did not begin with a grand plan, so the elemental symbolism becomes stronger in the later poems. Yes, we see the movement of air in “Burnt Norton” disturbing a bowl of rose leaves and carrying the laughter of children, but you would not conclude “This is an air poem” unless you had the other three Quartets to guide you. Likewise, the earth theme is not obvious after the first section of “East Coker,” but once we get to “The Dry Salvages,” we will be drowned in water imagery, and “Little Gidding” will pelt us with fire from beginning to end. Thus, Eliot begins “East Coker” rooted in the earth, in time and place and home. But immediately, the earth is overturned by the machinations of human societies succeeding and supplanting one another, building up to heaven and returning to dust. In my beginning is my end. In succession Houses rise and fall, crumble, are extended, Are removed, destroyed, restored, or in their place Is an open field, or a factory, or a by-pass. content_zh: 奇怪的是,人们可以阅读同名诗作无数次,每次拜访都会发现新的事物,就像一个旅行者回家过圣诞节,只为了发现它略有改变! 我同样重温了T. S. Eliot的四重奏:结局和我最初读到这些话、想象这些地方并试图理解作者含义时所想象的不一样。 Eliot也有同样的经历. 四重奏的意义是他最初设想它们的时候是一回事,他写它们的时候是另一回事,当公众开始分析它们的时候仍然是另一回事. 他从未相信它们会永远与世界上最具破坏性的战争联系在一起。 他甚至不知道会有四个。 一开始只有"伯恩特·诺顿"(Burnt Norton,作于1936年)一作一作一作一想. 它普遍受到批评者的好评,整个业务本来可以到那时结束. 但三年过去了,艾略特发现自己与最常见的作者病症相伴:不知道该写什么,或担心自己不再知道如何正确写作. 具体地说,他已经走了一段时间,没有创作出新诗. 自“Burnt Norton”出版以来,世界发生了变化。 日益严重的威胁一旦可能被忽视,就已演变成一股由毁灭性力量横扫欧洲各国并吞噬其道路的火焰。 将西方基督教文明遗留下来的东西联系起来的纽带,被被灭绝思想所取代而疯狂地抛弃了。 面对这样的危机,埃利奥特在旋转的混乱中寻找一个固定点. 他定居于英格兰萨默塞特的东科克村. 他的祖先安德鲁·埃利奥特于1669年离开那里,放弃了有历史意义的家族家园并移民到新英格兰. 近3个世纪后,托马斯·斯蒂恩斯·埃利奥特成为了第一个搬回祖国的家庭成员,家庭联系对他具有了精神意义. 1937年,他参观了东科克的圣迈克尔和All Angels教堂,在那里有一天他的骨灰会被放置. 我知道Eliot的经验。 我也是英国男人和女人的后人 他们的骨头埋在这片土地的每一个角落, 一些在我的访问过的坟墓。 我也是我家里第一个回到英国生活的人 哪怕只有一年 我确实感觉回到我的开始, 这可能是为什么我如此紧密地与四重奏联系起来。 Eliot在东科克发现的秘密 也改变了我自己的生活: 我们没有拯救自己或世界的能力, 完全依赖恩赐。 在所有四重奏中,这是最有法律和福音的诗. 四重奏通常与物理世界的四大传统元素相通:空气,地,水,火. 但正如我所指出,艾略特并没有从一个宏伟的计划入手,因此元素符号主义在后期诗作中变得更加强大. 是的,我们看到“Burnt Norton”中的空气运动扰乱了一碗玫瑰叶并带了孩子们的笑声,但除非有另外三个四方来指导你,否则你不会得出“这是一首空气诗”的结论。 同样地,在第一部分“东科克”之后,地球主题并不明显,但一旦我们到达“干涸的盐水”,我们将被水上图像所淹没,而“小吉丁”将从头到尾向我们开火。 因此,Eliot开始“东科克”扎根于地球、时间、地点和家园。 但是,立即,人类社会的成功和取而代之的诡计推翻了地球,使地球升入天堂并回到了尘土中。 在我开始的时候,就是我的结局。 房屋的起伏、倒塌、被延长、被拆除、被摧毁、被恢复或取代,都是空地、工厂或旁道。 如果你曾参观过萨利斯伯里平原上古老的巨石阵纪念碑 你知道它坐落在一条相交的公路上
author: Amy Mantravadi

title: A Few Thoughts on 300 Episodes of Grace (and Its Absence)
summary: Fun, Forgiveness, and Death   The post  A Few Thoughts on 300 Episodes of Grace (and Its Absence)  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
summary_zh: 乐趣、宽恕和死亡《A Few Thoughts on 300 Episodes of Grace (and Its Absence)》一文首次出现在《知更鸟》上。
title_zh: 300集恩典（及其缺席）的几点思考
content: Listeners will have a better idea of why The Mockingcast works (or doesn’t) and why they keep tuning in, 11 years later. We included a few such stories at the beginning of the 300 th episode , and the tears I shed were real. But I thought take the opportunity to offer a few observations from behind the curtain about what I personally appreciate about our podcast, what I’m most proud of, and what’s been challenging. No doubt my co-hosts would have other aspects they’d highlight. First, the longevity. It’s worth celebrating, even if it’s both a blessing and a curse. The time has allowed us to develop some pretty priceless chemistry. When I’m picking articles for us to talk about, I know that even if the material falls flat, I can rely on our dynamic to take up the slack. I trust my co-hosts, and it’s been very gratifying to watch us gel in a non-contrived way over the years. We’ve been through a lot together, and it shows, I think. Being around so long (in internet years) means we’ve had the benefit of watching things come and go. Sarah mentioned this recently in relation to the moralization of food in our society. It was super acute about eight years ago, then it retreated a bit with the body-positivity moment, now it’s back again under the guise of #maxxing. But that’s just one example. I could mention radical atheism, or gospel-centered this and that, or mindfulness. We’ve seen cultural fixations take hold and then recede, specific anxieties bubble up and dissipate. The longer view allows for a measure of perspective that I believe lends the show added depth. Longevity can also be a curse. The ebb and flow can foster a degree of detachment that masquerades as superiority. For example, it’s hard to take the latest rebranding of medieval monasticism (or justification by works) seriously when you’ve seen it happen four times under four different (best-selling) names already. Discipline becomes application becomes virtue becomes formation and so on. It’s a challenge to keep listening and paying attention, but a challenge that I’m proud of us for at least trying to live up to. Because beneath every one of the trends we’ve observed are real people with real hopes and dreams and disappointments. The second longevity-related challenge is the same one that afflicts anyone in a public role, especially those in ministry or thought life. It’s the danger of impersonating yourself. Whenever I detect in my voice any sense of “the grace guy needs to say a grace thing now” — it makes my skin crawl. Autopilot is the enemy, along with its cousin repetition. I remember a trusted listener once warning me that we were becoming a podcast about social media. Another said we were talking too much about parenting. These grooves are understandable, but to keep things fresh, especially over the long haul, you have to always be finding fresh vistas, not just in the culture but in yourself. It’s not easy. This leads me to the next observation: over ten years, it’s become notably more difficult to find suitable material for The Mockingcast . One of the things that I hold sacred about our show is its role as a refuge from culture wars. I want listeners to be confident that when they press play, we’re not going to trigger them about the same headlines that trigger them the rest of the day. We haven’t done this perfectly, I realize, but it remains a guiding principle. When the occasional how-dare-you emails come in, folks are usually surprised to hear that they come just as frequently from both sides of the aisle. If they didn’t, I’d try to course correct. Finding stuff that threads the needle of interesting and substantial but not pre-narrativized has gotten more challenging over our tenure. It’s like the ledge we walk has gotten narrower. Not nonexistent, mind you, just narrower. I’m so proud we’ve reached this milestone without, at least in my view, falling into an ideological ditch or becoming (too) predictable. I’d like to think that The Mockingcast , an
content_zh: 听众会更清楚为何《嘲笑者》在11年后(或不是)工作, 在三百集的开头, 我们包含了一些这样的故事, 我个人对播客的欣赏、我最自豪的以及挑战性。 无疑我的联合主办方还会有他们强调的其他方面。 首先,长寿。 这值得庆祝, 时间允许我们开发一些 相当无价的化学。 当我挑选文章让我们讨论时, 我知道,即使材料平平了, 我也可以依靠我们的动力来消遣。 我信任我的同座主持人, 我们一起经历了很多事情, 在网路上呆了这么久, 莎拉最近提到这个问题,谈到我们社会中食品的道德化。 大约八年前,它非常急性, 随身体接触的瞬间, 但这只是一个例子。 我可以提到激进的无神论, 或以福音为中心的这个和那个,或注意。 我们已看到文化定型逐渐稳固, 较长的视野允许某种角度的视角,我认为这可以使节目更深入。 长生亦能作一咒. ebb和流能培养出某种程度的离散,以伪装为优越. 例如,当你在四个不同的(畅销的)名称下看到中世纪修道院(或以作品为理由)的最新重塑很难认真对待。 纪律变成应用,美德变成形成等等。 继续倾听和关注是一项挑战,但我为我们至少努力做到这一点而感到自豪。 因为在我们所看到的每一个趋势之下,都是真正有希望、梦想和失望的人。 与长寿有关的第二个挑战也是影响任何公共角色,特别是部会或思想生活角色的挑战。 这是冒充自己的危险。 每当我从我的声音中察觉到任何“恩人现在需要说一件恩事”的感觉时,这让我的皮肤爬行。 自动驾驶是敌人,还有它的表弟重复. 我记得一位值得信赖的听众曾警告我,我们正成为社交媒体的播客。 另一个人说,我们谈论太多关于养育子女的问题。 这些凹槽是可以理解的, 但为了保持新鲜, 特别是从长远来看, 你必须总是找到新鲜的外观, 不仅仅是在文化中, 还是在你自己。 这不容易。 更难为《嘲笑者》找到合适的材料。 我对我们的表演持神圣态度之一 就是它作为文化战争的避难所的作用 我希望听众们有信心, 当他们按下播放时, 我们不会引发同样的头条新闻, 我们并没有完美完成这项工作, 人们通常会惊讶地听到, 如果不是,我会试着正确行事。 寻找一些能勾结到 有趣和实质性但并非预述的东西, 在我们的任期内变得更具挑战性。 我们走过的窗帘越来越窄了。 不是不存在的,你介意,只是狭小。 我感到非常骄傲的是, 我们达到了这个里程碑, 至少在我看来, 我认为,

title: Rumors of Grace
summary: What Mbird Has Been for Me   The post  Rumors of Grace  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
summary_zh: Mbird对我来说是什么恩典的帖子谣言首先出现在知更鸟上。
title_zh: 恩典的谣言
content: “You only work on Sundays, anyway.” One of the go-to jokes of a group of guys I hang out with. I laugh because, well, I just like to please people. But every time the boys say it, I think to myself, “If you only knew what being a pastor feels like sometimes.” An impromptu funeral at the clinic for veterinarians whose colleague committed suicide, scrolling to find an angry email about last week’s sermon or the changing of the carpet color in the narthex, begging financial generosity from people who pay your salary, lunch with a lonely man going through a brutal divorce, restocking the youth fridge with 7,000 Cheerwines, hearing that they’re gossiping about you again, failing yet again to prepare a sermon that marries TikTok and TED Talk, off to the shelter to serve dinner, did I even eat lunch? Did I mention that this was last Tuesday? Ministry is often pure gift. The highs are as high as they get. Pastors bear witness to the most intimate, most raw, most human, most beautiful and terrifying moments of people’s lives. We play at the level of the soul. We get paid to read and write and pray. We have a front-row seat to miracles: the bound freed, the sinner forgiven, the debts paid, the dead resurrected. It’s not lost on me that having a job rife with meaning is a privilege and honor. This is what God has chosen to make of my life, and I am truly grateful. And yet, there’s no way to get away from the fact that ministry is a burden too. Its shape is a cross. Its form is death and resurrection. People bring all their junk to church — and they should. Sunday mornings are not an assembly of the righteous, they are a sanctuary for sinners — hypocrites anonymous, I like to call it. One of the chief problems that has arisen in my ministry is that I find it so hard to be ministered to. Ministers minister, preachers preach, consolers console, but if you’re not careful, a pastor will find herself without a pastor, a preacher will find himself without a preacher. Everyone needs both. Not long ago I burnt out. Years after, I realize the burnout was not the product of overwork. The fire in my soul was extinguished because for years I had offered relief to others without finding ways to receive it myself. What becomes of a healer who forsakes his own wounds? Pay attention when your soul stops singing. And I did. I prayed for God to bring relief, somehow, someway. And then, to quote Morgan Freeman in The Shawshank Redemption , “a beautiful little bird flew into my drab little cage.” That beautiful bird was Mockingbird Ministries. And now for six years I have done what Michael Gershon calls “staking one’s life on the rumors of grace.” As the 300th of the Mockingcast draws near, I thought it fitting to say what Mbird has been for me: My theological home: Pastors in the mainline will tell you that our denominations are fracturing. It’s tempting to give in to extremes and to weaponize politics toward ecclesial ends. This has made me feel like I don’t belong anywhere politically, theologically, or pastorally. I know many fellow pastor Mbirders agree because we’ve talked about it. Pastors in the mainline who long for a ministry rooted only in the gospel are like an island of misfit toys. Mbird has become for us a gracious home and a place to be reminded again and again of the gospel of grace. My Preacher: I listen to the Mockingcast on Monday mornings. You pastors out there know Monday’s malaise. Dizzied and frenzied from all of Sunday’s work and pressured by a million regrets about the sermon or the attendance, I find sweet relief in the words of RJ, Sarah, and Dave. “That’s right,” I think. “This is what ministry about.” God may not speak to us all through an audible voice in our heads, but God does speak through the words of a sermon. On Mondays, the Mockingcast is the sermon I need to hear. And just like my own parishioners, after I hear the good news, I find myself ready for another week. My Storyteller: We are narrative beings. content_zh: “不管怎样,你只在星期天工作。” 我和一群人一起玩的笑话 我笑是因为我喜欢取悦别人 但是,每当男孩们说,我想,“如果你知道牧师有时会是什么感觉。 ” 在诊所为兽医举行即兴葬礼, 其同事自杀, 滚动寻找愤怒的电子邮件, 有关上周的布道或地毯颜色的改变, 我有提到这是上周二吗? 礼部常为纯礼. 高取相如来相. 牧师见证了人们生活中最亲密、最生动、最人性化、最美丽和最恐怖的时刻。 我们在灵魂的层面演奏。 我们得到报酬读写祈祷. 我们有一个前排的座位 奇迹: 束缚的释放者, 罪人原谅, 债务偿还, 死人复活。 工作充满意义, 这是上帝选择 使我的生活, 我真的很感激。 然而, 也没有任何办法可以摆脱这个事实, 其形状为十字. 它的形式是死亡和复活. 人们把他们所有的垃圾都带到教堂,他们应该这样做。 星期天早晨不是善人集会,而是罪人的避难所——伪君子匿名,我想称之为. 在我部里出现的主要问题之一是,我感到很难处理。 但是如果你不小心, 牧师会发现自己没有牧师, 每个人都需要两者。 不久前我烧焦了 多年之后,我意识到 燃烧不是过度劳累的结果。 我灵魂中的活火被扑灭了,因为多年来我一直向其他人提供救济,但没有找到自己接受的方法. 一个抛弃了自己伤口的医护人员会怎样? 你的灵魂停止唱歌时要注意 我这样做了。 我祈求上帝带来解脱,不知何故,某种方式。 然后,引用摩根·弗里曼(Morgan Freeman)在"肖申克救赎"(The Shawshank Resemption)中的话,“一只美丽的小鸟飞入了我的小兔子笼子。” 那美丽的鸟是鸟类部 而现在,六年来,我做了迈克尔·格申所说的“用恩典的谣言夺走自己的生命 ” 。 随着"摩克活人"第300期的到来,我认为应该说出Mbird对我的意义: 我的神学家:主线的牧师会告诉你,我们的教派正在分化. 将政治武器化, 这让我觉得自己不属于政治、神学或牧业的任何地方。 我知道许多牧师都同意, 主线的牧师渴望一个只植根于福音的部,就像一个不适应玩具的岛屿. content: Shelf Life , a new comedy from the producers of The Promised Land , follows a pastor who loses his pulpit and ends up working at a grocery store. Jim O’Heir ( Parks and Recreation ) and Zachary Levi ( Shazam! ) lead the cast, and the series is set to premiere exclusively on the Angel platform in 2027. Shelf Life is created, written and directed by Brian Cates and produced by Milk & Honey Studios. It is currently in production. The premise is a former pastor who is kicked out of the pulpit takes a job at a local grocery store, where he realizes his calling to care for others can’t be shelved while surrounded by quirky coworkers. The cast also includes Wesam Keesh, Donna Biscoe, Tommy Woodard, Jonathan Charles, Leilany Celeste, Jazelle Villanueva and Brittany Visser. Richie Johns produces. Mitch Hudson, an executive producer on the series, shared the news on Instagram. “It’s official – I’m executive producing a comedy series starring Jim O’Heir and Zachary Levi!” he wrote. He said Cates has “an incredible vision” as creator and director, that his business partner Johns is leading the producing team, and that Milk & Honey Studios is adding “another comedy show to our lineup” with Angel as a partner. “More info coming soon!” he added. Cates said he has spent 20 years working in the faith and comedy space and believes “if you make people laugh, you can make people listen.” He described the show as something families can watch together, “genuinely funny, but also honest about life, faith, failure and second chances.” The message, he said, is that “we all reach moments when we think we’ve passed our expiration date. But God isn’t finished with us yet.” O’Heir said that with Shelf Life “you come for the laughs, but you end up genuinely caring about these people.”

title: Lauren Daigle Has Released Christmas Music, So the Holiday Season Is Officially Open
summary: Every November, somewhere in a secure facility, a team of professionals gently thaws Mariah Carey so she can sing “All I Want for Christmas Is You” for the entire planet. Christian music has its own version of this tradition, and her name is Lauren Daigle. While nobody has to thaw her—she’s been out here the whole…
summary_zh: 每年11月，在一个安全设施的某个地方，一个专业团队会温柔地解冻Mariah Carey ，这样她就可以为整个星球唱“All I Want for Christmas Is You”。基督教音乐有自己的传统，她的名字叫劳伦·戴格尔（ Lauren Daigle ）。虽然没有人需要解冻她，但她一直在这里……
title_zh: Lauren Daigle发布圣诞音乐，圣诞季正式开放
content: Every November, somewhere in a secure facility, a team of professionals gently thaws Mariah Carey so she can sing “All I Want for Christmas Is You” for the entire planet. Christian music has its own version of this tradition, and her name is Lauren Daigle. While nobody has to thaw her—she’s been out here the whole time—this weekend she released two more holiday songs, this time with the Preservation Hall Jazz Band: “Sleigh Ride” and “Go Tell It on the Mountain.” If you feel like it is too early for this, please know that the paperwork has been filed. Halloween is over, the candy has been marked down to 50 percent, and the Christmas music season has legally begun. For anyone keeping score at home, this is not a new hobby for her. Daigle’s first Christmas album, Behold , came out in 2016 and climbed to No. 29 on the Billboard 200. It also started a tradition: the Behold Christmas Tour, which returns this December for its 10th annual run. That is the real Mariah comparison. A holiday arrives, and so does Lauren Daigle, with a setlist and a very good coat. The new songs are a pair of old favorites with a New Orleans accent. “Sleigh Ride” is the one that has been running through department stores since before you were born, and “Go Tell It on the Mountain” is the spiritual that has been spreading the Good News even longer than that. Preservation Hall brings the brass, the swing, and the general feeling that a very good party has broken out in a church basement. They also joined her last December for a holiday medley at the CMA Country Christmas special, so the chemistry was already on the record. There is also a business angle, if you like those. It is her first release on Capitol, Interscope and CCMG, which is a lot of letters to put on one sleigh. The songs will come out on a 7-inch vinyl on Nov. 27, the day after Thanksgiving, so you can be a person who owns a Christmas record while also being a person who is still full of pie. And if recorded music is not enough, the 10th annual Behold Christmas Tour opens Dec. 2 at the Ryman in Nashville, with stops in New Orleans and Orlando to follow. It is a beautiful room that was built for exactly this kind of evening, and it will probably smell like cinnamon candles and good intentions. The thaw has happened, the songs are out, and the season has officially been declared open. Please enjoy your holidays responsibly, which in this case means having “Sleigh Ride” on rotation.
content_zh:
每年11月,在一个安全的设施里,一群专业人士轻轻地解冻了Mariah Carey,这样她就能为整个地球唱出“我渴望的只有你”。 基督教音乐有它自己的这种传统版本,她叫劳伦·戴格.

这个周末她又发行了两首节日歌曲, 如果你觉得现在为时尚早,请知道文件已经归档。

万圣节结束,糖果被标记为50%,圣诞音乐季合法开始. 对于任何在家记分的人来说,这不是她的新爱好. Daigle的首张圣诞专辑"Beye"于2016年出道并登上"Billboard 200"的29号. 它也开创了传统: 圣诞之旅,

这是真正的Mariah比较。 节日到来 Lauren Daigle也来了 里面有固定名单 外衣很好看 新歌是一对有"新奥尔良口音"的旧相声. " 雪橇骑 " 是自你出生前就一直在百货公司跑来跑去的一款,而 " 在山上说吧 " 是传播 " 好消息 " 的时间甚至更长的精神。

保存 霍尔带来了青铜器,秋千,以及一般感觉一个非常好的聚会在教堂地下室爆发了. 他们去年12月也加入她,参加CMA乡村圣诞特辑会的节日梅德利会,因此化学已经录制了. 也有一个商业角度,如果你喜欢这些。

这是她首次在Capitol,Interscope和CCMG上发布,这是许多要放上雪橇的信. 歌曲会在感恩节后第二天的11月27日以7英寸的花花筒出道,这样你就可以成为拥有圣诞唱片的人,同时也是仍然充满了派的人. 如果录制的音乐还不够的话,第10届年度"看圣诞之旅"(Book Christmas Tour)将于12月开通.

2个在纳什维尔的雷曼车站,在新奥尔良和奥兰多停站后再跟进. 这是一个美丽的房间, 建造的正是这种夜晚, 它可能闻起来像肉桂蜡烛和良好意图。 冰冻已出,歌曲已出道,赛季正式宣布开播.

请以负责任的方式享受假期,这意味着轮回“雪橇骑”。

title: Inside Indie Tribe’s Plan to Disrupt Christian Hip-Hop
summary: On 'Who Do You Say I Am?', the Christian hip-hop collective reads the Bible's villains with empathy — and asks the church to do the same for everyone it writes off.
summary_zh: 在《你说我是谁？》（ Who Do You Say I Am? ）一文中，这位基督教嘻哈乐队以同理心解读了《圣经》中的恶棍，并要求教会为它所注销的每一个人做同样的事情。
title_zh: 探索独立部落颠覆基督教嘻哈的计划
content: Somewhere in the middle of talking about Scripture, Indie Tribe starts arguing about how to describe someone getting kicked in the groin. nobigdyl., Jon Keith, Mogli the Iceburg and DJ Mykael V are mid-sentence about the theological weight of community when the conversation collapses into a bit about their bandmate, Torey D’Shaun, who has stepped out and, per group tradition, is simply “in the bathroom.” The jokes runs a full minute before anyone remembers what they were talking about. This is more or less Indie Tribe’s operating system: theology, friendship, music and dumb jokes occupying the same room. Their new album, Who Do You Say I Am? , works the same way. They didn’t set out to make a concept record. nobigdyl., Jon Keith, Mogli and Mykael V have been a unit for years, joined more recently by D’Shaun, who folded into the group in 2024 in the middle of an album cycle. Their process has never looked like a studio session. It looks like a household. “We live together and eat together, pray together, we do Bible studies, all that kind of stuff, and we make music for a week,” Jon Keith says. They don’t start with a concept. They start with proximity, then look back at what they made and find the thread already running through it. “We kind of look at the range of the songs that we’re making,” Jon Keith says. “We’re like, ‘Okay, it kind of feels like God is moving this in a certain direction.’” Who Do You Say I Am? happened that way. Written and recorded in December 2024 and released March 27 this year, it’s the first project to feature D’Shaun from the ground up, and the group says his arrival changed the chemistry entirely. “This is really the first time to me that it feels like — I love our previous albums, but the way that this album has a heart and a story to it and a concept, it makes the other albums feel like mixtapes,” Jon Keith says. “This joint is easily the longest album we’ve done. It really feels like our first album album.” The title eventually gave them the question holding the record together: What does it actually feel like to be the person history remembers as the villain? “It’s the product of a lot of introspection that we’ve had,” Mogli says. “We’ve gone through the Bible together multiple times through different lenses, at different times in life when we’re going through different things.” The goal wasn’t to defend bad behavior. It was to stop flattening biblical figures into cautionary tales and start reading them like people, asking how it feels to be the character everyone’s quick to condemn. nobigdyl. pushes it further. The discomfort people feel toward Scripture’s messier figures, he argues, says more about a failure of imagination than a failure of faith. Take David, a man the Bible treats as a hero despite a life that would read as chaos by modern standards. “If you take David’s context and put it now, he sounds like Future,” nobigdyl. says. “How many baby moms he got? Indie Tribe wants listeners to extend the same grace to people outside the church that Christians are often quick to withhold. “We want to be disruptive to the world, but we also want to be disruptive to the church,” he says. “We want to wake them up.” He points to how easily Christians distance themselves from people whose lives look nothing like the ones they consider acceptable. “They’re still made in the image of God, and God is still able to work on these people,” he says. “The only thing that’s going to get you sent to hell is not belonging to Jesus. That’s it.” It’s a theology built for people who’ve already decided church isn’t for them, people nobigdyl. describes as not being “super theological” or part of “the Christian culture.” The album’s central question, borrowed from the moment Jesus asks his disciples who they say he is, is an invitation the group

title: This Sunday, the Global Church Will Pray for 388 Million Christians Facing High Levels of Persecution
summary: Congregations around the world will set aside Sunday, Nov. 1 for the International Day of Prayer for the Persecuted Church, and this year Open Doors, the Christian ministry that tracks persecution, is asking them to start with Syria. Its 2026 World Watch List moved Syria from 18th place to sixth, a 12-point jump in its…
summary_zh: 世界各地的会众将于11月1日星期日为受迫害教会的国际祈祷日腾出时间，今年，追踪迫害的基督教事工敞开大门，要求他们从叙利亚开始。其2026年《世界观察榜》将叙利亚从第18位提升至第6位，其…
title_zh: 本周日，全球教会将为面临严重迫害的3.88亿基督徒祈祷
content: Congregations around the world will set aside Sunday, Nov. 1 for the International Day of Prayer for the Persecuted Church, and this year Open Doors, the Christian ministry that tracks persecution, is asking them to start with Syria. Its 2026 World Watch List moved Syria from 18th place to sixth, a 12-point jump in its score and the largest in the top 10. Open Doors says Syria is now at its most dangerous for Christians since the Islamic State group occupied significant parts of the country. About 300,000 Christians live in Syria. Since the fall of the Assad government in December 2024, the country has been mostly controlled by forces led by Hay’at Tahrir al-Sham, an Islamic extremist group with roots in al-Qaeda. The group has made overtures toward moderation and held talks with representatives of Syria’s traditional Christian communities, but it is too soon to know what will come of the new leadership. Widespread instability has produced deadly clashes that have affected Druze and Alawites in particular, with Christians caught in the crossfire, and Islamic State attacks have resumed, including the deadly attack on a church in Damascus in June 2025. “The trauma of what happened hit us all hard,” said “Mourad,” who is responsible for the work of Open Doors’ local partner in Syria. “We thought getting rid of the previous regime would give us some sense of freedom, yet it seems there are still people who only believe in killing.” The interim Syrian constitution adopted in March 2025 makes Islamic law the main source of legislation, and it offers insufficient protection for religious minorities. Pressure on Christians is greatest in Damascus and Aleppo, while the northeast is generally safer. The World Watch List ranks the 50 countries where Christians face the most extreme persecution, using a points system built on data from experts on the ground in 100 countries. North Korea is first with a score of 97 out of 100, followed by Somalia, Yemen, Sudan and Eritrea. Syria is sixth with 90, ahead of Nigeria, Pakistan, Libya and Iran. Open Doors counts more than 388 million Christians worldwide facing high levels of persecution and discrimination for their faith, about one in seven, and in the top 50 countries alone, more than 315 million face very high or extreme persecution. In its 2026 report it recorded 4,849 Christians killed, 4,712 detained and 3,632 churches and Christian properties attacked. For more than 1,600 years Christians have set aside early November to remember believers who suffered for their faith. Open Doors’ free toolkit for churches and small groups includes guided prayer points, videos, sermon material and social images, and this year’s focus is the Middle East, beginning with Syria. Open Doors’ prayer points for Syria ask for three things: that believers would lean on God as their “Rock eternal” (Isaiah 26:4), that converts from Islam would find love and fellowship even when family and friends reject them, and that the victims of the Damascus church attack would feel God’s closeness.
content_zh: 世界范围内的教会将预留11月1日为受迫害教会国际祈祷日, 今年追踪迫害的基督教部也要求他们从叙利亚开始。 其2026年世界观察榜将叙利亚从第18名提升到第6名,比分跳出12分,位列前10名. 叙利亚现在对基督徒来说是最危险的, 约30万基督徒居住在叙利亚. 自2024年12月阿萨德政府倒台后,该国多由伊斯兰极端主义团体"基地"(Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham)所领导的势力所控制. 这个团体向着温和的态度,并与叙利亚传统基督教社区的代表举行了会谈,但现在还不知道新领导人会怎样。 普遍的不稳定导致了致命的冲突,尤其影响到德鲁兹人和阿拉维人,基督徒陷入了交火中,伊斯兰国又恢复了袭击,包括2025年6月大马士革一教堂被致命袭击. Mourad对叙利亚当地合作伙伴的工作负责。 “我们认为摆脱前政权会给我们一些自由感, 2025年3月通过的叙利亚临时宪法将伊斯兰法作为立法的主要来源,对宗教少数群体的保护不足. 大马士革和阿勒颇对基督徒的压力最大,而东北部一般比较安全. 世界观察列表将基督徒面临最极端迫害的50个国家排行榜,使用基于100个国家当地专家数据建立的分数系统. 朝鲜以97胜100负的分数排名第一,其次是索马里,也门,苏丹和厄立特里亚. 叙利亚以90分位列第六,领先尼日利亚,巴基斯坦,利比亚和伊朗. 开放门人数超过3.88亿,全世界因信仰而面临严重迫害和歧视的基督教徒约有七分之一,仅在前50个国家,就有3.15亿多基督教徒面临极高或极端迫害。 它在2026年的报告中记录了4 849名基督徒被杀死,4 712人被拘押,3 632所教堂和基督教财产被袭击。 1600多年以来,基督徒在11月上旬留作纪念因信仰而受苦受难的信徒. 开放的门对教堂和小团体免费的工具包包括导游的祈祷要点、录像、布道材料和社会形象,今年的重点是中东,首先是叙利亚。 开放的门对叙利亚的祈祷点要求三件事:信徒们倚靠上帝作为他们的"永生"(Isaiah 26:4),从伊斯兰教皈依的人即使家人和朋友拒绝也会找到爱和友谊,大马士革教堂袭击的受害者也会感受到上帝的亲切.
author: RELEVANT Staff

title_zh: WNBA明星索菲·坎宁安（ Sophie Cunningham ）致西奥·冯（ Theo Von ） ： “你所做的一切都不会让你与上帝的爱、恩典和宽恕分开”
content: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham told Theo Von on his podcast that nothing a person does or doesn’t do can separate them from God’s love, after Von said he wishes his connection with God were stronger. The conversation is in episode No. 692 of This Past Weekend . Von said his prayer connection with God is the part of his life he likes most, but that when he gets too busy it can feel disconnected. “I wish my connection was stronger,” he said. Cunningham answered, “Dude, I feel you,” and said she was saying it for other people listening too: “There’s nothing that you can or can’t do that’s going to separate you from God’s love and grace and forgiveness. Like that’s why Jesus came and died on the cross because he already knew everything you were going to do.” She added that what comes next is up to the person, who can “educate yourself and read the Bible,” but that “you’re already forgiven.” She also said she feels most connected when she is “prayed up,” a phrase Von said he likes and hears from a friend all the time. Earlier in the conversation, Cunningham said she relies on her faith because of what she does for a living. “You get a lot of hate, you get a lot of praise,” she said. Faith keeps her stable and “who I am,” she said, and she doesn’t care what people’s opinions are about her “because I’m not living for their praise.” Von later asked whether the media is unfair to Christians. Cunningham said that depends on perspective, but that she loves seeing more people say they are believers. “I feel like there’s a revival happening,” she said. She said it can be scary to speak up because people have had bad experiences with church, and that she likes seeing athletes with big platforms be “bold and courageous and come out about Jesus.” Von said more athletes he has gotten to know in the past four years seem to have faith, and that more of his friends are trying to learn about it too. “We want to have some more religious figures on to talk about stuff on here,” he said.

title: ‘I Need a Little Gravy on My God’: Kirk Franklin’s New Double Album Is His Answer to 33 Years of Critics
summary: Kirk Franklin’s new album I Am What I Am, his first double album, is out Oct. 30, and he says it is partly an answer to the people who have been questioning his choices for decades. At a listening party in Atlanta, he joked about the whole idea: “I need a little gravy on my…
summary_zh: 柯克·富兰克林（ Kirk Franklin ）的第一张双人专辑《我是我》（ I Am What I Am ）将于10月30日发行，他说，这在一定程度上是对几十年来一直质疑他的选择的人的回答。在亚特兰大的一个倾听派对上，他开玩笑说整个想法： “我需要一点肉汁在我的……
title_zh: “我的上帝需要一点肉汁” ：柯克·富兰克林的新双专辑是他对33年评论家的回答
content: Kirk Franklin’s new album I Am What I Am , his first double album, is out Oct. 30, and he says it is partly an answer to the people who have been questioning his choices for decades. At a listening party in Atlanta , he joked about the whole idea: “I need a little gravy on my God.” The album has 14 songs across two discs, seven studio recordings on the first and seven recorded live on the second. It is Franklin’s 14th studio album, according to the Associated Press, which reports that he is tired of defending his musical decisions. He told the AP he prayed with Chris Brown and Usher before a concert because they asked him to, a moment that drew criticism on social media. “We as believers sometimes become judge and jury,” he said. He also stands by working with GloRilla, whose music is explicit, on the single “This Time.” The song extended his record to 10 No. 1s on Billboard’s Hot Gospel Songs chart, the AP reports. “You start trying to play in other people’s sandboxes, it is going to come with scrutiny,” Franklin said. At the listening party he put it more plainly: “I’ve been trying to explain myself for the last 33 years. This felt like the right opportunity to let people know that I listen and I hear everything that is being said. I am aware. This is my humanity.” Jelly Roll opens the record on “Free Me Tonight,” a spoken-word track the AP says nods to Phil Collins’ “In the Air Tonight.” Franklin reflects on his imperfections and his public criticism on it. Franklin told the AP the song was cathartic and that he once worried it would end his career. “Gospel music is able to handle the raw, unfiltered truth about how ugly and difficult life can be,” he said. On “It Gets Better,” with Tobe Nwigwe, Franklin said at the listening party: “That song was my attempt to find a space to talk about mental health. I’ve had my own journey with anxiety and depression.” He also said, “Living up to the religious standards can create psychological trauma,” and recalled that in his childhood church, young women could be publicly shamed for getting pregnant while the men involved faced no comparable accountability. “Can you imagine the trauma?” he asked. Davido is on “Hope In You,” and Karen Clark Sheard of the Clark Sisters is on the live “Thank You for Everything.” The AP singles out the live “Welcome In,” in which Franklin describes feeling forgotten by God at times while expressing gratitude for God’s steadfast presence. He said the sound of Black church music changed while he was making the album. “The Black church culture changed,” he said. “The church got rid of their choirs and the music was in a space that was not my strength.” Franklin, who is 56 and a 20-time Grammy winner, has no plans to slow down. “The hole that I came from was so deep that whenever I’m around light, I never get tired of feeling the sunlight,” he told the AP.
content_zh: 柯克·富兰克林的新专辑"I Am What I Am",他的第一张双人专辑"October"已经出道了"10月30日",他表示这部分是对数十年来一直质疑自己选择的人的回答. 在亚特兰大的一个倾听会中,他开玩笑地说,“我需要一点肉汁来奉上我的上帝。” 该专辑有14首歌曲横跨了两盘,有7首录音室在第一盘上录制,有7首录音室在第二盘上录制. 据美联社报道, 这是富兰克林的第14张录音室专辑, 他告诉AP在演唱会前与克莉丝·布朗和乌舍尔一起祷告,因为他们要求他这样做,这一刻引起了社交媒体的批评. 他说,“我们作为信徒有时成为法官和陪审团。” 他也与音乐清晰的GloRilla合作, 歌曲将他的记录扩展至"Billboard"热福音歌曲图表"AP报告"上"10 No. 富兰克林说:“你开始尝试在别人的沙盒里玩, 在监听会上,他更明确地说:“过去33年来,我一直在试图解释自己。 这感觉像是让大家知道 我听了,我听到所说的话。 我意识到了 这是我的人性。” Jelly Roll在“今晚自由我 ” ( Free Me Tonight)上打开了记录, 富兰克林反思了自己的不完善和公众对它的批评. 富兰克林告诉AP这首歌是催泪瓦斯的,他一度担心这会结束他的职业生涯. 他说,“福音音乐能够处理关于多么丑陋和艰难生活的原始而未经过滤的真相”。 富兰克林在Tobe Nwigwe的“Gets Better”,在听歌会上说:“这首歌是我试图寻找一个空间来谈论心理健康的。 我以焦虑和忧郁经历自己的旅程。 他还说, " 达到宗教标准会造成心理创伤 " ,并回顾说,在他童年的教堂里,年轻妇女可能因怀孕而被公开羞辱,而有关男子则没有相应的责任。 他问道,“你能想象创伤吗?” 达维多在“希望你 ” , 克拉克姐妹会的凯伦·克拉克·谢德在现场直播“谢谢你的一切 ” 。 美联社特别列出现场直播的“欢迎入场 ” , 富兰克林描述有时被上帝遗忘的感觉, 他说,黑教堂音乐的声音在他制作专辑时改变了. 他说,“黑人教会文化发生了变化”。 “教会摆脱了他们的合唱团, 富兰克林,56岁,是20次格莱美奖得主,没有计划减速. “我所从来的那个洞很深,

title: Packers’ Josh Jacobs Says His Touchdown Celebration Is an Ode to the Gospel Song “Break Every Chain,” Not His Recent Arrest
summary: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs says the celebration that set off social media after his latest touchdown was a tribute to a gospel song, not a joke about his recent arrest. In the second quarter of the Packers’ 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers, Jacobs scored on a 1-yard run and briefly put…
summary_zh: 绿湾包装工队跑卫乔什·雅各布斯（ Josh Jacobs ）表示，在他最近一次触地得分后引发社交媒体的庆祝活动是对福音歌曲的致敬，而不是关于他最近被捕的笑话。在包装工队以27-19战胜卡罗莱纳黑豹队的第二节中，雅各布斯在1码的跑步中得分，并简要介绍了......
title_zh: Packers的Josh Jacobs说，他的达阵庆祝活动是对福音歌曲“打破每一条链条”的颂歌，而不是他最近的逮捕
content: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs says the celebration that set off social media after his latest touchdown was a tribute to a gospel song, not a joke about his recent arrest. In the second quarter of the Packers’ 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers, Jacobs scored on a 1-yard run and briefly put his hands behind his back while teammates congratulated him. Some viewers watching on television thought he was pretending to be handcuffed. Jacobs said he was modeling the moment after a gospel song called “Break Every Chain.” “The guys did it with me,” he said. “I didn’t think it was going to be a thing that can be perceived a certain type of way. But it’s 2026, and it is what it is.” It was Jacobs’ second game of the season. He had spent time on the NFL’s commissioner’s exempt list after charges were filed against him in August over a May altercation with his then-girlfriend, who said he threw her to the ground. Last month he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property. He was taken off the list last week and returned to the field, though the league’s investigation is still ongoing. Jacobs said he talked with receiver Savion Williams and other teammates before his season debut, and they planned two celebrations. After his first touchdown of the season, in a 20-17 loss at Detroit, he went to his knees and raised his arms to thank God. The “Break Every Chain” moment was meant for the next one. He also said the broadcast cut away early. “It was more to it than that,” Jacobs said. “They stopped showing the celebration after that.” The NFL’s investigation of Jacobs remains open.
content_zh: Green Bay Packers跑回Josh Jacobs说, 上次触地得分后引发社交媒体的庆典, 在打包员27-19战胜卡罗来纳黑豹队的第二季中,雅各布斯在一码跑道上打入了分数,并短暂地将手放在了背后而队友们向他表示祝贺. 一些在电视上观看的观众认为他假装被铐了. Jacobs说,他正在创作一首名为“打破每一条链子”的福音歌后的瞬间。 他说,“这些家伙是和我一起干的。” “我不认为这会是一种可以被看成是某种方式的东西。 但这是2026年, 这是雅各布斯在该赛季的第二场比赛. 他在8月因5月与当时的女友发生争吵而对他提出指控后,在NFL的免责名单上呆了一段时间,后者说他把她扔倒在地上。 上个月,他没有就殴打和财产损失的轻罪指控提出抗辩。 他上周从名单中除名,回到了球场,尽管联赛的调查仍在进行中. 雅各布斯说他在赛季出道前与接球员萨维翁·威廉斯等队友交谈,两人计划了两次庆祝活动. 在他第一次触地得分后,在底特律的一场20-17失利中,他跪倒并举起手臂感谢上帝. “打破每一条链子”的时刻是下一个时刻。 他还说广播提前中断. Jacobs说,“事情不是那样的。” “此后,他们不再展示庆祝活动。” NFL对Jacobs的调查仍未结束.

title: Pew: Americans Ages 23 to 26 Are Among the Least Religious Adults in the Country, While 18-to-22-Year-Olds Attend Church at Higher Rates Than Anyone
summary: If you’re 25, the Gen Z church revival you keep hearing about may not describe you. Pew Research Center’s newest report on American religion finds that adults ages 23 to 26 are actually the least religious age group in the country on the core measures it tracks, including how often they pray, how much religion…
summary_zh: 如果你25岁，你一直听到的Z世代教会复兴可能无法形容你。皮尤研究中心（ Pew Research Center ）关于美国宗教的最新报告发现， 23至26岁的成年人实际上是该国宗教信仰最少的年龄组，其追踪的核心指标包括他们祈祷的频率、宗教信仰……
title_zh: 皮尤： 23至26岁的美国人是该国宗教信仰最少的成年人，而18至22岁的人参加教会的比率高于任何人
content: If you’re 25, the Gen Z church revival you keep hearing about may not describe you. Pew Research Center’s newest report on American religion finds that adults ages 23 to 26 are actually the least religious age group in the country on the core measures it tracks, including how often they pray, how much religion matters to them and whether they identify with a religion. But the group just below them looks very different. Among adults 18 to 22, 41% say they attend a church, synagogue, mosque or other house of worship at least once or twice a month. That is higher than the 33% for the U.S. public as a whole, and higher than adults born in the 1990s, 1980s, 1970s and 1960s. Among adults 23 to 26, the number is 27%, one of the lowest of any age group. Pew calls the overall picture “complicated,” and the report is careful about what the younger figure can carry. Outside of attendance, the youngest adults are less distinctive. They pray and identify with a religion at lower rates than many older groups. They are no more religious than people that age were in 2014, and by Pew’s measures of prayer, religion’s importance and religious identification, both young groups are significantly less religious than their counterparts in 2007. That said, Pew’s sample is small. The 18-to-22 findings rest on 443 respondents from Pew’s 2025 and 2026 surveys, with a margin of error of plus or minus 5.7 percentage points. Applied to the 41% figure, that is a range of roughly 35% to 47%. Split the group by gender or party and the margins widen further. Pew also notes that this has happened before. In its 2014 Religious Landscape Study, 18-to-22-year-olds attended services at a rate 6 points higher than 23-to-26-year-olds. What is new is that the 2025 and 2026 surveys are the first in which the youngest group is significantly more religious than the next group up on all four of Pew’s core indicators. When the youngest adults have looked more religious in the past, Pew says, the effect has tended to fade with time. It adds that the bump may partly reflect a rebound from the pandemic, and that scholars of religion tend to study change over decades. Some of the details cut against the usual storyline about who is showing up. Young men now attend more often than young women, which Pew says it has not seen before, but 35% of the youngest women attend at least monthly, about the same as women born from the 1950s through the 1980s. Among the youngest Republicans, 55% attend monthly. The youngest Democrats also attend at relatively high rates compared with other Democrats, so Pew says it cannot call this an exclusively Republican phenomenon. Across all ages, Pew finds religion holding steady. The shares who identify with a religion, pray daily, call religion very important and attend monthly have been flat since 2020, and 34% of U.S. adults said in a June survey that they had attended services in person in the previous month, the highest since Pew began asking in 2020. Pew says it has no way of knowing whether the youngest adults will follow the old pattern or break it, and describes the open question as “a turning point or a blip.” If it is a revival, it belongs so far to the very youngest adults in the survey.
content_zh: 若你25岁, 皮尤研究中心关于美国宗教的最新报告发现,23-26岁的成年人实际上是该国在追踪的核心衡量标准上最不信奉宗教的年龄组,包括他们的祈祷次数、宗教对他们的重要性以及他们是否认同某一宗教。 但是他们下面的人群看起来很不一样。 在18至22岁的成年人中,41%的人说,他们每月至少去一次或两次教堂、犹太会堂、清真寺或其他礼拜场所。 这比整个美国公众的33%高,也比1990年代,1980年代,1970年代和1960年代出生的成年人高. 在23至26岁的成年人中,这一数字为27%,是任何年龄组中最低的。 皮尤称总体情况“复杂”,报告对年轻人物能够携带什么十分谨慎。 除了出勤外,最年轻的成年人也不太特别. 他们祈祷和认同宗教的比例低于许多老年群体。 他们的宗教程度不比2014年那个年龄的人多,根据皮尤的祈祷、宗教的重要性和宗教认同措施,2007年,这两个青年群体的宗教程度明显低于同龄人。 皮尤的样本很小。 18至22分的调查结果取自皮尤2025年和2026年调查的443个答卷人,误差幅度为上下5.7个百分点。 适用于41%的数字,约为35%至47%。 按性别或政党划分,差额进一步扩大。 Pew也指出,这以前发生过。 在其2014年的"宗教景观研究"中,18至22岁的青少年参加服务,比23至26岁的青少年高6分. 新情况是,2025年和2026年的调查是第一次最年轻的群体比皮尤所有四个核心指标的下一批群体宗教程度高得多。 当最年轻的成年人在过去看起来更加宗教化时,皮尤说,这种效果往往随着时间逐渐消退. 它还说,这一起伏可能部分反映了该流行病的反弹,宗教学者往往研究几十年来的变化。 一些细节与通常的故事情节相对应, 青年男子现在比青年妇女更经常参加,皮尤说以前从未见过这种活动,但最小的妇女中35%至少每月参加,大约与1950年代至1980年代出生的妇女相同。 在最年轻的共和党人中,有55%每月参加. 与其他民主党人相比,最年轻的民主党人也以相对较高的比率参加,因此皮尤称这不能称之为纯粹的共和党现象. 在所有年龄,皮尤发现宗教是稳定的。 认同某种宗教,每日祷告,呼唤宗教非常重要并每月出席的股份自2020年以来一直是平平的,34%的美国成年人在6月的调查中表示,他们上个月曾亲自参加过各种服务,是皮尤自2020年开始询问以来最高的. Pew说,它无法知道最年轻的成年人是否会遵循旧模式或打破旧模式,并形容这个尚未解决的问题是“一个转折点或一滴一滴地”。 如果是复兴,它迄今为止属于调查中最年轻的成年人。

title: The Most-Searched Thing in the Bible App This Year Was Psalm 91. ‘Anxiety,’ ‘Hope’ and ‘Healing’ Weren’t Far Behind.
summary: The search bar in a Bible app works like any other, which means it shows what people are worried about before they’ve said it out loud to anyone. YouVersion says “Psalm 91” was the single most-searched term in the app this year. In its newest release, the company also says “anxiety,” “hope” and “healing” were…
summary_zh: 圣经应用程序中的搜索栏与其他应用程序一样，这意味着它可以显示人们在向任何人大声说出来之前所担心的事情。YouVersion表示， “Psalm 91”是今年该应用程序中搜索量最大的术语。在其最新版本中，该公司还表示“焦虑”、“希望”和“治愈”是……
title_zh: 今年圣经应用程序中搜索次数最多的是诗篇91篇。“焦虑”、“希望”和“治愈”并不落后。
content: The search bar in a Bible app works like any other, which means it shows what people are worried about before they’ve said it out loud to anyone. YouVersion says “Psalm 91” was the single most-searched term in the app this year. In its newest release , the company also says “anxiety,” “hope” and “healing” were among the year’s most searched terms. YouVersion describes Psalm 91 as a psalm that encourages readers to turn to God for refuge and comfort in difficult times. The psalm runs 16 verses. Together, YouVersion says, the searches offer a glimpse into the personal questions and hopes people are bringing to Scripture. Daily use of the Bible App grew by more than 13% compared with 2025, reaching 18.5 million people a day. It also says it added more than 160 million new installs across its family of apps in 2026, after celebrating one billion installs last November. Daily engagement grew faster than installs, which the company reads as a sign that people are returning to the app and not only downloading it. Some of the highest engagement is outside the U.S. YouVersion says it sees some of the highest levels of Bible App engagement in Sub-Saharan Africa, the Middle East and Southeast Asia, and it is building regional hubs in places including the United Kingdom, Brazil, Kenya and Mexico. Its apps offer 3,800 versions of the Bible in 2,400 languages, and it works with a network of more than 45,000 churches and partners. Bobby Gruenewald, YouVersion’s founder and CEO, said in the release that the company has been encouraged by “how many people are turning to Scripture for answers to their questions.”
content_zh: 说明人们在对任何人大声说出来之前, YouVersion说“Psalm 91”是今年应用软件中最被搜索的词。 该公司在最新版中也说“焦虑”、“希望”和“康复”是今年最被搜索的术语之一。 YouVersion将"诗经"91描述为"鼓励读者在困难时期向上帝求助以寻求庇护和安慰"的"诗经". 菩萨行出十六句. YouVersion指出, 搜索可以窥见个人问题, 希望人们能带来圣经。 与2025年相比,"圣经App"的日常使用量增长了13%多,每天达到1850万人. 去年11月庆祝了十亿个安装, 日常参与比安装增长得快,公司读到这表示人们正在回归应用,而不仅仅是下载. 在美国YouVersion以外, 一些最高的接触者表示, 在撒哈拉以南非洲、中东和东南亚, 其应用软件以2400种语言提供3800个版本的"圣经",它与超过45000个教堂和合作伙伴的网络合作. YouVersion的创始人兼首席执行官Bobby Gruenewald在发布会中说,“有多少人转向圣经来回答他们的问题,这鼓励了公司。
