title: A Broken System Protects Traffickers, Not Girls
summary: I’m often asked about the night I spent in a Southeast Asian jail alongside three young girls who had been exploited by sex traffickers. But the primary question isn’t about why I was in jail. Rather, why were those three girls in jail to begin with? Why them, and not the traffickers who had taken…
summary_zh: 我经常被问及与三名被性贩运者剥削的年轻女孩一起在东南亚监狱度过的夜晚。但主要的问题不是我为什么入狱。相反，为什么这三个女孩一开始就被关在监狱里？为什么是他们，而不是抓走……的人贩子……
title_zh: 破碎的系统保护贩运者，而不是女孩
content: I’m often asked about the night I spent in a Southeast Asian jail alongside three young girls who had been exploited by sex traffickers. But the primary question isn’t about why I was in jail. Rather, why were those three girls in jail to begin with? Why them, and not the traffickers who had taken them from their families and sold them repeatedly for sex, turning their lives into a brutal nightmare? Why not the woman who had put tape over the mouth of the young girl so that the man who was raping her would not be disturbed by her screams. The system failed them. The brothel keeper was tipped off about their rescue operation, allowed to hide her crime, and told to dump the girls at a nearby bus stop. The police who should have rescued them instead arrested them on immigration charges. The trafficker walked free, while the girls were treated as criminals. As I sat with them that night, I longed for those girls to have never been taken to jail, much less a brothel. I wanted them to have always been at home with their families, going to school, and playing with their friends. I wanted them to have never been harmed in the first place. But the reality is, like millions of women and girls in our world today, they suffered the consequences of a broken justice system. And so, the reason I stayed with the girls is simply that the alternative was just too horrible. I preferred to be arrested myself rather than leave them vulnerable to further assault. But there’s an important detail to clarify: in the end, I did not need to stay the full night. Once it was clear I was not going away, the jailer himself took on the responsibility of assuring their safety. In a broken system, when even just one agent uses their authority for good, the door to justice begins to open. Shifting Power The very next day, my colleagues at International Justice Mission (IJM) and I were able to bring the girls to safety and long-term holistic aftercare. I continued to visit the girls for years, witnessing their healing as they moved into new lives of freedom. But nearly 25 years after that night in jail, the fight remains the same; we must not leave until those with governing power wield their power to protect the most vulnerable. If we fail to intervene for the women and girls being brutalized by violent criminals, including intimate partners and family members, the alternative is unconscionable. But when we do show up, we get to be part of shifting the levers of power. Entire systems – even the most corrupt and unjust – begin to change for good. In the 21st century, we must reckon with the reality that millions of women and girls are still not any more safe from violence than they have been in any previous era. It is still true, as it has been for decades, that one in three women will experience physical or sexual violence in their lifetime. Today, and in fact, every day, 140 women will be killed by their partners or family members. But far too often, law enforcement and other government actors appear to be on the side of violent perpetrators and other abusers, rather than those who are suffering violence. Whether it’s taking bribes to protect traffickers, criminalizing women and children who are being exploited, or allowing them to be intimidated into not reporting the abuse, agents of the law bear tremendous responsibility and opportunity to change the systemic violence they have enabled to perpetuate. Violent crime thrives on opportunity, and the argument for countering this could not be more clear: strengthening justice systems deters violence. When laws are enforced and traffickers and other abusers are held accountable, other perpetrators of violence are discouraged from committing similar crimes. I think of this as flipping the fear equation. When violent abusers begin to fear the consequences of law, women and children begin to live free from fear. In my work with IJM, I’ve helped build a model that has proved this theory of change. We’ve meticulously m
content_zh: 我经常被问及在东南亚监狱度过的夜晚, 但首要问题并不在于我为何入狱。 相反,为什么这三个女孩要入狱? 为什么是他们,而不是那些从家人那里夺走他们,并反复出卖他们的性生活,把他们的生活变成残酷的噩梦的人? 为什么不让那个把录音带放入年轻女孩口中的女人 让强奸她的男人不会被她尖叫所打扰 系统失败了 妓院老板被告知他们的营救行动,允许她隐瞒罪行,并说要把女孩们扔到附近的一个公交站。 本应救出他们的警察却以移民指控逮捕了他们。 贩卖者走得自由,而女孩则被当作罪犯对待. 当晚我和她们坐在一起时,我渴望那些女孩从来没有被关进监狱,更不用说妓院了。 我希望他们总是和家人一起在家,上学,和朋友一起玩. 我希望他们从一开始就没有受到伤害。 但是,现实是,同我们当今世界上数百万妇女和女童一样,她们遭受了司法制度被打破所造成的后果。 所以,我和女孩们在一起的原因 就是另一种选择太可怕了。 我宁愿自己被捕,而不是让他们受到进一步的攻击。 但有一个重要的细节需要澄清:最后,我不需要过夜。 一旦我明白我不会离开, 看守自己承担了保证他们安全的责任。 在一个破碎的体系中,即使只有一个特工善用权威,正义之门也开始打开. 正在移动电源 第二天,我在国际司法特派团(正义团)的同事和我得以使这些女孩安全地得到长期的全面照顾。 多年来,我继续探访这些女孩,目睹她们进入自由新生活时愈合。 但是,在狱中当晚近25年之后,这场战斗依然如故;我们决不能离开,直到那些拥有统治权的人行使权力保护最脆弱群体。 如果我们不能干预暴力罪犯,包括亲密伴侣和家庭成员对妇女和女孩的残暴行为,那么,另一种选择是不合理的。 但是,当我们出现时, 我们就会成为改变权力杠杆的一部分。 整个系统 — — 甚至最腐败和最不公正的系统 — — 开始永远改变。 在21世纪,我们必须考虑这样一个现实:数百万妇女和女童仍然比以往任何时代都更无法免遭暴力。 几十年来,每3个妇女中就有1个在一生中遭受身体或性暴力。 今天,事实上,每天都有140名妇女被其伴侣或家庭成员杀害。 但是,执法部门和其他政府行为者似乎往往站在暴力肇事者和其他施虐者一边,而不是那些遭受暴力的人一边。 无论是收受贿赂来保护被剥削的妇女和儿童,还是让他们受到恐吓来不报告虐待,法律工作者都肩负着巨大的责任和机会来改变他们得以延续的系统性暴力。 暴力犯罪依靠机会而兴起,打击暴力的论据再清楚不过了:加强司法系统可以阻止暴力。 当法律得到实施,贩运者和其他施虐者被追究责任时,其他暴力行为的犯罪人就被劝阻不犯下类似的罪行。 我认为这是在改变恐惧的等式。 当暴力虐待者开始害怕法律的后果时,妇女和儿童开始免于恐惧地生活。 在与IJM的合作中, 我帮助建立了一个模型, 我们非常谨慎

title: Researchers Say Radar Shows Chambers and Corridors Inside the Boat-Shaped Formation in Turkey That Some Believe Is Noah’s Ark
summary: A radar scientist working at a boat-shaped formation in eastern Turkey says his scans show organized patterns, chambers and corridors inside it, and that those features are not natural rock. The scientist, Khosrow Bakhtar, is a veteran U.S. defense scientist and the inventor of the BakhtarRadar system used at the site, according to the project’s…
summary_zh: 一名在土耳其东部船形编队工作的雷达科学家说，他的扫描显示里面有组织的图案、腔室和走廊，这些特征不是天然岩石。根据该项目的说法，科学家Khosrow Bakhtar是一位资深的美国国防科学家，也是现场使用的BakhtarRadar系统的发明者。
title_zh: 研究人员说，雷达显示土耳其船形编队内的房间和走廊，有些人认为是诺亚方舟
content: A radar scientist working at a boat-shaped formation in eastern Turkey says his scans show organized patterns, chambers and corridors inside it, and that those features are not natural rock. The scientist, Khosrow Bakhtar, is a veteran U.S. defense scientist and the inventor of the BakhtarRadar system used at the site, according to the project’s release. He reported the preliminary results from inside the Durupınar Formation, a roughly 515-foot structure near Mount Ararat that Ark hunters have studied since 1959. Bakhtar said the radar was set to mask natural geological signals, so a purely natural anomaly would not have shown up in the processed images. He called it “the most significant finding of 45 years of my career.” Prof. Cenker Atila of Sivas Cumhuriyet University, who oversees the permitted project, reviewed and confirmed the preliminary results, the release says. He added that the radar also shows a structure with three levels, which he compared to the three levels of the Ark in “our Holy Books.” The findings were presented at a symposium in Turkey, and the group, Noah’s Ark Scans, announced them this week. The group also reports recovering charred wood from almost 30 feet down inside the formation, and says the condition of the wood is what makes it interesting. Genesis describes the Ark coated in pitch, which burns easily, so the release suggests someone may have tried to set the Ark on fire long ago. Charring slows decomposition in soil, often to well under 1% a year, so “what was meant to destroy it may have actually preserved it,” the release says. The group also says the wood is not recent surface debris and was not carried in by mudflow, because it came from deep within the formation. The release allows other explanations for the charring, including lightning or volcanic activity. Founder Andrew Jones said the wood could be the charred remains of the Ark or the remains of a campfire a shepherd lit while using it for shelter centuries ago. The wood has been sent for carbon-14 dating and species identification, and the team says no firm conclusions should be drawn until the results are published. Dating would give the wood’s age and identification would show what kind of tree it came from, but neither result would by itself show that it came from a boat. Everything here comes from the group itself. The radar results are preliminary, the masking is the team’s own processing, and none of it has been through independent peer review. A 1996 study by geologist Lorence Collins and Ark hunter David Fasold concluded that Durupınar is a natural rock formation. Noah’s Ark Scans also sells guided tours and merchandise, is running a GiveSendGo fundraiser for more core drilling, and its release asks for donations and points readers to a gold dealer and a preparedness retailer. More radar processing and reporting is expected in the coming months, and Jones has said initial lab results are expected over the winter. Atila has said photos of the wood will be released in the near future.
content_zh: 一位在土耳其东部的船形编队工作的雷达科学家说,他的扫描显示它内部有条理的图案,室室和走廊,这些特征不是天然岩石. 科学家Khosrow Bakhtar是一位美国资深国防科学家, 他报告了Durupınar Formation公司内部的初步结果,这是Ararat山附近一个约515英尺高的结构,由Ark猎人自1959年以来研究。 巴赫塔尔说,雷达是用来遮掩自然地质信号的,因此在经过处理的图像中不会出现纯粹的自然异常. 他称之为“我45年职业生涯中最重要的发现”。 师曰. Sivas Cumhuriyet大学的Cenker Atila监督了许可的项目,审查并确认了初步结果。 他补充说,雷达还显示一个具有三个级别的结构,他与方舟子在“我们的圣书”中的三个级别相比。 调查结论在土耳其的一次研讨会上发表, 剧组还报告从形成地近30英尺下方取出烧焦的木头,并说木头的状况使得它很有趣. "创世记"描述了被涂入花筒的"方舟",这很容易被烧伤,因此发行表明有人可能早就想放出"方舟"了. 碳化物在土壤中的分解速度慢了,每年的分解率往往不到1%,因此“破坏它的意图可能是实际保存下来的”。 剧组还称该木不是近代地表出土出土的地表出土出土后被泥流所承载,因为它出土出土了形成地深. 释放后可以对焦炭进行其他解释,包括闪电或火山活性. 创始人安德鲁·琼斯(Andrew Jones)说,木头可能是"方舟"被烧焦的遗骨,也可能是数百年前在使用时被牧羊人点燃了的营火的遗骨. 该木被送去进行碳-14约会和物种鉴定,队伍表示在结果公布之前不应得出确定的结论. 约会可以说明木材的年代, 这里的一切来自团体本身. 雷达结果初步,口罩是团队自己的处理方式,没有经过独立的同行评审. 1996年由地质学家洛伦斯·柯林斯和方克猎人大卫·法拉尔德进行的一项研究得出结论,杜鲁普纳尔是天然岩层. 诺亚方舟扫描公司也出售导游和商品, 预计未来几个月会有更多的雷达处理和报告,琼斯表示预计冬季会有初步的实验室结果. Atila表示, 木头的照片将在不久的将来发布。

title: Gallup: Americans Under 30 Rate Their Lives 20 Points Lower Than They Did in 2010
summary: A 25-year-old in 2026 is starting adult life in worse shape than a 25-year-old in 2010, at least by their own account. Gallup’s newest wellbeing report finds that 44% of U.S. adults ages 18 to 29 are “thriving” so far this year, down from a high of 64% in 2010. Gallup counts someone as thriving…
summary_zh: 至少根据他们自己的说法， 2026年25岁的人开始的成年生活比2010年25岁的人更糟糕。盖洛普最新的幸福感报告发现，今年到目前为止， 18至29岁的美国成年人中有44% “茁壮成长” ，低于2010年的64%。盖洛普认为某人正在茁壮成长……
title_zh: 盖洛普： 30岁以下美国人的生活水平比2010年低20个百分点
content: A 25-year-old in 2026 is starting adult life in worse shape than a 25-year-old in 2010, at least by their own account. Gallup’s newest wellbeing report finds that 44% of U.S. adults ages 18 to 29 are “thriving” so far this year, down from a high of 64% in 2010. Gallup counts someone as thriving if they rate their current life a 7 or higher on a zero-to-10 ladder and expect to rate their life an 8 or higher five years from now. Most of the drop came recently. About two-thirds of the total decline has happened since 2019. Gallup is careful about causes, saying a set of factors “may explain” the decline among young adults. It points to a rise in depression, weaker close relationships, less daily enjoyment and less feeling active and productive each day. It also lists lower satisfaction with living standards, with leaders who create enthusiasm about the future and with progress toward personal goals. Among adults 30 to 44, it says the share currently having or being treated for depression is up 15 points since 2019, to 37%. Beyond those measures, Gallup names loneliness, which it says has been particularly acute among younger men, along with housing affordability and fear of losing jobs to AI. About half of adults 18 to 49 doubt Medicare and Social Security will be available in 10 years, far more than other age groups. Just 14% of adults 18 to 34 say they are “extremely proud” to be American, down 10 points since 2025. The numbers follow people as they age. Adults now 34 to 46 are at 46%, compared with 64% when they were the 18-to-29 group in 2010, so their ratings fell as they got older while the young adults behind them are starting from a lower place. Adults 30 to 44 are at 45%, down from a high of 62% in 2016 and 2017. Adults 45 to 64 are at 46%, which matches their low from 2008. The estimates come from three Gallup Panel surveys in February, May and August 2026 with 15,156 U.S. adults in total.
content_zh: 2026年出道的25岁少年开始的成人生活状况比2010年出道的25岁少年更糟糕,至少是靠他们自己的说法. 盖洛普最新的福利报告发现,今年到目前为止,美国44%的18至29岁的成年人在“抢走”,低于2010年的64%。 盖洛普认为,如果把目前的寿命定在7至10个梯子上,并期望从现在起将生命定在8至10个梯子上,那么,盖洛普就认为某人是繁荣的。 大部分的货最近才来 约三分之二的总下降发生在2019年以来. 盖洛普对原因很谨慎,说一系列因素“可以解释”年轻人的下降。 这表明抑郁症的上升,亲密的关系更弱,日常的享受减少,每天的活跃和生产的感觉也更差. 它还列出了对生活水平、对未来产生热情的领导人以及在实现个人目标方面取得进展的低满意度。 在30至44个成年人中,它说,目前接受或正在接受抑郁治疗的比例自2019年以来上升了15分,达到37%. 除了这些措施外,Gallup还称孤独,这在年轻男子中尤其严重,而且住房负担不起,担心会失去AI的工作。 大约一半的18至49个成年人怀疑在10年内将可获得医疗保健和社会保障,远远多于其他年龄组。 18至34岁的成年人中只有14%说,他们“非常自豪”是美国人,自2025年以来下降了10分。 数字跟随人们老去。 成人目前为34至46人,占46%,而2010年是18至29人组的64%,因此他们的收视率随着年龄的增长而下降,而背后的青壮年则从更低的地方开始。 成年人30至44人占45%,低于2016年和2017年的62%。 成年人45至64人的比例为46%,与2008年的水平相匹配。 估计数来自2026年2月,5月和8月的三起盖洛普小组调查,共计15,156名美国成年人.

title: Seven Rules for Catechizing
summary: In our interview with Dr Chad Van Dixhoorn, Behind the Scenes at the Westminster Assembly, he mentions the noted catechist Thomas Lye (1621–1684) and his seven rules for catechizing. Here, in an accessible format, is Lye’s explanation of his seven-part method. While some of the advice relates to his published version of the catechism, the seven […]   The post  Seven Rules for Catechizing  appeared first on  Banner of Truth USA .
summary_zh: 在我们对威斯敏斯特议会幕后查德·范·迪克斯霍恩博士的采访中，他提到了著名的教义问答家托马斯·莱（ 1621-1684 ）及其教义问答的七条规则。这里，以无障碍的格式，是Lye对他的七部分方法的解释。虽然一些建议与他出版的问答版本有关，但七[…]后问答的七条规则首先出现在美国真理的旗帜上。
title_zh: 问答的七条规则
content: In our interview with Dr Chad Van Dixhoorn, Behind the Scenes at the Westminster Assembly , he mentions the noted catechist 1 Thomas Lye (1621–1684) and his seven rules for catechizing. Here, in an accessible format, is Lye’s explanation of his seven-part method. While some of the advice relates to his published version of the catechism, the seven basic steps or rules may be widely applied. The reader should note that Lye was so accustomed to catechising people by means of a ‘question and answer’ method, that even his instructions concerning catechesis are communicated in sequential questions and answers! Introducing the Rules for Catechizing Q. 1. Are there any rules proposed to be observed in catechizing? A. Yes. Q. 2. Is there a title to those rules? A. Yes. Q. 3. Which is the title to those rules? A. A form of examination according to the rules or method proposed to be observed in catechizing. Q. 4. Is catechizing an ordinance? A. Yes. Q. 5. Whose ordinance? Is it God’s? A. Yes. Q. 6. How do you prove it? A. I prove it out of Proverbs 22:6: ‘Train up (or catechize) a child in the way that he [or she] should go, and when they are old they will not [or at least they should not] depart from it.’ Q. 7. How many rules are there to be observed in catechizing? A. Seven. Rule 1: Read and Return Q. 8. Which is the first rule to be observed in catechizing? A. Let the question be barely propounded, and the answer returned. Rule 2: Yes or No? Q. 9. What is the second rule? A. Try the child’s understanding, whether he (she) doth discern truth from falsehood. Q. 10. How shall the child manifest that? A. Only by saying Yes or No, to such short questions as may be raised from the preceding answer. Q. 11. Where are they set down? A. Next to the answers. Q. 12. Why is this necessary? A. Because to repeat words, and not to understand the truths contained in them, is but to act the parrot, and profits very little. Q. 13. But how must the child be made to say Yes or No? A. Without book only. Q. 14. Why then do we use to read them? 2 A. For two reasons. 1. Because we should learn to read them exactly. 2. Because the oftener we do read them, and the better we do consider them, the more capable we shall be to answer them truly without book, if we should (at any time) be so examined. Rule 3: Check the Words Q. 15. What is the third rule? A. Try the child’s ability to express his (or her) knowledge of the meaning of every hard and difficult word or phrase in the preceding answer. Q. 16. What reason is there for this? A. Because we cannot rightly apprehend truths, unless we clearly understand the meaning of those words in which truths are wrapped up. Q. 17. What may be of special use for an help to the child herein? A. The Alphabetical Table at the end of this catechism Q. 18. How may I find any difficult word in the Table? A. Mark with what letter it begins, and then look for it under the same letter in the Table. Q. 19. How may I know the difficult words in the answers? A. Note, that every difficult word explained in the Table is printed with a black English character in every answer. Rule 4: Prove the Point(s) Q. 20. What is the fourth rule? A. Draw the whole answer into several doctrinal propositions (if it contains more than one) and bid the child prove each or either of them by Scripture. Q. 21. Why should the answer be drawn into several doctrinal propositions? A. For two reasons: 1. Because there are several distinct truths contained in several answers of the catechism. 2. Because the more distinctly and particularly any truth is proposed, the more capable the child’s understanding is to apprehend it. Q. 22. Why must the child prove each of these doctrinal propositions by Scripture? A. Because the Holy Scriptures are the only foundation and proof of infallible and saving truth. Rule 5: Observe the Scriptures Q. 23. What is the fifth rule? A. Take the several Scriptures annexed to the answer, and in order propose them distinctly to the child:
content_zh: 他提到著名天主教徒托马斯·莱(1621年-1684年), 以方便的方式, 虽然有部分建议与他所出版的"阴道"版本有关,但七个基本步骤或规则可能被广泛应用. 读者应该注意到,Lye很习惯用 " 问答 " 的方法对人进行分类,甚至连他关于天主教的指示都用顺序问答来传达! 1. 是否提议在授衔中遵守任何规则? A. Yes. Q. 2. 这些规则是否有标题? 问题3. 这些规则的标题是什么? A. 按照拟在编目中遵守的规则或方法进行的检查。 问题4. 对法令进行授衔吗? 问题5. 谁的政令? 是上帝的吗? A. Yes. Q. 6. 你怎么证明? A. 我从 " Proverbs " 22:6中证明: " 训练(或授精)一个儿童,以便他(或她)去,当他们老了,他们不会[或至少他们不应该]离开。 " 问题7. 分类时要遵守多少规则? A.七. 第1条:阅读和返回问题8. 哪些是第一条在编目中遵守的规则? A. 让问题几乎不提,答案就回来了。 规则2:是还是否? A. 试看孩子的理智,无论他从谎言中辨别真理。 问题10. 孩子怎么表现? A. 只有回答是或否,才能回答上文答复中可能提出的简短问题。 问题11. 他们在哪里? A. 答案旁边。 问题12. 为什么有必要? A. 重复这些话,而不是理解其中包含的真理,只是做鹦鹉,利润很少。 问题13. 但如何让孩子说"是"或"否"?. A. 没有书。 问题14. 为什么我们用它来读? 2 A. 原因有两个。 1. 因为我们应当学习准确阅读。 2. 因为我们越经常地阅读,而且我们越看好,如果我们(在任何时候)接受这样的审查,我们就越有能力在没有书的情况下真正回答这些问题。 第3条:检查"字"Q. 第三个规则是什么? A. 尝试儿童表达(或她)对前一个答案中每个困难和困难的词或短语含义的了解的能力。 问题16. 这有什么原因? A. 因为我们不能正确地抓住真理,除非我们清楚地理解那些掩盖真理的文字的含义。 问题17. 向儿童提供帮助有何特别用? A. 本目录末尾的字母表 Q 18. 我怎么才能在桌子上找到任何困难的词? A. 标出它开始的字母,然后在表格的同名字母下查找. 问题19. 我怎么会知道答案中的困难? A. 注意,表格中解释的每个困难字,每个答案中都用黑色的英文字符打印出. 第4条:证明问题20。 第四个规则是什么? A. 将整个答案归纳为几个理论性建议(如果包含一个以上),并让儿童通过《圣经》证明每个或其中之一。 问题21. 答案为何应纳入若干理论性建议? A. 有两个原因: 1. 因为阴道的几个答案中包含有几种不同的真理. 2. 由于所提出的真相越明显,尤其是任何真相,儿童越能理解,就越能抓住真相。 问题22. 为什么孩子必须用"圣经"来证明这些理论命题? A. 因为"圣经"是不可逆和拯救真理的唯一基础和证明. 第5条:遵守"圣经"问题23. 第五个规矩是什么? A. 将答复所附的几本经文取而代之,以便向儿童提出:

summary_zh: 下周标志着Banner-Westminster周三推出了新的视频和音频资源。每周，我们的传播经理约书亚·凯拉德（ Joshua Kellard ）将与一位特邀嘉宾一起，就《威斯敏斯特问答》（ Westminster Shorter Catechism ）中的问题和答案进行深入对话。在这里，约书亚回答了一些关于哪些观众和听众的问题[…]这篇文章“我能从威斯敏斯特星期三期待什么？”首次出现在美国真理旗帜上。
title_zh: 我对威斯敏斯特周三有什么期待？
content: Next week marks the launch of a new video and audio resource from the Banner— Westminster Wednesdays . Each week our Communications Manager, Joshua Kellard, will be joined by a special guest for an in-depth conversation on the questions and answers contained in the Westminster Shorter Catechism. Here Joshua answers some questions about what viewers and listeners can expect from the series: Are these podcasts just for Presbyterians, or for a wider audience who may not be as familiar with the Shorter Catechism? These podcasts most certainly are for Presbyterians, but not exclusively so! The Westminster Shorter Catechism is an accessible and crisp statement of the Christian faith as it was recovered and clarified at and shortly after the Reformation. Therefore, I would venture to say that any true believer in the Lord Jesus who takes up the Shorter Catechism will find it to be a document that is rich, biblically rooted, encouraging, and edifying. We hope that these podcast episodes are all these things, too. And, I might add, not all our guests are Presbyterians! The point is to use the Shorter Catechism to help us understand and apply Scripture’s teaching What does each episode include? How long will each episode last? Each episode of Westminster Wednesdays begins with a reading of the question and answer for that week (sometimes there are two or even three, depending on the topic). Then we have an in-depth conversation on the biblical teaching covered by the question and answer with a special guest—usually a local church pastor, but we have a scattering of seminary teachers represented as well. Above: Some of the Westminster Wednesdays guests. The point is to use the Shorter Catechism to help us understand and apply Scripture’s teaching, especially with a view to helping all who listen to teach others in turn. We will often pause, for example, to ask how a father or mother might teach the truths covered on a given week to their children. The episodes are about 15 to 20 minutes in length. There is minimal ‘fluff’—we try to get straight to the topic at hand. How might the series help listeners in their devotions, and as they serve in the church? All biblical truth, seen by the light of faith, should motivate us to thank, praise, and love the Lord more. Given that the Shorter Catechism summarizes scriptural truth for understanding and for devotion, we should be able to see reasons to thank, praise, and stand in awe of God every week. That said, no merely human document should ever take the place of hearing and reading Scripture. The more time anyone spends in a confession or a catechism, the more they should be motivated to return to the Scriptures with fresh perspective and deeper hunger. We also hope the series will be a blessing to churches. For one thing, well–taught Christians are a blessing to the church. They can and should find ways to build up other members in the faith. It may also be the case that we have some pastors and elders watching or listening in. If so, we hope and trust they will be encouraged to consider whether catechesis could be part of their approach to teaching their congregations. Churches that practice both expository preaching and steady catechesis have often found these modes of teaching to be mutually reinforcing. Why did you choose to use the Shorter Catechism as a framework? There are quite a few Reformed catechisms out there, but only a handful are in frequent use today. The Shorter Catechism has the advantage of broad scope (there are 107 questions and answers in this ‘shorter’ document!) coupled with memorable expression. And, as Dr Chad Van Dixhoorn shares in our bonus historical episode Behind the Scenes at the Westminster Assembly (releasing 28 October), each of the questions and answers is a stand-alone unit—one doesn’t have to have read the whole document to understand what is being asked and answered. content_zh: 下星期将推出来自班纳-威斯敏斯特星期三的新视频和音频资源。 我们的通讯经理Joshua Kellard 每周都会有一位特邀嘉宾参加, 深入讨论威斯敏斯特短卡捷主义的问答。 在这里,约书亚回答了一些关于观众和听众可以从系列中期待什么的问题: 这些播客只是给长老会的,还是给那些可能不太熟悉"更短卡通"的更广大的观众的? 这些播客当然是长老会的, 威斯敏斯特·肖特克·卡特克主义(Westminster Shorter Catechism)是基督教信仰的一种易懂而简洁的表述,因为它在改革期间和之后不久被恢复和澄清. 因此,我冒昧地说,任何真正相信耶稣主的人,如果接受更短的卡德克主义,就会发现它是一份富饶、圣经根基、鼓励和启发性的文件。 我们希望这些播客节目也是这些东西。 还有,我想补充一下,不是所有的客人都是长老会的! 关键在于运用更短的卡德主义来帮助我们理解并应用圣经的教导, 每集会持续多久? 每集"威斯敏斯特周三"以阅读该周的问答开始(有时根据话题的不同会有两集甚至三集). 然后,我们与一位特别的来宾——通常是一位当地教会牧师——深入讨论了问答中包含的圣经教义问题,但我们也有众多神学院教师的代表。 上:一些西敏周三来宾. 重点是利用"更短的卡德克主义"帮助我们理解并应用"圣经"的教义,特别是为了帮助所有倾听者依次教导他人. 例如,我们往往会停下来问,父亲或母亲如何向其子女传授某一周的真相。 剧集长度约15至20分钟. 我们尽量直截了当, 该系列如何帮助听众的奉献,以及他们在教堂中服役? 所有的圣经真理,由信仰之光所见,应该激励我们感谢,赞美,更爱主. 鉴于 " 更短的卡特克主义 " 为理解和奉献总结了文字上的真理,我们应该能够每周看到感谢、赞扬和敬畏上帝的理由。 尽管如此,绝不应仅以人类文件取而代之的是听取和阅读《圣经》。 任何人在忏悔或阴道中花费的时间越多,就越应该以新的视角和更深的饥饿来激励他们回到"圣经". 我们也希望这一系列会给教会带来祝福. 首先,教好基督徒是教会的福分。 他们能够而且应当找到办法,在信仰中培养其他成员。 也可能是有些牧师和长老在看或听。 如果是这样,我们希望并相信,将鼓励他们考虑,天主教会能否成为他们教会的一部分。 既进行说明式传道,又进行平稳天主教的教会往往发现这些教学方式是相辅相成的。 你为什么选择用"更短的卡特主义"作为框架? 那里有很多改革式的天主教,但今天只有很少的宗教经常使用。 Shorter Catechism具有广泛的优势(本文"shorter"文件中有107个问答), 而正如Chad Van Dixhoorn博士在威斯敏斯特大会(10月28日放出)的《幕后新闻》中分享的, 读者常常被俗称神学或牧业所震撼。

summary_zh: 以下信件发表在2025年12月的《旗帜》杂志上。这本书是应一位读者的要求出版的，他认为这本书很有帮助，希望它的忠告也能祝福他人。您也可以在Banner播客上收听这封信的阅读。尊敬的[…]《讲道中的陷阱：一封关于申请的信》（ Pitfalls in Preaching: A Letter on Application ）一文首次出现在美国真理旗帜
title_zh: 讲道中的陷阱：一封关于申请的信
content: The following letter was published in the December 2025 issue of the Banner Magazine. It is published here at the request of a reader who found it helpful, in the hope that its counsel might be blessed to others also. You can also listen to a reading of this letter on the Banner Podcast. Dear J______, Following our conversation about application in preaching, I thought I would send along some thoughts I have had over the years on the subject. I want to point out some pitfalls you may want to keep in mind as you train R______. The only reason I know about them is from spending too much time in them myself! There has been a lot of self–examination and repenting over the years for me in this matter. The first thought is that too often (even in some of the best books on preaching) we hear that the text drives the sermon. This is a half-truth. A potentially dangerous half-truth. I have seen a man so intent on expositing his text well (and he did it very well) that he did not seem to notice or care that a third of the people in the room walked out before he finished preaching because he went on so long and the last meal of the conference was being served to meet the constraint of local train times. A wrong type of focus on the text and its explanation can make us oblivious to the very people the text is for. A preacher who stands up to preach having spent ninety per cent of his sermon preparation time in the week concentrating on the biblical text has not sufficiently realized what preaching actually is. In their book Letters Along the Way D. A. Carson and John Woodbridge put it this way: A chief reason why so much of what passes for evangelical expository preaching is so boring and irrelevant is that the preacher has spent a vastly disproportionate amount of preparation time in exegesis and outlines, and so little in thinking through how the Word of God is to wound and heal (to use the language of Hosea). 1 So preaching is about people. Preaching is about what God has to say to people about their lives . The text for a sermon is what God has to say to people . So the text of a sermon is like the recipe for a dish. A good cook would never be so focused on a recipe that she did not stop to realize that this was not at all the type of food her guests would need or appreciate. She would have her guests in mind from the start. After all, the goal of a good cook is not simply a matter of a recipe or a certain dish. It is feeding and feasting people . People drive the sermon. People are the reason God has given us the message in the biblical text. The biblical text leads the preacher to what the people need to hear from God. But the biblical text is only a means . The goal is people—to bring them somewhere that God wants them to go. To enlighten them, change them, help them, console them, correct them, train them to worship and serve God. People-oriented preaching comes from a God-centred, loving interest in them . Text-oriented preaching may simply come from the preacher’s love for preaching, for exegesis or for theology. A physician may be fascinated by medical treatments. But the good physician’s real interest is not treatments but people whose suffering has called for those treatments. Just so, true preaching is about people. That brings me to a second, related thought. We are often told that in preparing a sermon the key is finding the main idea of the text. To consider this as the key is not a people-oriented point of view and does not produce good preaching. It produces preaching with lots of emphasis on ideas and little emphasis on application. The key to preparing a sermon is not to find the main idea of the text. It is to find the main goal of the text. Not ‘What does the biblical text mainly say?’ But rather ‘What does this text intend to mainly do for people?’ What does the text intend mainly to effect in the lives of people? What does this text aim to move the people to believe, to do, to become? Application! A. T. Pierson, i
content_zh: 以下信件发表于"班纳杂志"2025年12月号. 它应一位读者的要求在这里出版,他觉得它很有帮助,希望它的律师也能得到他人的祝福。 也可以在"班纳·波德克特"上收听对这封信的读取. 亲爱的J-,在我们讨论申请布道后,我想,我将提出一些多年来我对这一问题的看法。 我想指出一些陷阱 你可能想记住 当你训练R. 我了解他们的唯一原因 就是自己花太多时间在他们身上 多年来,我一直以来都在自责自悔。 第一种想法是,太多时候(即使在一些关于布道的好书中),我们听到文字驱动布道. 这是半个事实。 一个潜在的危险 半真相。 我见过一个男人如此有意地公开他的文字(他做得非常好),他似乎没有注意到或关心房间里有三分之一的人在他完成布道之前就离开,因为他走了这么长一段时间,会议的最后一餐是用来应付当地火车时间的限制。 错误地注重案文及其解释会使我们忘记案文所要为的人。 一位挺身而出进行传道的传道者,在一周里,他90%的布道准备时间都集中在圣经文本上,但是他没有充分意识到实际的传道内容。 在他们所著的"沿着路"(Letrys A. A. Carson)和"约翰·伍德布里奇"(John Woodbridge)一书中这样写道: 传福音的宣讲之所以如此之多,实在是无趣而无关紧要的一个主要原因是,传道人花费了大量的不相称的准备时间来解剖和提纲,在思考"上帝之道"是怎样去伤口和愈合(使用"霍西"的语言)时却很少考虑. 1个 故传道以人为事. 意义在于上帝要对人们说 他们的生活 讲道的文字是上帝要对人们说的话。 所以布道的文字就像菜谱。 一个好厨师永远也不会把注意力集中在一个配方上,以至于她不禁意识到这根本不是客人需要或欣赏的食物类型. 她一开始就想着她的客人 毕竟,一个好厨师的目标不仅仅是一个菜谱或某种菜肴的问题. 它在给人们提供食物和盛宴。 人们驱使布道。 人们是上帝给我们圣经文本中的信息的原因。 圣经文本将传道人引向人们需要从上帝那里听到的. 但圣经文本只是一个手段。 目标是人们,把他们带到上帝要他们去的地方去。 为了启蒙他们,改变他们,帮助他们,安慰他们,矫正他们,训练他们去崇拜并服务于上帝. 以人为中心的布道来自以上帝为中心, 以文字为取向的传道可能只是来自传道者对传道、开教或神学的热爱。 医生可能因治疗而着迷。 但好医生的真正兴趣不是治疗,而是那些遭受痛苦需要治疗的人。 所以,真正的传道是关于人的。 这让我想到另一个相关的想法。 我们经常被告知,在准备布道时,关键在于找到案文的主要想法。 将此视为关键不是以人民为导向的观点,也不产生好传道. 它产生许多强调思想的布道,很少强调应用。 准备布道的关键不是找到文本的主要想法. 它是为了找到案文的主要目标。 而非"圣经主要说些什么?" 但更确切地说,“这个文本主要是为了什么?” 案文主要打算如何影响人们的生活? 这个文字的目的是要促使人们相信,去做,变成什么? 申请! A. T. 皮尔逊,i

summary_zh: 以下摘录来自詹姆斯·沃克（ James Walker ）的《苏格兰的神学和神学家》（ The Theology and Theologians of Scotland ） ，我们刚刚对其进行了排版，并以布面版重新出版。沃克在这里回应了对苏格兰基督教的批评，批评它过于教义化：然后，我认为这个想法在我们这个时代已经占据了许多人，苏格兰威士忌[...]后教条主义者反对教条首先出现在美国真理旗帜上。
title_zh: 教条主义者反对教条
content: The following excerpt is from James Walker’s The Theology and Theologians of Scotland , which we have just typeset and republished in a clothbound edition. Walker is here responding to the criticism of Scottish Christianity which faults it for being too doctrinal: Then, again, I think the idea has taken possession of many in our day, that Scotch religion is a religion of speculative dogma, with little in it of the personal Christ. Now it seems to me there is a great deal said at present about Doctrine or Dogma which means nothing. How can you act in regard to or feel about a thing, save as you have some conception and some opinion concerning it? You must have some opinion about the person of Christ, if He is to be an element in your practical life. How can He act on you otherwise? And, therefore, as you are Trinitarian, or Arian, or Unitarian, or Humanitarian, or something else, so will be the effect on you. And, in fact, the man who abuses dogmas is as much a dealer in dogmas as his neighbours. What is it but a dogma—generally asserted, indeed, with a fierce and contemptuous fanaticism, and carried out with a remorseless logic—that there should be no dogmas? Like scepticism, this sort of thing kills itself. Say what men will, all action, all organization, all religious or irreligious fellowship, is based upon a Credo. In regard to many who bring the accusation most readily about Scottish doctrinalism, I assert that there are none more doctrinal than themselves. The Broad Churchman maintains the doctrine of the Divine Fatherhood; puts that doctrine into definite conception; argues on the basis of that doctrine to immense conclusions, which make illusive a large amount of the deepest and most powerful experiences of Christian history. The Unitarian maintains the doctrine of the Divine Unity, and evolves therefrom proposition after proposition, overthrowing, as he thinks, all the life-giving Christian beliefs. The real truth is that orthodoxy is chary of the speculative. Mystery is one of its fundamental ideas. The Theosophic 1 belongs far more to heterodox Alexandrianism than orthodox Augustinianism. I do not think that it can be affirmed of Calvin, that he was as supreme in the metaphysical or speculative as in all else. Certainly our Scottish theology is not in any proper sense a metaphysical system, though there has been often a cloud or a halo of metaphysics about it, but the product in the main of an honest study of the Bible and a practical religious experience. The doctrines which have been prominently taught among us, such as the atonement of Christ, justification, the new birth, the indwelling of the Holy Ghost, are not in any sense speculative human reasonings, but transcendent facts,—mysteries which, according to all experience, tell with prodigious power on the human soul, and take hold of the deepest convictions of the least philosophical and cultured. content_zh: 以下摘录出自詹姆斯·沃克的"苏格兰神学与神学",我们刚刚对它进行打字并重新以布满的版本出版. 沃克在此回应苏格兰基督教的批评, 然后,我再说一遍,我认为这个想法在我们这个时代已经占有了许多人, 苏格兰宗教是一种投机教条的宗教, 很少包含个人的基督。 现在,在我看来,目前关于理论或道格玛的说法很多,这毫无意义。 除了你对某件事有某种概念和看法之外,你怎么能对某件事采取行动或感觉呢? 如果上帝要成为你实际生活中的一个要素,你一定对基督的人有些看法. 怎么会 他对你另当别论? 因此,既然你是三硝基亚人,或亚利安人,或统一人,或人道,或别的东西,那么,对你们的影响也会是这样。 事实上 虐待教条的人 和邻居一样是教条商人 除了一个教条外,什么是不应该有教条的? 教条一般是用一种激烈而可鄙的狂热主义来断言的,并且以毫无悔恨的逻辑来进行。 类似怀疑,这种东西会自杀。 说男人的意志,所有的行动,所有组织,所有宗教或非宗教的研究金,都是建立在克里多之上的. 对于许多最容易指控苏格兰教条主义的人,我断言,没有什么比他们自己更多的教条了。 Broad Churchman坚持了神之父的教义;将该教义置于明确的概念之中;基于该教义而论证了巨大的结论,这些结论使基督教历史上大量最深刻和最强大的经验变得虚幻。 统一主义者坚持"神通统一"的学说,并从中演化出在命题后的建议,推翻了他所想的,所有赋予生命的基督教信仰. 真正的事实是,正统性是投机性的魅力。 神秘主义是其基本思想之一. 相较于正统的奥古斯丁主义,"神话一"更属于异体的亚历山大主义. 我并不认为卡尔文能被证实 他在物理或推测方面 和所有其他方面一样至高无上 当然,我们的苏格兰神学在任何适当的意义上都不是一个元物理系统,尽管关于它经常有云或光环的元物理,但主要产物是对"圣经"进行诚实研究并实践宗教经验. 在我们中间受到突出教导的理论,如赎罪、辩护、新诞生、使圣灵安息等,从任何意义上讲,都不是推测人类的推理,而是超越的事实,根据所有的经验,这些神话以对人类灵魂的超乎寻常的力量加以说明,并信奉哲学和文化最低的信念。 沃克17和18世纪的苏格兰神学和神学家,詹姆斯价格28.00美元 原价:28.00美元 现价:25.20美元 " 在自己的部门里学习更多的加进纸板描述认可 " 。 – NICK NESTHAM Book Direct James Walker(1821–1891)属于能够掌握一个国家神学文献的这一稀有阶层。 这本珍贵的书里有水果... summary: The following is an excerpt from Walter J. Chantry’s Call the Sabbath a Delight (pages 96–102). summary_zh: 以下摘录自Walter J. Chantry的Call the Sabbath a Delight （第96–102页）。当一些基督徒开始相信守安息日为圣是他们的责任时，他们变得非常害怕，以免在主日从事错误的活动。这种担忧的形式通常是想要[…]与安息日有关的“良心案例”帖子首先出现在美国真理旗帜上。
title_zh: 与安息日相关的「良心案例」
content: The following is an excerpt from Walter J. Chantry’s Call the Sabbath a Delight (pages 96–102). When some Christians come to believe that it is their duty to keep the Sabbath Day holy, they become very fearful lest they engage in the wrong activities on the Lord’s Day. Such apprehension often takes the form of wanting very specific answers from a minister or a counsellor. May I go bicycle-riding on Sunday? Is it all right to go jogging on the Lord’s Day? Should I purchase medicine for a child with a sore throat? It is as if the believer is collecting a large list of items, next to which he is writing ‘do’ or ‘don’t’. This sort of inquiry regarding explicit details of behaviour is, unfortunately, encouraged by a type of church leader who feeds his ego by promoting himself as a kind of ethical guru. Wishing to be the ideal elder or conscientious teacher, this ‘leader’ offers direction in minute particulars of living. His style of handling practical issues of living makes his people utterly dependent upon his counsel. His people become incapable of coping with decisions unless the ‘oracle of wisdom’ has decreed exact permission or prohibition. Momentarily, it may seem wonderfully good fortune to have such an involved counsellor giving precise directives, but in the end it makes dependent children of those who ask. At the head of this chapter is printed Paul’s prayer for the Philippians. He asked the Lord to increase his flock’s knowledge and depth of insight. These gifts he desired for them so that they would be able to discern what is best when confronted with any decision. It was never intended that God’s people be given exhaustively itemized delineation of what to do in every circumstance. He did not place elders in leadership so that they might dictate what specific course to follow in every particular. He does not give divine revelation as to which alternative to choose at a given moment. Our Lord has given us the great principles of his word. Also, he has sent the Holy Spirit to assist our understanding, so that, in any given set of alternatives requiring judgment, the individual saint will be exercised in spirit. Only by inner wrestlings will he increase in discernment of what is best. In Hebrews 5:14 we are told that ‘solid food is for the mature, for those who have their powers of discernment trained by constant practice to distinguish good from evil.’ It may seem comfortable to have a list to tick off without thought. However, the truth is that such practice atrophies the mind and heart. General principles from God’s word are adequate guidelines to equip a Christian, aided by the Holy Spirit, to face every eventuality. The Sabbath Day is to be kept in mind. It is to be devoted with joy to the worship and service of God. This day is special and is not to be cluttered with our work or with the employment of others, except so far as will serve in God’s worship, in man’s necessities, and in showing mercy to our fellow human beings. God’s word is a sufficient guide. All that is needed is for the individual Christian to exercise his personal discernment as to what is best. Thus he trains himself to distinguish good from evil. Included in this exercise is the necessity of becoming independent of others. The fear of man’s opinion regarding your application of these principles must not keep you from applying the principles before God. This is a freedom of conscience given us in Jesus Christ. It must not be surrendered to anyone. Being subject to our Lord and his word demands that we keep ourselves free from the tyranny of human opinion, even ‘expert’ opinion. Many of the particular questions men and women ask cannot be given a definite answer. More rests upon motive and intent than upon the outward acts we do on the Sabbath. ‘May I go bicycle-riding on Sunday?’ Because younger children are not equipped to discern their own heart motives or the application of general principles, parents must make some rules for their households.

Chantry的《安息日称为欢乐》(第96-102页)的摘录。 当一些基督教徒相信安息日是他们的责任的时候,他们就非常害怕在主日从事不义的活动。 这种担心往往表现为希望部长或顾问作出非常具体的答复。 我可以星期天骑自行车吗? 在主节去慢跑可以吗? 我应该买药给喉咙痛的孩子吗? 似乎信徒正在收集一大堆物品, 不幸的是,这种关于明确行为细节的询问受到某种类型的教会领袖的鼓励,他们通过宣传自己是一种道德的教义来养活自己的自我。 希望成为理想的长辈或良心老师, 他处理生活的实际问题的风格使他的人民完全依赖他的律师。 除非`智慧之神'下达确切的许可或禁止令,否则他的人民将无法应付决定。 暂时来说,让这样一个参赞提供精确的指示似乎是极好的运气,但最后却使那些提出要求的人有受抚养的子女。 保罗为菲利浦人祈祷。 他要求上帝增加他的羊群的知识和洞察力。 他想要给他们这些礼物,以便他们在面对任何决定时能够辨别什么是最好的。 从来没有打算让上帝的子民在每一情况下都详细分门别类地划分应做什么。 他没有安排长辈担任领导职务,以便他们能够决定每一具体过程中应遵循的具体方针。 他没有透露在特定时刻可以选择哪种选择。 我们的主给了我们他所说的伟大原则。 另外,他还派遣了"圣灵"来协助我们的理解,这样,在任何一套需要判断的既定选择中,单个圣人将会在精神上行使. 只有通过内在的摔跤,他才能提高辨别什么是最好的。 在希伯来语:5:14中,我们被告知,`坚固的食物是给成熟的人的,对于那些有辨识能力的人来说,他们通过不断的练习来区分善与恶。 有一份清单可以不经思考地删除,这似乎很舒服。 然而,实际情况是,这种做法会损害心灵和心灵。 从上帝的言语来看,一般原则是适当的准则,可以使一个基督教徒在圣灵的帮助下面对每一次事件。 安息日要记住。 其能以欢喜而奉献于神通之所礼拜及事. 这一天是特别的,我们的工作或他人的工作不会受到干扰,除非在上帝的崇拜中、在人类的必需品中和在对我们的人类同胞表示怜悯中服务。 真主的话足为引导。 需要的只是基督徒个人对什么是最好的个人认识。 于是他训练自己 以区分善与恶。 这项工作包括必须独立于他人。 人类对于你应用这些原则的意见的恐惧,决不能妨碍你在上帝面前应用这些原则。 这是耶稣基督赋予我们的良心自由. 绝不能向任何人投降。 服从我们的主及其言辞,要求我们远离人类观点的暴政,甚至 " 专家 " 观点。 男人和女人提出的许多具体问题不能得到明确的答案。 更多的取决于动机和意图,而不是我们安息日的外在行动。 我星期天可以骑自行车吗? 由于年幼儿童没有能力辨别自己的心脏动机或适用一般原则,父母必须为家庭制定一些规则。

summary_zh: 我们都需要对上帝对所有众生和事件的主权统治有更大的敏感性。亚历山大·卡森（ Alexander Carson ）的研究《圣经所体现的天意的历史》（ The History of Providence as Manifested in Scripture ）可以帮助我们培养这种敏感性。以下是耶利米书第14章中他对犹大饥荒主题的评论：由于饥荒的存在， […]犹大的饥荒后：上帝的普罗维登斯显示首先出现在美国真理的旗帜上。
title_zh: 犹大饥荒：神的普罗维登斯显现
content: We all need a greater sensitivity to God’s sovereign rule over all beings and events. Alexander Carson’s study, The History of Providence as Manifested in Scripture can help train us in such sensitivity. Here are his comments on the subject of famine in Judah from Jeremiah 14: FOR the existence of plenty as of famine, the wisdom of this world looks no higher than to what are called second causes. God, it is considered, is no farther concerned in these matters than as the author of certain general laws. He has set the machine a-going, and it continues to work by its own construction, without any regulation of a superintending hand. Climate, soil, cultivation, need, it is confessed, favourable seasons, but any divine direction of weather is supposed to be unnecessary. Timely rain—or the want of it, is a matter below the attention of the Ruler of the world. The blight and the mildew, the wet and the caterpillar, are enemies with which the farmer is to struggle; but they are never considered as armies of devastation sent into the fields by a righteous Providence. The history of the Old Testament gives us a key to Providence in the production of famine or of plenty. God regulates the supplies of the children of men as exactly as if each individual of the human race had his rations assigned him by the angels of heaven every rising sun: ‘The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah concerning the dearth. Judah mourneth, and the gates thereof languish; they are black unto the ground; and the cry of Jerusalem is gone up. And their nobles have sent their little ones to the waters: they came to the pits, and found no water; they returned with their vessels empty: they were ashamed and confounded, and covered their heads. Because the ground is chapt, for there was no rain in the earth, the ploughmen were ashamed, they covered their heads. Yea, the hind also calved in the field, and forsook it, because there was no grass. And the wild asses did stand in the high places, they snuffed up the wind like dragons; their eyes did fail, because there was no grass. O Lord, though our iniquities testify against us, do thou it for thy name’s sake: for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against thee.’—Jer. 14:1–7. As in creation and in Providence, so in redemption, God hides himself in the midst of a blaze of light. In all his works he reveals himself, yet the enmity of the human heart will not allow men to see him. And what is most strange, the savage sees a divine hand in the works of Providence; it is unseen and denied by philosophical wisdom. The illiterate peasant hears God in his voice of thunder and storms, and acknowledges divine wrath in pestilence, sword, and famine. But the philosopher perceives nothing in all these but the course of nature. The wisdom of man makes itself ignorant of what the very beasts seem to feel. content_zh: 我们都需要更加关注上帝对所有生命和事件的主权统治。 Alexander Carson的研究, 《普罗维登斯的历史》, 以下是他从耶利米14号对犹大饥荒主题的评论: 对于饥荒时存在的富足,这个世界的智慧看起来并不比所谓的"第二原因"更高. 据认为,与某些一般法律的制定者相比,上帝在这些事务上没有更多的关切。 他把机器设为正常运行,它继续按自己的构造运作,没有任何管制的上司手. 气候,土壤,种植,需要,是承认的,有利的季节,但是任何神圣的天气方向都应该是不必要的. 及时降雨——或者说,这是世界统治者不关心的问题。 荒凉和温和的、湿润的和毛毛的,是农民要与之斗争的敌人;但他们从未被视为正义的普罗维登斯派入田地的毁灭军队。 "旧约"的历史为我们提供了普罗维登斯产生饥荒或富饶的关键. 真主为世人的给养而加以管理,犹如每个人的给养,每逢太阳升起,就奉天天神所赐给每个人一样。 犹大哀悼而其中的城门枯萎;他们已变成黑色的;耶路撒冷的呼声已升起。 其贵人又将小人送入水中去:来入坑中去,又无取出水来;又以器物入空而回;自惭而自愧,自蒙而出. 因为地是分明的,因为地上没有下雨,犁地人感到羞愧,就把头盖了起来. 有之,后人又以地为牛,而弃之,因有草而去. 野驴们的确站在高处,他们像龙一样把风扑倒;他们的眼睛确实衰败了,因为没有草. 主啊!我们的罪过虽能证明我们的罪过,但求你为你的名字而行之;我们的背负是多的;我们确已犯罪了。 与创造和普罗维登斯一样,在救赎中,上帝将自己隐藏在一束光芒中. 在他的所有作品中,他都暴露了自己,然而人心的敌意却不允许人见到他. 最奇怪的是,野蛮人看到普罗维登斯的作品中有神之手;它是看不见的,被哲学智慧所否定. 文盲农民在雷和风暴中听到上帝的声音,在瘟疫、剑和饥荒中承认神圣的愤怒。 但是哲学家在所有这些事物中,除了自然的走向,什么也看不出来. 人类的智慧使自己对野兽的感受一无所知. 更多信息:卡森所著"普罗维登斯的历史"(The History of Providence As Expressed in Books by Carson, Alexander price from: $ 13.50 学习更多选择选项描述) 基督教徒最感兴趣的话题。 以天经为阅读者,并举出真主赐予信士们的慰藉。 264pp. Featured Photo(当作品在社交媒体上分享时可以看见),

title_zh: 让苦涩的东西变甜的上帝
content: The Israelites had just walked between the walls of the water of the Red Sea and watched as the Lord washed away the whole Egyptian army. They sang a song of triumph on the far shore of the sea, rejoicing in the fear that had fallen on the surrounding nations (Ex. 15:14-16) and looking forward to taking possession of the Promised Land in the near future (Ex. 15:17). But within three days they raised a very different kind of sound—a chorus of grumbling against Moses because there was no water to drink at Marah (Ex. 15:22-26). I wonder what they expected would happen after the Red Sea. A straight, unhindered journey to the land flowing with milk and honey? Instead the first thing the Lord does is to lead his people to the undrinkable water of Marah. There is no question that the Lord is the one who led them there—it is easy enough to take a wrong turn when you are following Google Maps, but not when you are following a towering pillar of cloud or fire! So why did God lead Israel to Marah? Is it because he is sadistic and cruel and takes delight in watching his people suffer dehydration and fear? Is it because he is really bad at geography? Of course not! In fact we’re told why he brought Israel to Marah in Ex. 15:25: There the Lord tested them. In fact, the whole wilderness is a place of testing. That’s the significance of the wilderness—it’s a hard place. Deuteronomy 8:15 calls it ‘the vast and dreadful wilderness, that thirsty and waterless land, with its venomous snakes and scorpions.’ God is training his infant son to trust him—and training is always painful. There are no short cuts, whether in the physical training of our bodies to make them stronger and faster, or in the mental training of our minds to increase our knowledge and understanding, or in the spiritual training of our souls to grow in godliness. Learning to trust God is not something we can do lounging on the sofa. It means being put into situations that are stressful, confusing, messy and complicated, when we don’t understand what is going on or see any answers. Anyone can trust God when things are easy; the real test is if you will trust God when things are tough. Israel’s failure Marah was Israel’s first test and they failed. They have been travelling for three days and haven’t found any water. Supplies are running low. Perhaps as they saw the waters of Marah in the distance they finished up their last reserves: ‘It’ll be OK—we can refill very soon!’ Imagine the relief and joy as the first to reach Marah fall down and scoop the water to their mouths. And imagine them spitting it out as they discover it is foul and undrinkable. They’re not just disappointed—they’re horrified . Panic seizes them. ‘What shall we drink?’ (v. 24) This is not like someone in a restaurant complaining that their steak is a bit on the tough side or that the soup is a tad cold. They are exhausted and dehydrated and they can’t see any way of getting water. Suddenly life is hanging by a thread. There is nothing unreasonable about their concern. That is not why they fail the test. They fail the test because of their attitude. They grumble: the word means ‘hostile complaining, verbal attacks of dissatisfied people.’ Why do they grumble? There are at least two reasons: Faithlessness . They do not trust God. They don’t trust his power (that he can take care of them) or his goodness (that he wants to take care of them). They should have gone to the Lord with their needs, humbly asking him to provide what they needed. And this lack of faith was due to… Forgetfulness . This is the diagnosis of Psalm 78:40ff: How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness and grieved him in the desert! … They did not remember his power or the day when he redeemed them from the foe , 43 when he performed his signs in Egypt and his marvels in the fields of Zoan. The people had such short memories! It has only been three days since they walked through the Red Sea! It has been just a few weeks since they witn
content_zh: 以色列人刚刚走入了红海的水墙之间,看着上帝冲走整个埃及军队。 他们在远海岸上唱了一首"胜利之歌",欣喜地感受到了降临于周边民族的恐惧(Ex. 15:14-16)并期待着在不久的将来占有所承诺之地(Ex. 15:17). 但他们在三日内,举出一种非常不同的声音,一种对穆萨抱怨的合唱,因为在马拉没有水可饮(前15:22-26). 不知道红海之后他们会怎样 直走无阻地去 充满牛奶和蜂蜜的土地? 取而代之的是,主所行之事,是引其民入于马拉所出不可饮之水也. 毫无疑问,主是带领他们到那里去的——当你遵循Google地图时,很容易错转,但当你遵循高耸起的云柱或火柱时,就不是了! 那么为什么上帝带领以色列找到马拉? 是不是因为他是虐待狂和残忍的,在看着他的人民遭受脱水和恐惧时感到愉快? 是不是因为他在地理上很不好? 当然不是! 事实上我们被告知他为何在前15:25将以色列带到马拉:上帝在那里测试过他们。 事实上,整个荒地都是试验地. 这是荒野的意义, 8: 15 脱胎手术称之为:"大而可怕的荒野, 渴而无水之地, 有毒蛇和蝎子. 真主正在训练他的儿子,以便他信任他。训练确是痛苦的。 无论是身体锻炼,使其更强而更快,还是心灵修炼,以增进我们的知识和理解,或是心灵修炼,以在教化中成长,都没有任何短短的削减. 学会相信上帝不是我们能在沙发上做的事 这表示当我们不明白发生了什么情况或看到答案时, 当事情变得容易的时候,任何人都可以信任真主;真正的考验是,如果事情变得艰难的时候,你们要信任真主的话。 以色列的失败马拉是以色列的第一个考验, 他们已经旅行了三天, 补给不足。 也许当他们看到马拉的海水, 想象一下,解脱和欢乐是第一个到达马拉的人倒下,把水灌入口中. 想象一下他们发现它肮脏而不可饮用时就吐出它. 他们不仅失望, 恐慌抓住他们。 我们喝什么? (v.24) 这不像餐馆里有人抱怨 他们的牛排有点硬 或者汤有点冷 他们已经精疲力竭并脱水, 突然间,生命被一丝一缕地挂起 他们的关切没有什么不合理的。 这并不是他们失败的原因。 他们因为态度而未能通过测试. 他们抱怨道:这个词的意思是“敌意抱怨, 他们为什么抱怨? 至少有两个原因:失信。 他们不相信上帝。 他们不相信他的能力(他能照顾他们)或善良(他想照顾他们), 他们应该带着自己的需要去主那里,谦卑地要求他提供他们需要的东西. 缺乏信心是因为... 这就是对"诗经"78:40ff的诊断:他们在荒野中频繁地反抗他,在沙漠中为他悲伤!...... 他们不记得他的威力,也不记得他从敌人手中赎回他们的那一天,43岁时他在埃及行过他的迹象,他在Zoan地上行过他的奇事。 人们记忆很短! 他们从红海走过才三天! 几周前他们才开始

summary_zh: 费丝·库克（ Faith Cook ）的《麻烦之旅》（ Troubled Journey ）讲述了她作为OMF中国传教士的女儿的早期经历。为了表彰父母的信仰、勇气和自我牺牲，她还富有同情心地揭示了与父母长期分离所带来的家庭剥夺。下面的摘录是该书的第11章，其中[…]邮政父母：传教士儿童的经历首先出现在美国真理旗帜上。
title_zh: 邮政父母：传教士儿童的经历
content: Faith Cook’s Troubled Journey narrates her early experiences as the daughter of OMF missionaries to China. Honouring the faith, courage, and self-sacrifice of her parents, she also shines a compassionate light on the family deprivations brought about by long periods of separation from them. The excerpt below is Chapter 11 of the book in question, which cover Faith’s childhood between the ages of fourteen and eighteen. A passage on the P & O Carthage was booked for Stanley and Norah [Faith’s parents—Ed.] in early January 1952, only eight months after our family had first arrived back from China. It was a subdued Christmas we spent together that year, the last for some years to come. Frantic packing followed, purchasing school uniform and preparing for the long outward journey back to the Far East, this time by sea. A round of speaking engagements filled the days for my parents and seemingly eased the ache of the forthcoming separation. As the day of parting drew ever nearer, I noticed a new tenderness in their attitude towards me – a tenderness that only added to my distress. And at last came the day of departure. It would be four years before we would see them again. Photographs were taken on the steps of the mission headquarters, as all joined to wish the departing missionaries well. Norah’s expression told a story, as did fifteen-year-old Christopher’s forced smile, for in reality, the boy’s spirit was at breaking point. On we went to the station where our parents would board a train to Southampton. A large contingent of missionary personnel followed, for this departure was highly significant for the entire future of the mission, urgently seeking a new role for its operations now the door to China was closed. I found myself thrust to the back of the crowd as the train slowly moved off. Suddenly one more thoughtful friend spotted the irony of the situation and pushed me to the front to catch the last glimpse of my parents as they stood waving at the window of the train, my mother looking tense and tearful, and my father strained. Back at the mission home once more, we were at a loose end. No guardian had yet been appointed to care for us, although one or two kindly adults helped out if I asked for assistance. The Spring term would soon begin and I was glad. Some of my new clothes were too long and needed altering, and I discovered with alarm that the shoe repairer considered my school shoes beyond his skills to patch up. Never handy with a needle, I tried my best to turn up the hems myself. At last the third week of January arrived and I was on the train back to my well-loved school – a place I now regarded as home. Although soon immersed once more in all the trivia of boarding school life, I found time each week to write a letter to my parents. The first few letters were addressed to ports en route for Malaysia where the P & O Carthage would call: Aden, Penang and then to Singapore to await their arrival. Stanley and Norah treasured these schoolgirl epistles, storing them all up, until at last my father would present his married daughter with a shoe box crammed with letters dating from January 1952 until the time that he and my mother finally retired from missionary service in Malaysia more than twenty years later. These letters form a unique commentary on the development of a postal relationship with my parents that would form the bedrock of my security and development from a young teenager to womanhood and beyond. Faithfully my parents replied to each letter, commenting on my progress, chiding when they could sense my behaviour was becoming erratic, and offering advice as well as they were able. Not long after arriving back at the mission headquarters in London at the end of the spring school term, I discovered that a middle-aged couple had been appointed as guardians for the children of the missionaries: Louis and Nancy Gaussen. Understanding and kindly, they were well-suited to care for the children. ‘Mr and Mrs Gaussen
content_zh: Faith Cook的"麻烦之旅"讲述了她作为OMF传教士去中国的女儿的早期经历. 她以对父母的信仰、勇气和自我牺牲的敬意,也为长期与父母分离所带来的家庭贫困而发出同情之光。 下面的节录是该书第11章,其中涵盖了费斯14至18岁的童年. 1952年1月初,我们一家刚从中国回来才八个月,为斯坦利和诺拉(Faith的父母——Ed.)预订了P & O迦太基号上的一段。 那年是我们一起度过的圣诞 几年来的最后一天 紧随其后的弗朗克包装,购买了校服并准备了远东的漫长出行旅程,这次是海上出行. 一轮的演讲为我父母提供了时间,似乎缓解了即将到来的分居的痛苦。 随着离别日的临近,我注意到他们对我的态度出现了新的温柔,这种温柔只会使我更加痛苦。 终于到了出发之日 四年后我们才能再见到他们 对特派团总部的步骤进行了拍照,因为所有人都希望离开的传教士们一切顺利。 Norah的言论讲述了一个故事,15岁的Christopher被迫微笑也讲述了一个故事,因为实际上,这名男孩的精神正在崩溃。 我们去了车站 在那里,我们的父母 会登上火车到南安普顿。 随即派出了大批传教人员,因为这次出走对传教团的整个未来都具有重大意义,因此紧急寻求为传教团的行动起新的作用,现在中国的大门已经关闭了。 我发现自己被推倒 在人群的后部 当火车慢慢地离开。 突然又有一位深思熟虑的朋友发现情况具有讽刺意味,把我推到前面,以抓住我父母站在火车窗前挥手的最后一眼,我母亲看起来紧张而泪流满面,而我父亲也感到紧张. 回到了任务之家, 我们处在一个松散的结局。 目前还没有指定监护人来照顾我们,不过,如果我想得到帮助,一两个成年人会帮助我们。 春季学期即将开始 我很高兴 一些我的新衣服太长,需要更换,我惊恐地发现,修鞋者认为我的校鞋超出了他的能力来补补补. 我从不用针指手画脚,我尽力自己把螺丝弄大 终于在一月的第三个星期抵达, 我坐上火车回到我深爱的学校, 虽然我很快再次沉浸在寄宿学校生活的三难之中,但我发现每周都有时间写信给我的父母。 最初的几封信是寄给前往马来西亚的港口,P&O迦太基会称这些港口为:亚丁,槟城,再到新加坡等他们到达. 斯坦利和诺拉珍藏了这些女学生的表皮, 把它们全部储存起来, 直到最后我父亲会向他的已婚女儿展示一个鞋盒, 里面塞有1952年1月的信件, 直到他和我妈妈20多年后终于从马来西亚的传教士退休。 这些信件构成了关于与我父母发展邮政关系的独特评论,这将构成我从青少年到妇女时代及以后的安全和发展的基石。 诚然,我的父母每一封信都回信,评论我的进展,当他们能感觉到我的行为变得不规则时,他们就会发号施令,并尽可能地提供建议。 在春季学期结束回到伦敦的使团总部不久后,我发现一对中年夫妇被指定为传教士子女监护人:路易和南希·高森. 理解和友善,他们很适合照顾孩子。 高森夫妇

Some teaching on the Christian life asserts that […]   The post  In the Christian Life There is No Necessary Crisis Experience  appeared first on  Banner of Truth USA .
summary_zh: 六个帖子中的第四个帖子包含了阿尔伯特· N ·马丁（ Albert N. Martin ）在1984年旗帜青年大会（ Banner Youth Conference ）上给出的教学内容，展示了基督教生活的基本圣经神学。在基督徒的生活中，没有承诺或命令的危机经历是必不可少的元素。一些关于基督徒生活的教导断言， […]《基督徒生活中没有必要的危机经历》一文首先出现在《美国真理旗帜》上。
title_zh: 在基督徒的生活中，没有必要的危机经历
content: The fourth of six posts containing the substance of teaching given by Albert N. Martin at the 1984 Banner Youth Conference, presenting a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. There is no crisis experience promised or commanded as an essential element in living the Christian life. Some teaching on the Christian life asserts that only a low level of Christian experience can be realized by the person who has not had a crisis experience subsequent to regeneration, or at least subsequent to conversion and to the beginning of conscious Christian experience. Furthermore, it is asserted that the crisis experience is both commanded and promised by God as the entrance into a qualitatively new dimension or level of spiritual experience, reality and power. Throughout the history of the Christian church there have been many different strands of this crisis teaching. There is what we might call ‘classic Wesleyan perfectionism,’ which concentrated particularly upon sanctification and spoke of a baptism of purifying fire, or of coming into a state of perfect love. It concentrated not so much on power for service or upon inward feelings, but on a crisis experience in which the power of indwelling sin was to all intents and purposes negated. I have read enough of classic Wesleyan theology to know that there are different opinions as to what John Wesley himself taught on the subject. But in a general descriptive manner this, I believe, is an accurate representation of old-style classic Wesleyan perfectionism. Then, too, there is ‘the old Pentecostalism’ in which the emphasis was upon a baptism in the Holy Spirit, generally subsequent to conversion, and invariably manifested by speaking in tongues: the way you knew that you had this baptism of power was that, when it came to you, you spoke in tongues. The primary focus in old classic Pentecostalism was the matter of power for service. Thirdly, there is the modern ‘charismatic movement.’ Like classic Pentecostalism, its teachers use many of the same passages in the Book of Acts to support their theory of this necessary crisis. So they emphasize that in most cases—although there are different schools among modern charismatics—it will be manifested by the speaking in tongues. Some are content to believe you have ‘got it’ if you have a season of holy laughter. Others, however, say that you have not spoken in tongues because you have some psychological hold-ups, and if these can be removed the tongues are there. You just have not given them utterance. Here the emphasis is not so much on a baptism of purifying fire (as in the case of old classic Wesleyan perfectionism), or the baptism of power (as in the case of old classic Pentecostalism), but more upon a baptism of joyful praise-filled experience. I have been speaking of generalities, but I believe they are accurate. Fourthly, there are the various forms of ‘higher life’ teaching. What they have in common is this: you are simply converted, simply united to Christ, simply regenerated, and then you come to a crisis of surrender and faith, in which ‘you let go and let God’ and appropriate the indwelling life of Christ. The common denominator is that it is a crisis without any external manifestation of tongues or holy laughter or shouting or jumping, but the end result will be new power to live a holy life—the emphasis falls upon the ability to be more efficient in the path of holiness. Fifthly, there is a kind of teaching which has both old and modern proponents. It focuses on assurance, and has been expressed in terms of the biblical language of a ‘sealing of the Holy Spirit.’ Some of the Puritans—Thomas Goodwin, for example—taught this. There have been certain preachers in our own day who have believed this very strongly and emphasized it repeatedly. The basic concern in this teaching is that, subsequent to regeneration and conversion, there is a crisis experience in which the believer enters into a qualitatively new dimension of assurance by
content_zh: 阿尔伯特·N·马丁在1984年班纳青年会议上发表的包含教学内容的六篇文章中的第四篇,介绍了基督教生活的基本圣经神学. 没有任何危机经历作为过上基督教生活的一项基本要素得到承诺或接受。 一些关于基督教生活的教义主张,在再生后,或至少是在皈依后,以及自觉的基督教经历开始后,没有危机经历的人,只有低水平的基督教经验才能实现. 此外,有人断言,危机经历既是上帝的旨意,也是上帝的允诺,是精神经历、现实和力量进入一个全新的层面或层次的。 在基督教会的历史上,这种危机教育有许多不同的内容。 我们可能称之为“经典的卫斯理完美主义 ” , 它不是把精力集中在服务或内在感情上,而是集中在一种危机经历上,在这种经历中,罪恶的威力是所有意图和目的所否定的。 我读了足够多的经典的卫斯理神学,知道对于约翰·卫斯理自己教授的这个主题,有不同的看法. 但从一般的描述方式来看,我认为,这是对老式经典的卫斯理主义的准确表述. 也存在“五旬节派”的旧现象, 重点是圣灵中的洗礼, 通常是在皈依之后, 古老的经典五旬节主义的主要焦点是服务的权力问题. 第三,有现代`魅力运动'。 和经典的五旬节主义一样,它的老师们也用"行动书"中的许多同名段落来支持他们对这个必要危机的理论. 所以他们强调,在多数情况下,尽管现代魅力中存在着不同的学校,但用舌头说话将表明这一点。 如果你有一个圣笑的季节, 然而,其他人说,你没有说出舌头,因为你有一些心理障碍,如果这些障碍可以取出,舌头就在那里。 你只是没说 这里强调的不是净化火的洗礼(如旧经典的卫斯理完美主义),也不是权力的洗礼(如旧经典的五旬节主义),而是更强调充满欢乐的赞美经验的洗礼. 我一直在谈论泛泛而谈,但我认为它们是正确的。 第四,有各种形式的 " 更高的生活 " 教学。 他们的共同点是:你们只是皈依正教,只是与基督联合,只是再生,然后你们遭遇了投降和信仰的危机,你们在危机中“放手,放任真主出征”,而顺从基督永生。 共同的分母是,这是一场没有外在表现出舌头或圣笑或叫喊或跳跃的危机,但最终结果将是新的力量来过上圣生活——强调在圣道上更有效率的能力. 第五,有一种教学既有老的也有现代的支持者。 它侧重于保证,并用圣经中的"封圣"来表述. 一些清教徒——例如托马斯·古德温——教授了这个。 在我们这一天里,有一些传道者非常强烈地相信并反复强调这一点。 该教学的基本关注是,在再生和转生之后,存在着一种危机经历,信仰者通过下列方式进入了保证的质的新层面:

title: Amy Carmichael: Times of Refreshing and Times of Trial
summary: Iain H. Murray’s Amy Carmichael: Beauty for Ashes is a short retelling of the remarkable life of the Irish missionary to India. What follows is Chapter 4 of that title, ‘Hard Days and Golden Years.’ If there was any pattern to Amy Carmichael’s life it was of times of refreshing then of trials, of exhilarating ‘climbing’ […]   The post  Amy Carmichael: Times of Refreshing and Times of Trial  appeared first on  Banner of Truth USA .
summary_zh: 伊恩· H ·穆雷（ Iain H. Murray ）的《艾米·卡迈克尔：灰烬之美》（ Amy Carmichael: Beauty for Ashes ）是对爱尔兰传教士前往印度的非凡生活的简短复述。接下来是该标题的第4章， “艰难的日子和黄金岁月。“如果说艾米·卡迈克尔的生活有任何模式的话，那就是令人耳目一新的时代，然后是考验的时代，令人兴奋的‘攀登’的时代[…]艾米·卡迈克尔的帖子：令人耳目一新的时代和考验的时代首先出现在真理美国的旗帜上。
title_zh: 艾米·卡迈克尔：令人耳目一新的时代和审判的时代
content: Iain H. Murray’s Amy Carmichael: Beauty for Ashes is a short retelling of the remarkable life of the Irish missionary to India. What follows is Chapter 4 of that title, ‘Hard Days and Golden Years.’ If there was any pattern to Amy Carmichael’s life it was of times of refreshing then of trials, of exhilarating ‘climbing’ then of walking in dark ravines. In part her explanation was that demonic activity follows the work of the Holy Spirit. As she quoted from George Bowen, When Christianity assumes an aggressive attitude the first result is a great exhibition of Satanic power. Satan’s power to be manifested must be assaulted. 1 Such an understanding does not come so readily to us who do not live, as she did, within sight of demon possession, or within hearing of tom-tom drums calling devotees to idols. Shortly before Walker 2 had left on his last mission, he had been sitting with Amy and others in deck chairs under the stars. ‘We had been talking’, she later wrote, of work and workers, and of those (to me) most wonderful women, who seemed perfectly self-reliant, needing no strong arm alongside. I remember how, suddenly startled at the bare thought of working alone, in the sense of all the burden of responsibility, I exclaimed that I never could do it. Mr Walker laughed. ‘Well, you don’t have to’, he said. 3 Amy was the weaker when her ‘strong arm’ died at the age of fifty-four. What she owed to Walker’s ‘courageous championship’ of the children’s work, ‘through its first very difficult years, no words can tell, nor can words tell how he is missed’. 4 At times, as she faced her loss, she would need to say to herself, ‘Don’t give up, don’t be afraid: go on.’ Prayer for ‘fortitude’ entered her life. There were unsympathetic neighbours who observed the work at Dohnavur who supposed that Amy would now be more vulnerable. One of these was a lawyer who, soon after Walker’s death, wrote with the demand that current work on the building of a wall around the compoundbe stopped, and that a half-built nursery should be pulled down. They were using ground, he claimed, to which they did not have legal title. ‘He had waited till Mr Walker’s death had left us, as he thought, defenceless, almost desolate, and sure to be easily cowed by threats of court trouble.’ The wall building had been prompted by the passage of a tiger through the compound at night; and the new nursery was necessitated by the growing numbers of children for whom Dohnavur had become home. Amy ignored the letter and heard nothing more of the threat. The Dohnavur family of seventy children and grown-ups in 1906, had doubled itself by this date, and the need of more helpers was pressing. Mrs Catherine Carmichael was never able to return. She died on July 14, 1913. A few weeks earlier a letter from her to Amy began with the words, ‘My own most precious earthly possession’. While Amy did not lament her mother’s death—for no Christian death was to be ‘lamented’—in the days ahead she needed to preach to herself, ‘I must remind myself to live in the joy of those gone, not grovel in the sense of my loss.’ Mrs Carmichael had been a constant supporter and representative for Dohnavur in Britain. She acted as the home secretary to whom gifts could be sent, and helped to make her daughter’s books more widely known. In 1912 those books had been noted by Queen Mary, wife of King George V, who expressed her thanks for them. While Amy was busy in 1913 writing Walker of Tinnevelly , there came the possibility of the loss of her closest female friend and helper, Ponnammal, who had been with her ever since, as a young widow, she had come to new life through Walker’s preaching. She now needed surgery for cancer and Amy went with her to a Salvation Army Hospital at Neyyoor for a period. In their absence from Dohnavur (forty-six miles away), and the absence of Mabel Wade who was on furlough, 70 of the children were ill. The need for more medical facilities at Dohnavur itself was evident. After much s
content_zh: 伊恩·H·默里所著的"艾米·卡迈克尔:爱希斯的美人"(Amy Carmichael: Beautiful for Ashes)是爱尔兰传教士到印度的出众生的短篇回忆. 下面是该标题的第4章: " 艰难的日子和黄金年 " 。 如果Amy Carmichael的生活有任何规律的话, 她的部分解释是,妖魔活动遵循了圣灵的工作. 正如她从乔治·博文所引述的那样,当基督教采取侵略态度时,第一个结果就是撒旦力量的伟大展览. 必须攻击撒旦的力量。 1 对我们来说,这种理解并不像她那样活在恶魔拥有的目光下,或者在听到汤姆·通鼓呼唤献给偶像的人面前。 在行走者2号执行上个任务前不久,他一直和艾米等人坐在星空下的甲板椅上. 她后来写道:‘我们谈过了',内容是工作和工人,以及那些似乎完全自力更生、不需要任何坚强的手臂的妇女。 我记得,我突然对独自工作的赤裸裸的想法感到惊奇,因为我肩负着所有的责任,我感到惊叹,我永远做不到。 华克先生笑了 他说,你不必这么做。 3 Amy在54岁时死亡, 她对沃克的“勇敢的冠军”儿童工作所负的责任是,“在第一个非常困难的岁月里,言语无法分辨,言语也无法分辨他是如何被错过的”。 页:1 有时,当她面临损失时,她需要对自己说: " 不要放弃,不要害怕:继续吧。 " 祈求`宽恕'进入她的生活。 有不同情的邻居在多赫纳武尔观察作品,他们认为艾米现在会更加脆弱. 其中一个是一位律师,他在Walker死后不久写道,他要求停止目前在大院周围建造一堵墙的工作,应当拆除一个半建的托儿所。 他声称,他们使用了他们没有合法所有权的地盘。 他一直等待着沃克先生的死像他所想的那样离开我们,他手无寸铁,几乎是荒凉的,而且肯定很容易被法庭麻烦的威胁吓倒了。 墙上建筑的动因是一只老虎在夜间穿过大院;新的托儿所是因越来越多的儿童成为家而必需的。 艾米无视信件,没有听到更多的威胁. 1906年有70个孩子和成年人的多赫纳武尔家族,到这时已使自己翻了一番,迫切需要更多的帮助. 凯瑟琳·卡迈克尔夫人一直没能回来 她于1913年7月14日去世. 几周前,她给艾米的一封信开头写道,“我拥有自己最珍贵的地产”。 Amy没有为她母亲的死感到悲哀——因为没有一个基督徒的死是`在她需要为自己传道的几天里感到悲伤',`我必须提醒自己生活在那些死去的人的欢快中,而不是在我失去的意义上的忧郁'。 卡迈克尔夫人一直是英国多赫纳武尔的支持者和代表。 她担任家庭秘书,可以向她寄送礼物,并帮助使她女儿的书更广为人知。 1912年,这些书被乔治五世国王的妻子玛丽王后所注意到,玛丽王后对之表示感谢. 在1913年艾米忙于写作"Tinnevelly"的Walker(Walker of Tinnevelly)时,出现了失去她最亲密的女性朋友和助手Ponnammal(Ponnammal)的可能性,她从那时起就一直与她在一起,作为一个年轻的寡妇,她通过Walker的传道而来到了新的生活. 她现在需要手术治疗癌症,艾米和她一起去内约尔的救世军医院住了一段时间. 在他们离开多克纳武尔(相距四十六里外),而当时在放假的马贝尔·韦德(英语:Mabel Wade (film))不在的情况下,70个孩子生病了. Dohnavur本身显然需要更多的医疗设施。 这么多之后

Principle 2: There is no escape from tension and conflict in living the Christian life. I do not say that the Christian life is all tension and all conflict. The kind of teaching I am attempting to expose as fallacious is as follows: At a conference a speaker takes a text out of context to which he attaches or from which he extracts a shibboleth – perhaps the shibboleth of Christ living his life through us, or the saving life of Christ, or the abiding life. Then the preacher, having expounded his theory of the Christian life, gives an appeal like this: ‘Child of God, are you weary of the tension of wrestling with your remaining sin? Are you tired of struggling in prayer? Are you weary of having to battle with impure thoughts and thoughts of envy and pride and jealousy? Are you tired of this incessant conflict?’ And every true Christian sits there with his fangs dripping, saying, ‘Oh God, you know I am tired, I would give anything to have one day, one day in which I did not have to battle with dullness of heart and distraction of mind and the seductions to sin that come from without and from within’. And the speaker then says ‘Ah, if you are tired of the tension, weary of the conflict, if you will but take these steps, then Christ will so live his life through you that it will be a life marked by the negation of tension and conflict. You will be so filled with the Spirit, so taken up in the Spirit, that tension and conflict for all intents and purposes will be a thing of the past as long as you maintain the posture of the abiding life. The moment you feel tension and conflict, it is because you slipped out of that life, back to your old ways.’ Now that is not a caricature, that is spelled out in page after page, book after book. Beware of the writings of Watchman Nee! Beware of some of the writings of such as Norman Grubb and Hannah Whithall Smith. Beware of these writings, because if you take them seriously they could drive you either into a world of unreality or into a world of scepticism. title_zh: 在基督徒的生活中，没有“万能钥匙”
content: The first of six posts containing the substance of teaching given by Albert N. Martin at the 1984 Banner Youth Conference, presenting a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. A question of major importance is ‘How am I to live as a Christian’? It is one thing to be certain on biblical grounds that I have life from Christ, now I must be clear as to how I am to live the life of Christ. My purpose in setting before you some of the major principles of living the Christian life is three-fold: —I wish to sketch in a biblical theology of the Christian life. My purpose is unashamedly one of indoctrination. I wish by God’s help, by Spirit and word, to indoctrinate you in a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. —I wish to inoculate you and to immunize you against the major false views of the Christian life. Some of us desperately wish we had received such an inoculation early in our Christian experience. We spent many years chasing rabbits that we could never catch. We went after experiences and states of mind and heart in the hope that somehow in so doing we would find what it really meant to live as a Christian. —I wish to purge you of any existing misconceptions which you may presently have. It may not be pleasant but it is in your own best interests. We now examine these major principles of the Christian life. Principle 1: There is No One ‘Master Key’ to Living the Christian Life The kind of teaching I am purposing to focus upon in this principle goes something like this: There is a Christian who for many years has found himself in the doldrums. He has had his sails hoisted but he goes nowhere. It seems that he knows little of the wind of the Spirit filling his sails and carrying him anywhere. Or, to change the analogy, he may have his sails hoisted but they seem for ever to be full of holes, and while all around him have hoisted sails and appear to be making progress he seems to be going nowhere. And then one day at a conference or while reading a book or in his own devotions he comes across a passage of Scripture, say John chapter 15, and there he reads in the words of our Lord Jesus that beautiful analogy of the Christian’s relationship to Christ as the relationship of a branch to a vine. This so ignites his own spiritual life that he is almost overnight lifted to an entirely new plateau of spiritual vitality. Either the holes in his sails get mended or it is as though a mighty zephyr from God himself fills his sails, causing them to billow out to the full. He makes more substantial progress in the Christian life in six months than he has made in the previous six years. This man says that the master key to the Christian life is understanding John 15 and if others will only come to understand the concept of Christ’s relationship to his people as the branch and the vine are related they too will come to an entirely new plateau of spiritual vitality and reality in their Christian walk. Another example could be someone who has been struggling with a certain besetting sin which leaves him continually bowed down and crippled with guilt. Here is a young Christian struggling with a certain area of besetting sin, unknown to others, and he is constantly bogged down. His wheels are up to the hub-caps in mud, and no matter how much he changes the gears and pushes down on the accelerator he is spinning his wheels and all he is doing is using up petrol and making a mess. He is in that position for weeks and months perhaps, and then one day at a conference or reading a book or in his own devotions he comes to Romans, chapter 6, and he reads the glorious truth that in union with Jesus Christ all that he was as old man has been put to death, and in union with Jesus Christ the totality of the old life has been buried in Christ’s tomb and he is now a new man in Jesus Christ and he sees that he is called upon to reckon it so, and in the light of that, present himself as alive from the dead. content_zh:
阿尔伯特·N·马丁在1984年班纳青年大会上发表的六篇包含教学内容的文章中的一篇文章,介绍了基督教生活的基本圣经神学. 一个非常重要的问题是:我如何作为一个基督徒活下来? 从圣经上确定我的生命来自基督是一回事,现在我必须明白我如何活基督的生命.
在你们面前,我提出一些关于基督教生活的主要原则,目的有三个方面:——我想在圣经中描绘基督教生活的神学. 我的目的就是毫不羞愧地教化别人 我希望通过上帝的帮助,通过精神和文字,将你灌输到基督教生活的基本圣经神学中去.
我希望为你们接种疫苗,并为你们接种疫苗,反对基督教生活中的重大错误观点。 我们当中有些人非常希望我们早期在基督教经验中得到这样的接种。 我们花了很多年 追赶我们永远抓不到的兔子
我们追寻经验 和精神状态和心境, 希望能找到作为基督徒生活的真正意义。 我希望清除你目前可能存在的任何误解。 这也许不愉快,但符合你的最佳利益。 我们现在审查基督教生活的这些主要原则。
然后有一天,在会议中,或者在读到一本书时,或者在自己的奉献中,他穿过了圣经的一行,如约翰·第15章,他用我们的主耶稣的话来读到,把基督教与基督的关系比作树枝与藤条的关系。
这如此点燃了他自己的精神生活,以至于几乎一夜之间被抬到一个全新的精神活力高地. 要么他的帆上有洞被修补好 要么就好像上帝亲自放出一个强大的快活器 来灌入他的帆上 让他们满地找牙 他在6个月里在基督教生活中取得了比前6年更大的实质性进步.
这个人说,基督教生活的主要关键在于理解约翰·15,如果其他人只了解基督与其人民的关系概念,因为树枝和藤蔓是相连的,他们也会在基督教行走中来到一个精神活力和现实的全新的高地。
另一个例子是,有人一直在为某种困扰他的罪行而挣扎,使他不断屈从并因罪恶而致残。 这里有一个年轻的基督教徒在挣扎着 某些困扰的罪恶领域, 其他人不知道, 他经常陷入困境。
他的车轮在泥地上被吊起,无论他如何改变齿轮并推倒了加速器,他正在旋转他的车轮,他所做的就是用上汽油并制造一团糟。
赫里斯特和他看到,他被召唤去 如此估计, 并据此, 现身 活着 从死亡。 他读了这段话,

summary_zh: 在全部圣经中遇到活着的耶稣。耶稣圣经将耶稣提升为圣经的主要故事，并鼓励你在参与他的故事时忠实地跟随他。另请参阅新的和著名的基督徒书籍十二月免费的东西周五（ Zondervan Reflective ）免费的东西周五（ Zondervan Reflective ）
title_zh: 法律的美丽
content: This week, the blog is sponsored by Zondervan . This article is taken from The Jesus Bible , from Passion Publishing and Zondervan. The Lord called Joshua to be strong and courageous as Joshua replaced Moses as Israel’s leader and led the people into the promised land. This calling was based on his obedience and submission to the Word of God. As the Creator, God knows how life is meant to be lived and the way for people to experience life to the full ( Jn 10:10). The gift of the law was a gracious act of God to instruct his people in his ways. It was never intended to be a moralistic plan to earn God’s favor. Rather, the law was given to those who had already experienced God’s redeeming grace. In the law, God provided instructions for how his children can love him and other people. This law is not a collection of arbitrary dictates from a malevolent deity, but instead it is the wisdom of God distilled in human language. It is a path to joy and life — the way people were meant to live. The Bible continually portrays the law of God in this fashion. For example, in the longest psalm in the Bible, Psalm 119, the author says that he loves, treasures, delights in and longs for the law. It is a source of hope, peace, joy and direction. In Psalm 19, the psalmist says the law refreshes the soul, makes wise the simple, gives joy to the heart and gives light to the eyes (Ps 19:7 – 8). The law is a beautiful gift from a gracious God. Jesus testified to the lasting value of the law when he said that he did not come to abolish the law (Mt 5:17). Instead, Jesus amplified the law, explaining the transformation that should result as a proper response to his work. In his masterful Sermon on the Mount in Matthew 5 through 7, Jesus called people to a far greater standard of obedience than mere conformity to external regulations. Instead of simply condemning murder, Jesus unmasked the anger that fueled this act. Adultery is not the prime culprit, but lust rooted in the human heart is the real problem. Jesus methodically outlined the heart-level change that the law relied upon. Rather than rendering the law obsolete, Jesus showed that the law continued to provide an authoritative standard and guidance for God’s people. Now, because of the finished work of Christ, believers have hope that the price for their disobedience of the law has been paid and that they have God’s Spirit dwelling within them, providing them the power to live the life God intends. content_zh:
博客由Zondervan赞助, 这篇文章取自"耶稣圣经","激情出版"和"赞德凡". 耶和华召约书亚为强而勇敢,因为约书亚取代了摩西成为以色列领导人并带领人民进入所应许之地. 这个召唤是基于他的服从和顺从上帝之道.

作为造物主,上帝知道生命的本意,知道人们如何体验到生命的完全(Jn 10:10). 法律的天赋是上帝的恩惠行为,以指示他的人民如何行事. 这从来就没有打算成为赢得上帝恩惠的道德计划。 相反,法律是给予那些已经经历过上帝赎回恩惠的人的。

在法律中,上帝为他的孩子如何能爱他和其他人提供了指示. 这部法则并不是从邪恶的神灵中任意地指令的集合,而是用人类语言来提炼出上帝的智慧. 这是通往快乐和生活的道路——人们本该生活的方式。 圣经以这种方式不断地描绘出上帝的法则.

耶稣作证了法律的持久价值,他说他不是来废除法律的(Mt 5:17). 相反地,耶稣放大了律法,解释了应该因适当回应他的工作而导致的转变. 在他精通马太福音5号到7号的"山上赛蒙"中,耶稣把人们称为服从的标准远远高于单纯遵守外规.

耶稣不是简单地谴责谋杀,而是揭发了激起这一行为的愤怒. 通奸不是罪魁祸首,但植根于人心的欲望才是真正的问题. 耶稣有条不紊地概述了法律所依赖的心脏层面的变化. 耶稣没有使法律过时,而是表明法律继续为上帝的人民提供权威的标准和指导.

现在,由于基督的完成,信徒们希望他们违抗法律的代价已经付出,他们心中有上帝的精神,给他们以神想要的生活的力量。 另见12月自由聚会(Zondervan反省会)12月自由聚会(Zondervan反省会)自由聚会(Zondervan反省会)的基督教新书。
