title: Tips for Resolving Conflict in Marriage
summary: Conflict in marriage is inevitable, but resolving it well is a skill. Here are 6 practical tips that range from examining your own sin first to a 10 p.m. rule. See Also Danger Signs of an Unhealthy Dating Relationship The Beginner’s Guide to Conflict Resolution Free Stuff Fridays
summary_zh: 婚姻中的冲突是不可避免的，但妥善解决冲突是一项技能。这里有6个实用技巧，从先检查你自己的罪到晚上10点的规则。另请参阅不健康约会关系的危险迹象周五解决冲突的初学者指南免费内容
title_zh: 解决婚姻冲突的技巧
content: It is inevitable that lives lived in deep intimacy will generate conflict. We wish this weren’t so, but sadly, it is. Therefore, wise couples learn to anticipate conflict and learn to resolve it well. I was recently asked to provide some thoughts on conflict resolution, and thought I’d share what I came up with. Yet as I have sat with couples and tried to help them work through various issues, it has shocked me to find how many have never learned to settle conflict well. Many set habits and patterns in their early years that become hard to break or overcome. I have met with couples who have only ever tried to resolve conflict by raising their voices, and with others who have only ever tried to resolve it by going silent. I have met with some who have only ever relied on text messaging instead of speaking face to face, and with others who have long since given up and don’t even bother trying anymore. Much of this stems from their first years and their failure to get well grounded in conflict resolution. To that end, here are a few suggestions on resolving conflict well. First, borrowing from Robert Murray M’Cheyne, follow this pattern: For every one look at your spouse’s sin, take ten at your own. It’s easy enough to become an expert in the way your spouse sins against you, but it’s far more important to become an expert in the ways you sin against your spouse. It concerns me when I see someone who seems adamantly committed to his spouse’s holiness but seemingly not very interested in his own. Your first calling before the Lord is to deal with your own sin so you can put it to death and come alive to righteousness. Second, invite your spouse to identify your sin. Because of the sheer quantity of the time and intimacy you share, you will inevitably sin against your spouse more than you will sin against anyone else. Not only that, but married life lets your spouse see the kinds of sins that no one else will. Only he or she sees how you sin in the bedroom, for example, or when you’re running late and nobody else is around. What’s more, your spouse sees deeper into your soul than anyone else and, therefore, knows more about you. In a healthy marriage, if you are truly committed to holiness, it only makes sense that you will ask your spouse to speak into your life. It is wise to provide a safe setting to do this where you won’t be a baby or a bully, and won’t sulk or lash out. Set aside some time, tell your spouse that you’d like to hear what sins you are committing, then listen patiently and calmly, without showing anger or being defensive. Having done that, go away, think about it, pray about it, and don’t respond until a day later. This could be a great means of grace in your life. Third, identify times when you won’t try to resolve conflict. Aileen and I, for example, have a long-established 10 o’clock rule, which means we won’t try to fix anything after 10 p.m. We are well aware that Ephesians 4:26 says, “Do not let the sun go down on your anger,” but we have also learned that some issues simply cannot be neatly resolved by bedtime. (Married folk will know that some of the most common conflicts tend to happen between the time you get into bed together and the time you actually fall asleep.) The later the day gets, the more we tend to operate out of emotion rather than reason. And some things seem way worse in the evening when we’re tired than in the morning when we’re fresh. So if we haven’t worked it out by 10, we will call a halt, kiss one another, pray with one another, say something like “I love you and we are going to be all right,” and then go to sleep. Then we can try to work it out at a better time, when we are in a better frame of mind. And honestly, in the light of day, we often realize the situation wasn’t nearly as dire as we thought and that it can be covered by love (1 Peter 4:8). Fourth, invite others in when necessary. Sometimes the most helpful thing you can do in a time of conflict is invite some friends or so

生活在深深的亲密中的生活必然会引发冲突。 但可悲的是, 因此,明智的夫妇学会预测冲突并学会妥善解决冲突。 最近有人要求我提出一些解决冲突的想法,

然而,当我与夫妇们坐在一起,努力帮助他们解决各种问题时,我发现有多少人从未学会妥善解决冲突,这让我感到震惊。 许多人在早年就设定了难以打破或克服的习惯和模式.

我见过夫妇们,他们只试图通过提高声音来解决冲突,而其他人则只试图通过沉默来解决冲突。 我会见了一些只依靠短信而不是面对面发言的人,

其主要原因是他们最初的岁月和未能在解决冲突中扎根。 为此,我们提出一些关于妥善解决冲突的建议。 首先,向罗伯特·默里·姆谢恩借款,遵循这一模式: 每看一看配偶的罪孽,就自己拿十。

成为你配偶对你的罪过的专家是很容易的, 当我看到有人 似乎坚定致力于他的配偶的圣洁,

你第一次在主面前召唤是 处理你自己的罪过 这样你就可以把它死 并活到正义。 其次,请您的配偶 识别你的罪恶。 由于你所分享的时间和亲密关系,你不可避免地会对你的配偶犯下比对其他人犯下更严重的罪行。

不仅如此 婚姻生活让你的配偶看到 别人不会犯的罪 只有他或她看到你在卧室的罪过, 更何况,你的配偶比任何人都更深刻地看待你的灵魂,从而更了解你。

在一个健康的婚姻中,如果你真正致力于圣洁,那么你要求你的配偶在你的生活中说话就只有道理了. 最好提供安全的环境,

也不要发怒或防卫。 并且直到一天后才回应。 这可能是你生命中伟大的恩典手段. 第三,确定你何时不会试图解决冲突。

例如艾琳和我早就有十点的规则, 我们清楚地知道,以弗所4:26说,“不要让太阳落在你的愤怒上,”但我们也了解到,有些问题根本不能通过睡觉来彻底解决。

(结婚后人们会知道,一些最常见的冲突往往发生在你们上床睡觉的时间与实际入睡的时间之间. 一天越晚,我们就越倾向于出于情感而不是理性而行动. 有些事情在晚上比早上更糟糕,

因此,如果我们还没有在10点之前解决,我们将叫停,互相亲吻,相互祈祷,说出类似“我爱你,我们会没事的”的话,然后睡觉。 然后,我们可以尝试在更好的时间,当我们处于一个更好的思维框架时,解决它。

老实说,在白天,我们常常意识到,情况没有我们想象的那么糟糕,而且可以被爱所覆盖(1:彼得:8). 第四,在必要时邀请其他人参加。 有时候,在冲突时期,你能做的最有帮助的事 就是邀请一些朋友

content: Good morning. Grace and peace to you. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include a lot of great books to start a new month. If all goes according to schedule, the list will include works on apologetics, singing, Karl Marx and D.L. Moody, missionaries who were recently martyred in Haiti, and much more. Enjoy the bounty! Logos users will want to take a look at this month’s free and nearly-free books. You’ll also find some early Black Friday deals that include some commentaries at up to 80% off. It’s also worth browsing the monthly sales . Recommended Reading A Candy Shop Owner, a Customs Officer, and a Beloved Family. I like this illustration. “Anyone traveling to another country knows that customs officers don’t mess around. They might grill you about what you are bringing into the country, who you are visiting, where you are going, and what your intentions are in the country. I’ve been asked all of those questions. I’ve never felt warmly welcomed by a customs officer. Currently our daughter lives in Southern California. We look forward to those sweet times she can come home. When she arrives home for Christmas, will we grill her? ‘What are the purposes of your stay at our home?’ ‘Who do you plan to visit?’ ‘What are you bringing into our home?’ Certainly not! We will throw the door open, wrap her in our arms, and welcome her in. She is family!” Your Definition of Blessing Is Too Small. “How do we square the Bible’s unblushing promises of blessing for the faithful with its theology of suffering? Put another way, how does Psalm 128 fit with a passage like Psalm 88, where the faithful one seems utterly abandoned to the darkness? One way to answer this question succinctly is to realize that the Bible, first, expands the meaning of blessing in this life, and second, eternalizes it.” These are helpful categories when we consider a difficult topic. 5 Ways Retirees Can Serve the Church. I am not yet a retiree, but when the time comes, this article lists some of the ways I will want to serve my church. “‘Retirement at last! Now I can sleep as late as I want to. Now I get to do nothing all day.’ Such is a popular description of how retirement looks to many people. I know some who would even add, ‘Now I get to play golf every day.’ Obviously, this does not reflect the Christian perspective of someone who understands that his chief end is ‘to glorify God and enjoy Him forever.’ This is not to say that sleeping later and playing golf are anti-Christian. However, there are some significant ways that retirees can still serve the church.” You Can See Everything: On Masks, Performing, and Holiness. You have probably heard at least something about the new film You Can See Everything . Joseph Whitenton explains that the movie provokes the question of whether you can ever truly know someone, then says “I can’t help but feel a deep sense of dread. Is this really all we can say about our relationships to one another? That it might be impossible to really know someone? To even know ourselves? Are our lives just a string of performances? I can’t help but think about how a social media centered age might further contribute to this feeling of constantly performing, as Bo Burnham, another comedian/prophet has observed.” The Straightest Path to Happiness. Randy Alcorn: “In God’s world, happiness is found in discovering what’s truly in our self-interest: loving God and our neighbor. This profound, paradigm-shifting concept, understood correctly, makes the false dichotomy obvious in the question, ‘Should I serve others, or should I act in my own best interests?'” The Danger of ‘No Enemies to the Right’. Writing for The Daily Wire , Andrew Walker tells about the danger of the slogan “no enemies to the right.” “There remains asymmetrical warfare in the Left’s continued aggression toward conservatives. Biblical fidelity also requires impartial judgment — even when it goes against ‘our side.’ Brothers and sisters on the Right need to hear that. When conservati

content: In my weekly Works & Wonders column, I combine a brief devotional with other interesting and uplifting bits and pieces I gleaned throughout the week. I hope you enjoy this week’s collection! It includes: When God Acts in Power Wikipop Weather Photographer of the Year Bring on the Dawn Big Words Men Sing 1. When God Acts in Power No element of God’s character can be separated from any other. You or I may use the power available to us recklessly, imperfectly, or sinfully—we may act forcefully yet unwisely, or authoritatively yet with evil motives and immoral outcomes. We may act impulsively, on the basis of false information, or in ways that foster prejudice or injustice. In this way, power can be used to bring about great good or great harm. But God never acts in such a way that he diminishes any part of his character. Hence, when God acts in power, he invariably exercises that power in ways that are wise, holy, just, good, and true. I think Jen Wilkin says this well: “The truth of God’s limitless power would be absolutely terrifying were it not paired with the truth of His limitless goodness.” God’s power separated from his other attributes would mean there is nothing that would withhold or restrain him. Yet God’s power paired with his other attributes is tremendously comforting, for we know he will use his power only in ways that are ultimately for our good and his glory. 2. Wikipop Wikipop is a microsite that offers the answer to just one question: What Wikipedia page was everyone looking at yesterday? You probably won’t be shocked to know that on Saturday, when I finalized this article, it told me that everyone had been looking for Patrick Stewart, who died a few days prior. (Note: I add this site with a bit of trepidation because I can’t predict what article will be featured on the day you click the link, so hopefully it’s nothing bad!) 3. Weather Photographer of the Year I know I keep sharing photography contests, but as I said last week, this is the time of year when many of them announce the winners. But this one is different from others I have shared since it features weather. In the Weather Photographer of the Year shortlist, you’ll find exactly what you’d expect—a stunning collection of photos of the weather. 4. Bring on the Dawn I know many people who have appreciated Douglas McKelvey’s Every Moment Holy books, which offer liturgies and prayers for all of life’s moments. Anchor Hymns recently collaborated with McKelvey on an album titled Bring on the Dawn that was inspired by his books. I’m pretty sure that if you appreciate the books, you’ll also like the music. 5. Big Words Sometimes the best apps are the simplest—the ones that do just one thing, but do it well. That’s the case with Big Words . What does it do? It lets you use your phone (or iPad or other screen) to display big words. “Make a full-screen sign, timer or message from a link. Hold up your phone at arrivals, put a countdown on the TV, or show the Wi-Fi password at the front desk. No account, no app, nothing stored on a server. The link is the whole display, so you can share it or bookmark it.” There is nothing to download, so you can just go ahead and bookmark it to use when the need arises. 6. Men Sing I love this delightfully countercultural “Men Sing” trend that’s happening among Dutch Reformed churches, and would love to see it spread. What is it? It’s just men getting together to sing hymns. I had hoped to attend the recent one in Hamilton, but was on the road at the time. Hopefully I can make it to the next one. You can find videos from churches in Hamilton , Grand Rapids , and Chilliwack . I assume it’s happening in other places where there are lots of Dutch Reformed churches. Well done, Dutch guys! 你或我可能会莽撞地、不完美地、或罪恶地使用我们所拥有的权力——我们可能会以邪恶的动机和不道德的结果,采取强而不明智或权威的行动。 我们可能根据虚假信息或以助长偏见或不公正的方式采取冲动行动。 这样,权力可以用来带来巨大的好坏.
但上帝从不以这样的方式行事,以致于削弱他性格的任何部分. 因此,当上帝行使权力时,他总是以明智、神圣、公正、善良和真实的方式行使这种权力。
我认为Jen Wilkin说得好 : “ 如果上帝无限力量的真理不与他无限善良的真理相配的话,那将是绝对可怕的。 ” 神的力量与他的其他属性相分离,将意味着没有任何东西可以扣留或约束他.
然而,上帝的力量与他的其他属性相配,是极为安慰的,因为我们知道,他只会以最终有利于我们及其光荣的方式使用他的力量。 2. Wikipop Wikipop是一个微站点,只回答一个问题:昨天大家看的维基百科页面是什么?

content: Good morning. My gratitude goes to Ligonier Ministries for sponsoring the blog this week to ensure you know about the new Grow app . It’s a free download and offers a lot of great content. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include a variety of deals spanning a bunch of different eras and genres. Recommended Reading Jessica Lee writes about the growing no contact movement in which people sever their relationships with people they find toxic or problematic. I think of the young women I mentor who are flooded with reels, encouraging them that the best way to deal with the strained relationship with their mom is to put up higher boundaries that limit contact, or to cut off contact altogether. Even if they don’t take these drastic measures, they cannot help being influenced by the ideas, and neither can we. We are steeped in a therapy culture that talks a lot more about self-care than self-sacrifice, and we would be naive if we didn’t acknowledge the formative influence it has on us. And so, when relationships (whether with a parent, sibling, or friend) get hard, as they inevitably will, our first impulse is often toward self-preservation (putting up higher boundaries) and not self-sacrificial presence and faithfulness. Read: Going No Contact?: Ruth and Faithful Presence. Madeline Livingston has been going through a time of deep sorrow, and from that perspective writes a meditation about grief and glory. In my grief, I can turn to a Savior who has known human frailty and deep suffering, a Savior who in his most desperate moment prayed, “Let this cup pass from me. Yet not as I will, but as you will” ( Matthew 26:39 ). I can trust in the goodness and provision of a Father who did spare his own Son, but gave him up to rescue us and make us his own ( Romans 8:32 ). I can rest in the compassion of a Maker who collects all my tears in his bottle ( Psalm 56:8 ), a Good Shepherd who carries me safely through the lowest valley and restores my soul ( Psalm 23 ). As Sorrow and Suffering take me by the hand, they invite me to run to the solid ground of God’s promises made yes and amen through Christ. They urge me on to seek solace in the only place it can truly be found, in a arms of a Father who is my “refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble” ( Psalm 46:1 ). Read: When Sorrow & Suffering Take You by the Hand. Sarah Eekhoff Zylstra did a lot of interviews to try to arrive at some best practices for churches that are evangelistically effective. Her article offers a lot of food for thought. Thirty years ago, evangelical churches leaned on programs like Evangelism Explosion or Continuous Witness Training to deliver evangelistic focus and training, church leader Thom Rainer said. Those structured initiatives fit well in a culture that was more Christian and more institutionalized—it took an average of 20 church members to reach one person for Christ per year. Today, it takes 50, Rainer said. “Evangelism efficacy, evangelism effectiveness, has definitely diminished.” That trend is likely to continue. As social media and AI fill our time and increase our social anxiety, even relational evangelism is growing more difficult. Read: Best Practices from Evangelistically Effective Churches. Like Darryl Dash, I’ve been hearing and reading a lot of doom and gloom lately, much of it related to the rise of AI. But also like Darryl, I don’t feel particularly alarmed. I read quite a few predictions of doom over the weekend, including some from self-professed tech optimists. Supposedly, some infrastructure in the United States is under attack. The idea is that AI is becoming too powerful and will overwhelm whatever safeguards we have in place to protect things like our water systems and electricity. The proposed solution is to prepare for the disaster by buying generators, solar panels for generators, and stockpiling water and other basic supplies. content_zh: 早上好,你好吗? 感谢利戈尼耶各部赞助本周的博客, 这是免费的下载, 今天的销售和交易包括一系列跨越不同时代和流派的交易。 建议阅读 Jessica Lee写道,人们与他们发现有毒或有问题的人们断绝关系,但这种接触运动却在不断增加。 我想到那些我辅导的年轻女性,她们被卷轴淹没,鼓励她们,处理与母亲的紧张关系的最佳方式是设置更高的界限限制接触,或者完全切断接触. 即使他们不采取这些激烈的措施,他们也受不了这些想法的影响,我们也不能这样做。 我们身处一种治疗文化中,谈论自我护理比自我牺牲要多得多,如果我们不承认它对我们的形成影响,我们就会天真。 因此,当关系(无论是与父母、兄弟还是朋友的关系)变得困难时,我们的第一个冲动是往往朝向自我保护(提出更高的界限),而不是自我神圣的存在和忠诚。 读:去去不接触? 鲁斯和忠实的存在。 马德琳·利文斯通经历了一段深深的悲痛时期,从这个角度看,他写了一篇关于悲痛和荣耀的冥想. 在我悲痛中,我可以求助于一个知道人类脆弱和深重苦难的救世主,一个在他最绝望的时刻祈祷的救世主,“让这个杯子从我身边流过。 然而,不是我愿意,而是你愿意”(Matthew 26:39.). 我可以相信一个父亲的善良和供养,他确实饶了自己的儿子,但为了拯救我们而放弃了他,使我们成为自己的父亲(罗马8:32. 我可以安心地忍受一个造物主的怜悯,他把所有的眼泪都收在他的瓶中(诗篇56:8),一个好牧人,他把我安全地带入最底层的山谷并恢复我的灵魂(诗篇23. 当悲伤和受苦将我牵上手时,他们邀请我跑到上帝通过基督许下的承诺的坚实地步。 他们敦促我在一个真正能找到的地方寻求安慰,在一个父亲的怀抱中,他是我的“抵抗和力量,在困难中非常现成的帮助”(第46:1段)。 读取:"悲伤"和"受苦受难"由"手取""你"时. Sarah Eekhoff Zylstra做了很多访谈,试图为福音派有效的教堂达成一些最佳做法. 她的文章为思考提供了很多食物. 教会领袖汤姆·赖纳(Thom Rainer)说, 这些结构化的倡议非常适合一种更加基督教化和更加制度化的文化——平均每年需要20名教会成员为基督而接触一个人。 今天,它需要50,雷纳说。 “福音会的功效,福音会的功效,肯定已经下降。” 这一趋势很可能继续下去。 由于社交媒体和AI填补了我们的时间并增加了我们的社会焦虑,甚至连关系福音派也越来越困难. 读取:Evangelistic 有效教会的最佳做法。 与达里尔·达什(Darryl Dash)一样, 我最近也听到并阅读了许多末日与忧郁, 但与达里尔一样, 我读到很多关于周末末日的预言, 包括一些自以为是的技术乐观主义者的预言。 假设美国的一些基础设施受到攻击。 这个想法是AI正在变得太强大,并且会压倒我们现有的保护诸如我们的供水系统和电力之类的东西的保障措施. 拟议的解决办法是通过购买发电机、发电机太阳能电池板以及储存水和其他基本用品来为灾难做好准备。 然而,作者们承认,我们无法真正保护自己,使其免受歧视。

content: October was a strong month for new Christian books. I tried to keep you in the loop week by week, but I also wanted to provide a roundup for the end of the month. Of all the books that came our way in October, here are the ones that most stood out to me, arranged in what I think is a nice new format. As always, I’ve included the publisher’s editorial description for each. Book of the Month Crossway · Hardcover · 736 pages The Westminster Confession of Faith: A Comprehensive Commentary on Its History, Theology, and Application Edited by J. V. Fesko, John R. Muether, and D. Blair Smith If I had to put one book on the top of the stack this month, it would probably be this commentary on the Westminster Confession of Faith—and I say that as a Baptist who respects, but does not hold to, the WCF. The contributors include Sinclair Ferguson, Chad Van Dixhoorn, and Kevin DeYoung. This is a reference work that pastors and serious readers will want to add to their libraries. “This essential collection of essays presents an accessible guide to the Westminster Confession of Faith for 21st-century readers. Each chapter is devoted to a section of the historic document, carefully studying its context, its significance to the faith, and its application, as well as any controversies.” Buy it at Amazon · Westminster Books For Your Own Soul Books for any thoughtful Christian reader. Crossway · Hardcover · 264 pages Finally Home: The Christian Hope of Heaven Dane Ortlund In this book, Dane Ortlund ( Gentle and Lowly ) turns his attention to heaven. He draws on Scripture, of course, and also on writers like Thomas Goodwin, Jonathan Edwards, and C. S. Lewis. “If we are not in Christ, this life is the best we will ever experience. If we are in Christ, this life is the worst we will ever experience. … In Finally Home , Dane Ortlund plunges into the word of God and the wisdom of the saints to help us rightly think about heaven, and to draw strength from our coming future more deeply than we ever have before.” Buy it at Amazon · Westminster Books IVP · Paperback · 192 pages Everyday Discipleship: How Faith Shapes the Most Practical Areas of Life Jeremy Treat This is a practical book that teaches how following Jesus extends into every part of life, including those that are very ordinary, like meals, work, rest, and technology. It includes a discussion guide for groups. “Pastor Jeremy Treat understands this disconnect. In Everyday Discipleship , he dismantles the harmful sacred-secular divide that leaves many Christians feeling spiritually compartmentalized, uncertain about how faith applies to ordinary life, and unable to fully enjoy Christ in the entirety of our lives.” Buy it at Amazon Banner of Truth · Clothbound · 248 pages God Is Our Refuge and Strength: 150 Devotionals Through the Psalms William Boekestein & Rob Ventura Every Banner of Truth release is noteworthy, isn’t it? This one offers a short devotional reading to accompany each of the 150 psalms. “You need the Psalms. The Psalms are the Bible’s devotional heart. … Through brief, practical expositions of all 150 psalms, this volume proclaims, explains, and applies each one in light of the New Testament and the finished work of Jesus Christ the Lord.” Buy it at Amazon · Westminster Books Counseling & Care Resources to care for Christians. One Measure Ministries · Redemption Press · Paperback workbooks SoulCare Groups™ Workbooks: Anxiety, Grief, and Sexual Integrity Gary & Linda Baer I am excited about the SoulCare Groups™ workbooks, which came out this month. Each is a twelve-week group study meant to be used alongside a few trusted biblical counseling books. The first three volumes cover anxiety, grief, and sexual integrity. “SoulCare Groups™, a biblical counseling workbook series from One Measure Ministries, equips churches to offer groups-based care through structured twelve-week topical studies.” Buy them at Amazon: Anxiety · Grief · Sexual Integrity For the Church and Its History Books to u
content_zh: 十月是基督教新书的强月. 我试图让你每周循环, 但我也想提供 一个回合的月底。 在10月我们走过来的所有书中, 这里有那些最突出的, 以我认为一种很好的新格式排列。 我总是把出版商的编辑描述都包括进去。 " 月之十字路口"一书 硬封面 736页 " 威斯敏斯特信仰的忏悔:对其历史、神学和应用的综合评论 " 由J. V. Fesko、John R. Muether和D. Blair Smith编辑 如果这个月我不得不把一本书放在堆起的顶上,那很可能就是关于威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔书的评论——我说,作为一个尊重但不坚持周转基金的浸信会信徒。 撰稿人包括辛克莱·弗格森(Sinclair Ferguson),乍得·范迪克斯霍恩(Chad Van Dixhoorn)和凯文·德杨(Kevin DeYoung). 这是牧师和认真的读者想要加入他们的图书馆的参考作品. “这一系列重要的散文为21世纪的读者提供了一本《威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔指南》。 每一章都专门讨论历史文件的一节,仔细研究其背景、其对信仰的意义、其适用以及任何争议。” 在亚马逊购买, Crossway-Hardcover-264页 最后回家:天堂的基督教希望-丹麦奥特伦德 在这本书中,达尼·奥特伦德(英语:Dane Ortlund (Gentle and Lowly))将注意力转向了天堂. 他当然借鉴了"圣经",同时也借鉴了托马斯·古德温,乔纳森·爱德华兹和C·S·刘易斯等作家. “如果我们不是在基督中,这种生活是我们所经历的最好生活。 如果我们在基督, 这样的生活是我们所经历的最糟糕的。 . . . . . . . 最后,Dane Ortlund在“家园”中投入了上帝的言行和圣徒的智慧,帮助我们正确思考天堂,并比以往更深刻地汲取我们未来的力量。” 在亚马逊购买它 威斯敏斯特书 IVP 页面存档备份,存于互联网档案馆 192页 每日论文:信仰如何塑造最实用的生活领域 Jeremy对待 这是一本实用的书,教人们如何追随耶稣,如何延伸至生活的每一部分,包括那些非常平凡的,比如吃饭,工作,休息,以及技术等. 它包括为各团体编写的讨论指南。 “牧师Jeremy Treat理解这种脱节。 在日常的分歧中,他拆除了有害的神圣-世俗鸿沟,这些鸿沟使许多基督徒感到精神上的分化,对信仰如何适用于平凡的生活并不确定,无法在我们的一生中充分享有基督。” 248页《上帝是我们的庇护与力量》:150个通过诗人威廉·博克斯坦(William Boekestein)和罗布·文图拉(Rob Ventura)发行的《真理之行》值得注意, 这张是随150个诗歌的每个诗篇的简短的奉献读物。 “你需要诗歌。 圣诗是圣经的奉献之心。 . . . . . . . 通过对所有150个诗作的简短、实用的阐述,本卷根据《新约》和耶穌基督所完成的工作,宣布、解释和适用每个诗句。” 在Amazon 公司购买, 我对本月推出的“SoulCare Groups”工作手册感到兴奋。 每项研究都是为期12周的团体研究,目的是与一些值得信赖的圣经辅导书籍一起使用。 前三卷收录了焦虑,悲伤和性完整性. “SoulCare GroupsTM是《一个计量部》的一本圣经咨询工作手册系列,它使教会有能力通过结构化的12周专题研究提供基于群体的护理。” 在亚马逊购买:焦虑 · 悲伤 · 教会及其历史书籍的性正直

content: Good morning. I am making my way home from Colorado today after a productive series of meetings and video shoots. I’ll look forward to a more normal week next week! In the meantime, be sure to check in tomorrow for Weekend A La Carte and on Sunday for a favorite feature, Works & Wonders. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include lots of interesting books like an exposition of the London Baptist Confession, some brief biographies of Christians you should know, and Thaddeus Williams’s book on reverence. Some of my books are 50% off at ChurchSource in their print editions: Visual Theology , A Visual Theology Guide to the Bible , and Pilgrim Prayers . Recommended Reading Time Flies—and Death Comes Speedily. The older you get, the more you come to understand that time flies and death comes speedily. “As teenagers, my friends and I were awash with youthful pride, poking fun at weighty things we knew little about—completely ignorant that our life here below is ‘a mist that appears for a little time and then vanishes.’ The dew was still afresh upon our heads; the road of life unfurling in a great spool before our feet, disappearing into the far-off horizon. We could quote you verses here and there from the Scriptures, all the while being completely unversed in this point: “It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting, for this is the end of all mankind, and the living will lay it to heart.” In our minds, we could afford to mock death because we were, at the time, so far removed from it.” Was Piper Unprepared? A little while ago, John Piper indicated that he may have been unprepared for pastoral ministry when he began it. In this episode of Ask Pastor John , he is asked to explain what he meant by that. Take Your Faith Deeper with Ligonier’s Grow App. During a time of spiritual decline, God used the Protestant Reformation to bring renewal to His church through the recovery of the biblical gospel. This Reformation Day, explore the truths that fueled renewed devotion to God and His Word in the Grow app from Ligonier. Discover hundreds of Reformation-themed articles, video teaching series, and conference messages to help strengthen your faith and deepen your walk with Christ. Download the Grow app today. (Sponsored) The Engineering Behind Every Heartbeat. This is a celebration of the engineering of the human heart. “The human heart does not beat like a perfect clock. The time between beats changes as the body breathes, moves, rests, and reacts to the world around it. New research shows that these changes are part of a feedback system linking the heart, brain, and nerves. The heart keeps a steady rhythm while remaining flexible when needed, much like a well-built control system.” When You Trick-or-Treat, Nod to Martin Luther. Daniel Hyde writes in a local paper to explain to its readers the Protestant contribution to Halloween. “So, by all means, dress up and hand out the candy. When the doorbell rings, remember: The principle that no authority may command conscience protects the civil liberty of the religious and nonreligious alike.” God’s Left Hand. Bryce Waller: “The most difficult part about politics is what happens after the elections. In Romans 13:1, God calls us to be subject to these governing authorities—to obey the laws they pass, to show them honor and respect, to give them our hard-earned money by paying taxes. Voting is one thing, but submitting my life to a politician, showing respect to that guy , paying taxes to those people —even the people I didn’t choose? That’s not so easy.” These are good things to work out before an election since it will shape your response, whether you are happy with the results or dismayed. 17 Exhortations For Christian Citizens. On a somewhat related note, here are 17 exhortations for Christian citizens. “Bad government and national decline grieve those who love their country and bring a kind of chaos—a hard providence for Christian citizens. Yet even worse form
content_zh: 早上好,你好吗? 今天我从科罗拉多州回家的路 经过一系列富有成效的会议和录像拍摄。 我期待下周能更正常一点! 同时,请务必在明天的周末A La Carte 和星期日的首选节目Works & Wonders 登入。 今天的销售与交易交易包括许多有趣的书籍,如伦敦浸信会忏悔书的展出、一些你应该知道的基督教徒的简略传记以及Thaddeus Williams的"敬重"一书。 我的一些书在Church Source的印刷版中, 被推荐阅读"时空飞翔"——死亡会迅速来袭. 越老越了解时间飞逝 " 少年时,我的朋友和我充满了青春的自豪感,对我们所知甚少的重量级事物玩得很开心——完全不知道我们下面的生活是`一段短暂出现的雾,然后消失'。 露水仍然浮出水面;生命之道在我们脚前的大水池中被冲出,消失在遥远的地平线上。 我们可以在此地和那部经典中引用你们的迹象,当时,他们对于这部经典是毫无知识的。你们去哀号之所胜过去宴会之所胜过去宴会之所胜;这是全人类的结局,是活人的心事。 在我们心目中,我们可以以死亡为笑柄,因为我们当时远离死亡。” Piper没有准备好吗? 不久之前,约翰·皮珀表示他开始牧业时可能还没有准备好. 在"问约翰牧师"这集里 他被要求解释他的意思 在精神衰落的时期,上帝利用了新教的改造,通过恢复圣经福音给他的教堂带来复兴。 在利戈尼耶的"成长的应用"中,探索那些促使人们重新忠于上帝和他的话的真理。 发掘出上百篇以改革为主题的文章,视频教学系列,以及会话等信息来帮助增强你的信仰并深化与基督的行走. 今天下载 Grow 应用程序 。 (赞助)"每个心跳"背后的工程. 这是对人类心脏工程的庆祝. “人的心不像一个完美的钟。 随着身体的呼吸、移动、休息和对周围世界的反应,间隔时间会改变。 新的研究表明这些变化是连接心脏,大脑和神经的反馈系统的一部分. 心脏保持平稳的节奏,同时在必要时保持灵活,就像一个完善的控制系统。” 当Trick -or -Treat, 点头马丁路德。 丹尼尔·海德在当地的一篇文章中向读者解释新教对万圣节的贡献. “所以,无论如何,要穿好衣服,把糖果递出去。 当门铃响起,记住: 任何当局不得控制良心的原则保护宗教和非宗教的公民自由。” 上帝的"左手"。 布莱斯·沃勒(Bryce Waller):"政治方面最困难的部分是选举之后发生的事情. 在罗马13:1中,上帝号召我们服从这些执政当局——服从他们通过的法律,向他们表示荣誉和尊重,通过交税来给他们我们辛苦得到的钱. 投票是一回事,但把我的生命交给一位政治家, 对他表示尊敬, 这并非易事。 这些是选举前要解决的好事情,因为它将决定你的反应,无论你对结果满意还是沮丧。 17 对基督教公民的劝告。 与此相关的是,对基督教公民提出了17条劝告。 “坏政府和民族衰落使那些热爱祖国并带来某种混乱的人感到悲痛——这是基督教公民的难能可贵。 更糟糕的形态

content: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include books about the Old Testament, Proverbs, faithful presence, the life and influence of Tim Keller, and a whole lot more. Westminster Books is continuing their Reformation sale by offering discounts on ESV Bibles as well as the tremendous new 500th anniversary edition of Tyndale’s New Testament. Recommended Reading How the Mainstream Recruits for the Manosphere. Aaron Renn explains how “asymmetric blame, hectoring lectures, and selectively revived norms are driving young men to the influencers the mainstream condemns.” How Mental Illness Became an Identity. Myles Werntz has an interesting review of a new book by Fredrik deBoer that explains how mental illness became an identity. “Mental illness in the 21st century is an expanding category—and one increasingly dominated by its most functional and therefore visible members. That displacement—in our collective imagination and public discourse—of the profoundly mentally ill by my college students didn’t happen all at once. And how did it happen? Was it because of the closure of traditional mental hospitals, like those of One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest ? Was it because of the internet-driven phenomenon of self-diagnosis by very functional influencers? The marginalization of psychiatry as a profession? Or denial, romanticization, and politics?” It Can Happen Here, Too. “As numerous countries in Europe experience riots, many in America are asking, ‘What on earth is happening on the continent that was, in many ways, the cradle of Western civilization?’ As historic buildings, places of worship, and commercial properties combust before our eyes on the nightly news, how are we to make sense of this?” Carl Trueman warns that what’s happening in Europe could also happen in the United States. 8 Ways to Help Your Kids Love the Church. Shiphrah Lakka offers a series of ways to help your kids learn to love the church. “While discipleship at home is extremely important and something every Christian parent should pursue, it can never replace the church. Reading Scripture together, praying as a family, and teaching our children about God within our homes are vital practices. Yet God’s design for believers extends beyond the walls of our homes. He calls us to belong to a community of believers who worship, serve, and do life together.” I Hate Your Halloween Decorations. Marc Sims writes about the reality of Halloween today. “The next time I am out, we will really slow down to take in the diorama you set up of black hooded figures encircling a pentagram-alter with a fake infant set in the middle of it, that way he can become familiar with Satanic rituals and child sacrifice. I mean, where else is he going to get this important cultural experience? Apparently, you are under the impression that becoming desensitized to violence and death is an important step for our whole neighborhood to take in—to celebrate, even. Here, frumpy old Marc ( boooo! ) was worried about why our culture seems ever more eager to relish death and the demonic—but you have shown me that this is really just fun! Save a fake a corpse for me!” Why Paper Books Endure. Daniel Darling explains his ongoing love for paper books (even while he’s not entirely opposed to electronic ones). “When I began my writing career in the early 2,000s, every single writing conference I attended featured speakers who issued grave warnings. E-books would eventually take over. Paper books would be a thing of the past. Libraries are nice relics of another era. Except that didn’t happen.” Something Worth Doing These words by Maltbie Davenport Babcock have often been a challenge to me, and I wouldn’t be surprised if they challenge you as well. We often think that if we had that man’s means or that man’s ability or that man’s opportunity, we could do something worth doing; but, as we are, there is no possibility of any great thing. title: Is It a Sin to Use AI Porn?
summary: What happens when the people in porn are not real exist, but are merely generated by AI? Could AI allow us to create ethical pornography that solves one of the foremost concerns that come with real pornography? In other words, is it a sin to look at AI-generated porn? See Also 10 Ugly Numbers Describing Pornography Use in 2017 10 Articles on Pornography 7 Good Reasons To Stop Looking at Porn Right Now
summary_zh: 当色情片中的人并不真实存在，而只是由人工智能产生时，会发生什么？人工智能是否允许我们制作道德色情作品，以解决真实色情作品带来的首要问题之一？换句话说，看人工智能生成的色情片是一种罪恶吗？另请参阅2017年描述色情使用的10个丑陋数字10篇关于色情的文章7个现在停止观看色情的好理由
title_zh: 使用人工智能色情片是罪过吗？
content: Over the past two decades, I have written a great deal about pornography . At many different times and in many different forms, I have urged people to consider a long list of arguments against it. I’m thankful to have interacted with many people who have come to see pornography as evil and who have committed themselves to sexual purity. Some of the strongest and most effective arguments against using pornography are based upon the humanity of the people who are involved in it. So, for example, in “ 7 Good Reasons To Stop Looking at Porn Right Now ,” I wrote that we need to consider the cost to those who make it. “Pornography exacts a high cost of those who create it—the cost to their bodies, to their souls, to their mental well-being, to their dignity, to their future. A vast amount of the pornography you enjoy is created by people against their wills. The simple fact is, by watching porn, you are watching rape and deriving pleasure from it. You become a willing participant in sexual violence and you allow that actor on the screen to suffer for your pleasure.” Even if some pornography is consensual, a great deal of pornography is not, and the viewer cannot know which is which. Similarly, in “ 8 Sins You Commit Whenever You Look at Porn ,” I said that those who watch it are guilty of sexual assault. “A person who drives a getaway car for a band of bank robbers will rightly be charged with murder for anyone who is killed in committing that crime. The person who voluntarily watches sexual assault for purposes of titillation is rightly guilty of that sexual assault. And a nauseating quantity of pornography is violent in nature, displaying men taking advantage of women. Sometimes these women have volunteered for such degradation and sometimes they are forced or raped into it. To watch such horrifying smut is to be a participant in it and to bear the moral blemish of it.” While these are far from the only arguments against pornography, I believe they are especially effective ones. But what happens when the characters involved in pornography are no longer people? What happens when they no longer exist at all, but are merely generated by AI? Could AI allow us to create “ethical pornography” that solves one of the foremost concerns that come with “real” pornography? In other words, is it a sin to look at AI-generated porn ? (For our purposes, we will assume that we are already rejecting deepfake porn—using the likeness of an existing person—as morally repugnant and both immoral and illegal. Instead, we are considering images of people who are generated entirely by AI.) The simple answer is yes: it is as sinful to look at AI-generated porn as it is to look at human-created porn. While some of the arguments may not be as relevant, the majority are unchanged. Before I explain how and why, I want you to listen to a warning: we are all experts at circumventing the spirit of the law by abiding within the strict letter of the law. There is something deep within us that wants to defy the rules that are given to us, and we become skilled at justifying the ways we do this. Often this involves reducing morality to a strict binary, then convincing ourselves that because we have not blatantly broken the law, we have abided by it. This was exactly the sin of the Pharisees of Jesus’s day who would strictly tithe the spices they grew in their gardens, yet fail to live according to the higher principles of justice, mercy, and faithfulness. There is something of the Pharisee in each one of us. With that in mind, here are reasons why it is a sin to use pornography that has been generated by AI. You are still lusting , even if you are lusting after a person who exists only on a screen. To lust is to long for an illicit sexual pleasure, and to long for an illicit sexual pleasure is to find satisfaction in what God has forbidden. It is to make something other than God necessary for your joy—in this case, the sexual release that would come with looking at an
content_zh: 在过去20年里,我写了很多关于色情的内容。 在许多不同的时刻,我以许多不同的形式敦促人们考虑一长串反对它的论点。 我很感激与许多人互动, 一些强烈而最有效的反对使用色情作品的论据是基于参与其中的人的人道. 因此,例如,在“停止看色情电影的7个好理由”中,我写道,我们需要考虑制作者的成本。 " 色情制品的制作者付出了高昂的代价 -- -- 他们的身体、灵魂、精神健康、尊严、未来的代价。 你所欣赏的大量色情作品都是由人们违背自己的意愿所创造的. 简单的事实是,通过看色情片, 你正在看强奸,并从中获得乐趣。 你成为性暴力的自愿参与者,你允许屏幕上那个演员为取悦而受苦。” 即使有些色情作品是合意的,但大量的色情作品却不是,观众也无法知道哪个是. 同样,在“每当你看到色情制品时,你就会犯下八起罪行”中,我说,观看色情制品的人犯有性侵犯罪。 “为一帮银行劫匪驾驶逃跑的汽车的人,将因犯下这种罪行而被杀害的人受到谋杀的指控。 自愿观看性攻击以达到抚慰目的的人理应犯有性攻击罪。 而令人恶心的色情作品数量在性质上是暴力的,展现出男性利用女性. 有时,这些妇女自愿从事这种有辱人格的工作,有时她们被迫或被强奸。 目睹这种令人发指的一团糟,就是参与其中,并承担其中的道德污点。” 虽然这些与反对色情制品的唯一论点相去甚远, 但是当参与色情的人物不再是人时会怎样呢? 当它们不再存在,而只是由AI产生时会发生什么? 大赦国际能否允许我们制造出“道德色情制品”,解决与“真正的”色情制品有关的最主要关切之一? 换句话说,看AI生成的色情片是不是罪过? (为了我们的目的,我们将假定,我们已经在拒绝利用像现有个人那样的深层假色情,认为这种色情在道德上是令人厌恶的,既不道德又非法。) 相反,我们正在考虑完全由大赦国际创造的人的形象。 ) 简单的回答是:看AI生成的色情片和看人造色情片一样罪恶. 虽然有些论点可能并不那么相关,但大多数论点没有改变。 在我解释方式和原因之前,我要你们聆听一个警告:我们都是通过遵守严格的法律条文来规避法律精神的专家。 我们内心深处有些东西想藐视赋予我们的规则,我们变得有技巧为我们这样做的方式辩护。 这往往涉及将道德降低为严格的二进制,然后说服自己,因为我们没有公然违法,我们遵守了法律。 这恰恰是耶稣时代的法利赛人的罪过,他们严格地说要将自己在花园所种的调味品的两倍之多,但却未能按照正义、慈悲和忠诚的更高原则活下来。 我们每个人都有法利赛人 考虑到这一点,以下是使用大赦国际制作的色情制品的罪责。 你仍然在贪欲, 即使你在贪欲 一个人只存在于屏幕上。 性欲是渴望非法的性快感,而渴望非法的性快感是寻求上帝所禁止的满足. 是为了让上帝之外的东西成为你欢乐的必备之物——在这种情况下,是性释放,而这种性释放会伴随着对一个...

content: Good morning. May the Lord be with you and bless you today, my friends. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include lots of good books from New Growth Press and other publishers. Among them you’ll find several good options from Jared Wilson. Recommended Reading Goodbye, ‘Sam’s Club’ Megachurch. Hello, Stained Glass. Christianity Today reports on what I consider a welcome trend: church buildings that look like churches instead of warehouses. It begins this way: “Trinity Presbyterian finally has a church building of its own. That building has arches. And carved hammerbeams that tell the story of the Bible.” 3 Reasons Why Christians Should Lay “R.I.P.” to Rest. Nick Batzig thinks it would be best for Christians to lay R.I.P. to rest. “I’ve noticed something of a concerning trend over the past several years. It is the way in which believers speak about culture-impacting individuals at their deaths. Instead of simply expressing appreciation for their life and achievements, it has become commonplace for Christians to use the shorthand ‘R.I.P.’ (rest in peace) on social media when speaking of individuals in whose lives there was no evidence of saving grace at their death. At the risk of sounding ill-tempered, I wish to set out several reasons why I am troubled by this occurrence.” Go Deeper with Ligonier’s Grow App. Looking to put down roots in God’s Word? The Grow app from Ligonier Ministries gives you clear Bible teaching and guides your daily study for a deeper walk with Christ. Ministry Partners can also access the verse-by-verse notes from the Reformation Study Bible directly in the app and get reliable answers to their theological questions with the Ask Ligonier intelligent assistant. Not a Ligonier Ministry Partner yet? Try these features for 30 days when you download Grow and sign in. (Sponsored) Beauty Demands to Be Noticed. Michael Jensen is right: beauty demands to be noticed. He tells about people who understand the connection between beauty and transcendence and says, “Clearly, the reductive and polemical explanation of the atheists isn’t proving to be compelling. People can’t square their deeply felt experience of the world with that. To the people I’ve been speaking with, at least, the world simply cannot be reduced to its material components, nor can its coherence be explained by resorting to chance.” Aslan Sane: The Bowiefication of Narnia. I’ve got a pair of articles to share that comment on the forthcoming Narnia movies, each taking a different perspective. In the first, the writer remembers the old Narnia series from her childhood and bridges from there to what we know of the new one. She’s not impressed with it. Aslan and the Christians Who Can’t Be Enchanted. In the second, the author rebukes people like me (and the previous author) who have expressed concerns. He reminds us that it’s a movie for kids and that we don’t really know much about it yet. (I’d say he writes with some degree of exaggeration when he accuses me of losing my mind, but I’m glad to consider what he says nonetheless.) The Day of Pioneer Missions Is Not Over. Writing for Desiring God, my friend Tim Keesee wants us to know that the day of pioneer missions is not over. “Pioneer missionaries are still needed today because there are vast territories and high-rise megacities where the gospel message has yet to reach.” Videos Worth Watching Here are several brief videos that are worth your time. 5 Signs Your Church Might Be Too Seeker Sensitive. Adriel Sanchez explains seeker sensitivity and offers signs your church might lean too much in that direction and become seeker driven. How to Leave a Church Well. Hershael York speaks specifically to pastors to explain how and when to leave a church well. The Enduring Word. This short film from Crossway celebrates God’s providence through the history of Bible translation. Flashback What’s The Point Of Family Devotions? title: This Week in Christian Books (October 27, 2026)
summary: This week brings a substantial new commentary on the Westminster Confession of Faith from a whole team of Reformed scholars, an updated edition of a well-known apologetics book, a couple of books for kids, and a new edition of the ESV. summary_zh: 本周带来了整个改革宗学者团队对威斯敏斯特信仰告白的实质性新评论，一本著名护教书籍的更新版本，几本儿童书籍和新版ESV。另请参阅2026年10月新的和著名的基督教书籍（加上11月的预览）对利未记熄灯的最佳评论
title_zh: 本周基督教书籍（ 2026年10月27日）
content: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books, so each week I let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. This week brings a substantial new commentary on the Westminster Confession of Faith from a whole team of Reformed scholars, an updated edition of a well-known apologetics book, a couple of books for kids, and a new edition of the ESV. In each case, I’ve included the publisher’s description. (This is a new feature I trialed last week. The response was positive, so I’m going to keep it going. I have tried to improve the format and layout to make it easier to read.) Books for Everyone Crossway The Westminster Confession of Faith A Comprehensive Commentary on Its History, Theology, and Application Edited by J. V. Fesko, John R. Muether, and D. Blair Smith Endorsed by: Joel R. Beeke, Michael Horton, Keith A. Mathison, Robert Letham, and Jonathan L. Master Publisher’s description What is Reformed theology? In 1646, a group of theologians composed what is arguably the most comprehensive statement of faith, the Westminster Confession. Their efforts to preserve Protestant theology against opposing beliefs endured. Today, amid growing interest in Reformed Christianity, the Westminster Confession remains an indispensable guide for living out doctrine, worship, and church governance sola Scriptura, “by Scripture alone.” This essential collection of essays presents an accessible guide to the Westminster Confession of Faith for 21st-century readers. Each chapter is devoted to a section of the historic document, carefully studying its context, its significance to the faith, and its application, as well as any controversies. Clear, thorough explanations of principles, including the Trinity, creation, providence, baptism, last judgment, and more, make this the definitive guide on Reformed Christian doctrine. The essays are written by faculty from Reformed Theological Seminary in their areas of expertise, ensuring a trustworthy and high-quality text for church leaders, teachers and students of theology, and laypeople. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . Crossway I Don’t Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist Updated Edition Norman L. Geisler and Frank Turek Endorsed by: Gavin Ortlund, Sean McDowell, Gregory Koukl, Alisa Childers, and Josh Howerton Publisher’s description To some, the concept of having faith in a higher power or a set of religious beliefs is nonsensical. Indeed, many view religion in general, and Christianity in particular, as unfounded and unreasonable. Frank Turek and Norman Geisler argue, however, that Christianity is not only more reasonable than all other belief systems but is indeed more rational than unbelief itself. With conviction and clear thinking, Turek and Geisler guide readers through some of the traditional, tested arguments for the existence of a creator God. They move into an examination of the source of morality and the reliability of the New Testament accounts concerning Jesus. The final section of the book deals with a detailed investigation of the claims of Christ. This updated volume with fresh arguments will be an interesting read for those skeptical about Christianity, as well as a helpful resource for Christians seeking to articulate a more sophisticated defense of their faith. Buy it at Amazon . Baker Books Giver of All Good God as the Beginning and End of Ethics Chase R. Kuhn Publisher’s description Where do our ethics come from? Are they based on unchanging realities or subject to revision as human culture develops and changes? What distinguishes Christian ethics from other moral claims? And how can Christians engage these questions with clarity and confidence—without either abandoning their convictions or abandoning the conversation? In Giver of All Good , Chase R. Kuhn argues that the answer begins not with ourselves—our feelings, our culture, our moral intuitions—but with God. What we believe about God shapes how we live. Our theology guides
content_zh: 星期二是大多数出版商发行新书的一天,所以每周我都会告诉你,我最密切地关注的出版商刚刚给我们带来了什么。 本周来自整群改革派学者对"威斯敏斯特信仰的忏悔"(Westminster Confession of Faith)提出了实质性的新评论,并更新了一出名作"通俗小说"(Apologetics Book),一出给孩子们的几本书和一出"ESV"的新版本. 每一次,我都包括出版商的描述。 (这是上星期我试演的新节目) 回应是积极的, 我努力改进格式和布局,使其更容易阅读。 ) 由J. V. Fesko、John R. Muether和D. Blair Smith编辑, 乔尔·R·比克、Michael Horton、Keith A. Mathison、Robert Letham和Jonathan L. Master Publishers对改革神学的描述。 1646年,一群神学家组成了可以说是最全面的信仰声明"威斯敏斯特忏悔". 他们努力保护新教神学,反对对立的信仰。 如今,在对改革后的基督教越来越感兴趣的情况下,威斯敏斯特忏悔仍然是“仅靠圣经”活出学说、崇拜和教会治理的不可或缺的指南。 这份重要的散文集为21世纪的读者提供了威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔的可获取指南. 每一章都专门讨论历史文件的一节,仔细研究其背景、其对信仰的意义、其应用以及任何争议。 对原则,包括"三一","创造","天赐","受洗","最后的判断"等进行明确,彻底的解释,使这成为"改革后基督教学说"的决定性指南. 论文由改革神学院的教师在其专业领域撰写,确保教会领导人、神学教师和学生以及外行者能够获得可靠和高质量的文本。 在亚马逊或威斯敏斯特书店买的 Crossway I don't have enough Faith to be an Atheist 更新版 Norman L. Geisler and Frank Turek 由加文·奥尔特伦德,肖恩·麦克道威尔,格雷戈里·库克尔,艾莉莎·柴尔德斯和乔什·豪尔顿出版商的描述认可 对一些人来说,对更高权力或一套宗教信仰有信仰的概念是没有意识的. 事实上,许多人认为,一般宗教,特别是基督教,是毫无根据和不合理的。 然而,弗兰克·图雷克和诺曼·盖斯勒(Norman Geisler)认为,基督教不仅比所有其他信仰体系更合理,而且确实比不信本身更合理. 以信念和清晰的思考,图雷克和盖斯勒指导读者通过一些传统的,经过考验的关于创造出神存在的论点. 他们开始研究道德渊源和"新约"中有关耶稣的叙述的可靠性. 该书的最后一节详细论述对基督的主张的调查. 这本附有新论点的增订本,对于那些对基督教持怀疑态度的人来说,将是一个有趣的读物,也是基督教徒寻求更尖端地捍卫其信仰的有用资源。 在亚马逊买的 Baker Books of All Good God的出品人作为伦理学的开始和结束 Chase R. Kuhn出版社的描述 我们的道德从何而来? 它们是建立在不断变化的现实基础上,还是随着人类文化的发展和变化而需要加以修改? 基督教道德与其他道德主张有什么区别? 基督徒如何以明确和自信的方式处理这些问题,而不放弃他们的信念或放弃对话? Chase R. Kuhn指出,答案不是从我们自己开始的——我们的感情、我们的文化和我们的道德直觉——而是从上帝开始的。 我们对上帝的信仰 塑造了我们的生活 我们的神学指南

title_zh: 第一人称：伟大的使命—我们主人的月球射击
content: Portrait of Jeff Ginn, IMB senior ambassador of U.S. and global relations. IMB Photo I was born in 1961. The U.S. president at that time was John F. Kennedy. In that year he issued a challenge to our nation. It was that we build a rocket ship, put men in it, send it to the moon, have them walk on the surface, plant our flag, then return them safely to earth. He called on the nation to accomplish this within a decade. This extraordinary, demanding, costly endeavor is known to history as Kennedy’s “moon shot.” The nation rose to the challenge. I still remember watching in 1969 a grainy, black-and-white broadcast as Neil Armstrong stepped on the surface of the moon and declared, “One small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.” We often think of the astronauts with admiration. And rightly so. They were courageous. However, let’s note that the Apollo mission employed some 400,000 additional people to fulfill the mission. Team members included mission controllers, metal fabricators, communication specialists, caterers, engineers, scientists, nurses, doctors, mathematicians and computer programmers. Beyond these, all U.S. taxpayers contributed! It took a nation to get two astronauts to the moon and safely return them! That term, “moon shot,” has made its way into our vocabulary. It can be used for other daring, costly, and valuable undertakings. It is fair, then, to say that the Lord Jesus, our Master, has a moon shot of His own! His mission merits our lives and resources. His mission includes all who name Christ as Lord collaborating to fulfill it. At the International Mission Board, all our plans, strategies and decisions center around this biblical idea that we all must work together to fulfill Christ’s mission. We all must pray. We all must give. We all must go. We all must send. Matthew 28:18-20 is one passage, perhaps the best known, that gives us the details for our mission. The name that evangelicalism has given to this passage is “The Great Commission.” The word “commission” is not one that we use commonly. It simply means a command. How interesting that, with hundreds of commands in Scripture, this is this one that gets the definitive article, “the,” and the adjective, “great.” Does it merit that moniker? I say that it does, and I offer three reasons why. Because it makes a great claim When quoting the Great Commission, it is common for folks to omit verse 18 and simply begin with verse 19. But to do so undercuts the weight that Jesus’ claim in verse 18 adds. There He claims to have all authority in heaven and on earth. That essentially is a claim to divinity — to supremacy. He is saying that He is the King above all kings and the Lord above all lords. When we consider His claim, we all have a choice to make. To borrow from C. S. Lewis, we could decide that He is a liar or a lunatic. Following liberal theologians or Muslim theology, we could decide that much of what is taught about Him in the New Testament is the stuff of legend — that the disciples exaggerated and “created” the Christ of faith. Jeff and Nell Ginn served with the International Mission Board in Colombia. Jeff currently serves churches as IMB senior ambassador. IMB Photo But the decision that I have made (and on which I’ve staked my eternal destiny) is that He is not a liar, nor a lunatic, nor a legend. He is, in fact, Lord! My prayer is that all will decide similarly. As such, He has the authority to issue any commission and our only right response is, “Yes, Lord!” His authority is why, 35 years ago, my wife, Nell, and I said “yes” when He called us to serve with the IMB in Cali, Colombia.  It was under His authority that we planted churches and taught future leaders in the seminary there. Because it gives a great command Not only is it the Great Commission because of the claim that it contains, it is great because of the command it presents.  In verses 19 and 20 there are at least four verbal ideas mentioned: go, make disciples (one word in the origina
content_zh:
美国和全球关系高级大使杰夫·吉恩的肖像. IMB Photo I生于1961年. 当时的美国总统是约翰·肯尼迪. 当年,他向我国提出了挑战。 正是我们造了一艘火箭船,把人装进去,送去月球,让他们行走在地表上,种下我们的旗帜,然后安全地还给地球.

他呼吁全国在十年内完成这项工作. 这一艰巨而昂贵的努力在历史上被称为肯尼迪的"月出"。 国家奋起迎接挑战.

我仍然记得1969年在尼尔·阿姆斯特朗踏上月球时观看了一场黑白交织的广播,并宣布“人类迈出了一小步,人类迈出了一大步”。 我们经常以钦佩的眼光来看待宇航员. 没错 他们是勇敢的。 然而,我们要指出的是,阿波罗飞行任务又雇用了大约40万人来完成这一任务。

小组成员包括特派团控制员、金属制造员、通信专家、宴会人员、工程师、科学家、护士、医生、数学家和计算机程序员。 除此之外,所有美国纳税人都贡献了! 一个民族把两个宇航员送入月球安全送还!. “被射出月球”一词已经进入我们的词汇。

它可用于其他大胆、昂贵和有价值的工作。 那么说上帝耶稣 我们的主人 拥有自己的月球镜头是公平的! 他的使命值得我们给予生命和资源。 他的使命包括所有将基督命名为"主"的人,他们合作完成使命.

在国际传教委员会,我们的所有计划、战略和决定都围绕这个圣经思想,即我们大家必须共同努力来完成基督的使命。 我们都必须祈祷。 我们都必须给予。 我们都得走了。 我们都得送去 Matthew 28: 18 -20是一段,也许最有名的一段,这给我们提供了我们任务的细节.

福音派给这个段落起的名字是“大委员会”。 “委员会”一词不是我们常用的。 这仅仅是命令 如此有趣的是,在《圣经》中有数百个命令, 这篇是获得“the,”和形容词“Great”的决定性文章。 这值得吗? 我说它确实如此,我提出三个原因。

因为它在引用Great Commission(Great Commission)时提出了很大的主张,人们通常省略了第18节,简单地从第19节开始. 但这样做会削弱耶稣在第18节中声称增加的分量。 那边 他声称在天地间拥有一切权威. 这基本上是对神权——至高无上——的宣称。

他说他是国王 高于所有国王 高于所有领主 当我们考虑 他的主张,我们都有一个选择。 从C. S. Lewis那里借钱 我们可以决定他是骗子还是疯子

追随自由主义神学家或穆斯林神学,我们可以决定,"新约"中关于他的大部分教义是传说的东西——门徒夸大并"创造了"信仰的基督. 杰夫和内尔·吉恩在哥伦比亚的国际使团委员会任职。 杰夫目前为教会担任IMB高级大使.

因此,他有权发布任何委托书,我们唯一的正确答复是:“是的,主啊!” 35年前,他的妻子Nell和我在打电话请我们到哥伦比亚卡利为IMB服务时说“同意”。 正是在他的授权下,我们在那里的神学院里植入了教堂并教导了未来的领导人.

But leaders with the International Mission Board say some of the greatest needs today are for professionals whose work happens behind the scenes. IMB leaders report that critical roles such as teachers, healthcare workers, counselors, accountants, logistics specialists and member care personnel are helping advance the Great Commission in ways many churches never see. Doreen Baker, IMB director
summary_zh: 当大多数"南方浸信会"想到传教士时,他们常常会描绘出教会的植树人和福音派. 但国际使命委员会的领导人说,今天最需要的是那些在幕后工作的专业人员。 咨监委领导人报告说,教师、保健工作者、顾问、会计师、后勤专家和成员护理人员等关键角色正在帮助推进大委员会,许多教会从未看到过。 多琳·贝克,IMB导演
title_zh: IMB寻求教师、医护人员、商业专业人士担任传教士
content: IMB missionary Dr. Heidi Haun, left, checks on patients at Baptist Medical Centre in Nalerigu, Ghana. There are needed roles for IMB missionaries in healthcare, ministering to the needs of local populations and utilizing this time to minister to spiritual needs. IMB Photo When most Southern Baptists think of missionaries, they often picture church planters and evangelists. But leaders with the International Mission Board say some of the greatest needs today are for professionals whose work happens behind the scenes. IMB leaders report that critical roles such as teachers, healthcare workers, counselors, accountants, logistics specialists and member care personnel are helping advance the Great Commission in ways many churches never see. Doreen Baker, IMB director of TCK (third culture kid or missionary kid) education, sees a constant need for education professionals. Teachers are needed in international schools, which cover a variety of global educational entities, and in other settings to provide for missionary kids and their educational needs. “Teachers are significant in that not only are they providing instruction for students, but they are an integral part of the core missionary task ,” Baker said. “We also have great needs for consultants to support our families on the field with their children’s education in many ways.” Baker previously served 25 years teaching in Asia and experienced how education creates access to missions where traditional pathways may be limited. IMB missionary Ellie Bohrer teaches a 12th grade World Views class at Black Forest Academy in Germany. The IMB is seeking other educators, like Bohrer, who are willing to use their skills on the mission field. IMB Photo Scott Ray, IMB senior director of global deployment, noted that many missionary positions go unfilled simply because they fall outside traditional perceptions of missionary service. He said professional skills can provide both practical ministry support and access to countries where traditional missionary visas are difficult to obtain. Opportunities exist for finance professionals, veterinarians, medical workers, Send Relief personnel and others. Healthcare remains one of the most strategic areas in demand. Tom Hicks, IMB director of global health strategies, said many medical professionals have the wrong perception about mission work. “We do have an issue where people will select out because they don’t think that what they do is useful on the mission field,” he said. In reality, Hicks said many areas across the globe are increasingly seeking family medicine physicians, internists, pediatricians, pediatric nurse practitioners, OB providers, physical therapists, occupational therapists, speech pathologists and lactation consultants. The need is especially significant in sub-Saharan Africa, where young populations create a growing demand for pediatric care. Healthcare professionals also provide a unique advantage in countries that restrict missionary activity. “Missionaries with a vocational value, like healthcare missionaries, have opportunities to go places that others can’t go,” Hicks said. Another often-overlooked ministry is member care, which focuses on the spiritual, emotional, mental and relational health of IMB missionaries. Chris Martin is the IMB director of global member care. “Member care missionaries stand alongside those missionaries that are thought of traditionally as church planters or evangelists and support them,” Martin said. Many who serve in these roles come from counseling backgrounds and help missionaries navigate stress, conflict, grief and other challenges that can affect long-term ministry effectiveness. Martin compares their role to Aaron and Hur in Exodus 19, holding up Moses’ arms during battle, strengthening those serving on the front lines. IMB missionary Glen Garner uses his business skills and experience as the logistics director for missionaries serving globally. He lives in Lima, Peru, with his wife, Shannon
content_zh: IMB传教士海迪·哈恩博士出走,在加纳纳莱里古的浸信会医疗中心检查病人. 咨监委的传教士在保健、满足当地居民需要和利用这一时间满足精神需要方面需要发挥作用。 IMB Photo 当大多数"南方浸信会"想到传教士时,他们经常会描绘出教会的植树人和福音会信徒. 但国际使命委员会的领导人说,今天最需要的是那些在幕后工作的专业人员。 咨监委领导人报告说,教师、保健工作者、顾问、会计师、后勤专家和成员护理人员等关键角色正在帮助推进大委员会,许多教会从未看到过。 多琳·贝克(英语:Doreen Baker,IMB Director of TCK (TCK)教育(英语:TCK (third Culture kid or missionary kid)))的导演,不断看到教育专业人士的需求. 国际学校需要教师,这些学校包括各种全球教育实体,其他环境则需要教师,以满足传教儿童及其教育需要。 教师不仅为学生授课, 也是核心传教任务的组成部分。 " 我们还非常需要顾问,以多种方式支持我们在外地的家庭,教育他们的孩子。 " 贝克以前在亚洲执教了25年,并体验了教育如何创造进入传统途径可能有限的特派团的机会。 IMB传教士艾莉·波克勒在德国黑森林学院教授一门12年级"世界观"课程. IMB正在寻找其他教育者,比如波尔,他们愿意在任务领域运用自己的技能. Martin说,“会员关心传教士与那些传统上被认为是教会植树人或福音传教士的传教士站在一起并支持他们。” 担任这些角色的许多人来自咨询背景,帮助传教士应对压力、冲突、悲痛和其他挑战,这些挑战可能影响部委的长期效力。 马丁将他们的角色比作出埃及19号的Aaron和Hur,在战斗中举起摩西的手臂,强化了在前线服役的人. IMB传教士格伦·加纳(英语:Glen Garner)利用其作为在全球服务的传教士的后勤主任的业务技能和经验. 他和妻子香农住在秘鲁利马

title_zh: IMB传教士通过新信徒和当地教会看到神在工作
content: In South Asia, Maryam and a local pastor baptize Tara, a new believer. IMB missionaries work alongside local believers and churches to fulfill the Great Commission. IMB Photo Twenty minutes had passed already. The sun was going down, and they were looking everywhere, but they only saw men in the park. Sophia, an International Mission Board missionary, joined another IMB missionary and Maryam, a South Asian Christian. They went to the park to share the gospel, but approaching a man in their Muslim-majority city was out of the question. They kept walking and watching. Even if they went home without a single conversation, Sophia knew Maryam would want to try again. This woman who had grown up with a distrust of Muslims, now searched a park for a Muslim woman to tell about Jesus. When Sophia first invited her along, Maryam never imagined a Muslim could come to know Jesus. But the more they went out sharing the gospel together, the more God softened her heart. “One day, I found she was sharing in the park by herself, without me,” Sophia said with a laugh. These days, she shares regularly — with classmates, with rickshaw drivers, with women in the park, when she can find them. God transformed Maryam’s heart. He could transform this walk through the park, too. “So we stopped,” Sophia said, “and prayed, ‘God, give us just one woman to talk to.’” Then they spotted her — a girl sitting alone on a bench. Meeting the girl on the bench She looked like other conservative Muslim women in the area, covered in black except for her face. They approached casually, not wanting to frighten her. It was Eid al-Adha – “one of the biggest Muslim holidays here,” Sophia said. They greeted her and asked about her holiday plans. Her name was Tara, and she wasn’t intimidated at all. “You may think I’m a Muslim from the way I dress,” she said, “but actually in my heart, I have left Islam.” “I was a little shocked,” Sophia said, hearing such a bold statement from a stranger. Tara told them she was a university student at a conservative Islamic school, but she had grown disillusioned and discontent with the religion. “ I don’t believe in Islam anymore,” Tara said. Without knowledge of God, she had no one to pray to, and it left her lonely. She’d been searching — Buddhism and Hinduism from friends, even a meeting with atheists, who struck her as unhappy, following only themselves. “Do you know any Christians?” Sophia asked. “Would you like to hear what we believe?” “Sure, please share.” They read about Jesus’ birth, and Tara was hungry for more. When she asked about church, Sophia described their congregation of about 40 believers, many from a Muslim background. Though she wasn’t ready to visit the church, Tara continued her interest in learning. Sophia and Maryam met with her every week in coffee shops, tea shops, Sophia’s home, wherever they could talkthat wasn’t too loud or have “too many ears and eyes” observing them. Finding her closest friend They read through the Gospel of John. One November day in a coffee shop, they reached the passage on the Samaritan woman at the well, and Sophia noticed Tara was crying. “Tara, I see you have tears,” Sophia said. “Let’s stop. Let’s talk about it .” That day, Tara prayed to receive Christ. Soon after, she wanted to visit the church, though nervous how believers would receive her in a hijab. “They will love you,” Sophia told her. “Don’t worry.” Tara went and was welcomed. That Christmas, 80 people packed Sophia’s apartment, singing and dancing in circles. Across the room, Sophia saw Tara, wearing red Christmas garland like a scarf and a smile stretched across her face. “Tara grew up very conservative – music was not even allowed in her home. But now she’s dancing, worshiping the Lord with us with music and songs.” In South Asia, Maryam and a local pastor baptize Tara, a new believer. IMB missionaries work alongside local believers and churches to fulfill the Great Commission. IMB Photo That spring, Tara was baptized.

title_zh: 神通过IMB在意大利的传教士保持忠诚
content: The eastern face of St. Peter's Basilica in the Vatican City in Rome, Italy, is famous for its central balcony from which popes give their papal addresses. Most people in Rome have at least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” IMB Photo In the city where Jason and Lizzy Davis serve, some steps have a lot of meaning. And the meaning is different for them than it is for the thousands who travel there to visit that site. “If you come to Rome, you can come to a place called the Holy Steps,” Jason said. “People go there, and they’ll crawl up on their knees and pray the rosary all the way up.” From the top of the steps, a mural depicting Jesus on the Cross looks down on those making the pilgrimage. For Jason and Lizzy, it’s a spiritual experience, a picture of a religion that asks people to earn their way to Jesus. “That’s really the opposite of what the gospel is. The gospel is Jesus saying, ‘No, you can’t do it . . . no matter how good you think you are,’” they said. Most people in Rome have at the very least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism, as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” Jason explained, “It’s where the Pope lives in the Vatican. It’s very much part of the religion and culture. It’s all intertwined here.” An ‘unavoidable’ call Jason and Lizzy are investing their lives as International Mission Board missionaries in Rome, Italy, to share the truth of the gospel. The Davises partner with national believers through a new church plant, and they’re seeking to plant more churches within the city. Lizzy said for her, the call to missions was unavoidable. “I grew up as a third culture kid, or a missionary kid. My parents were on the mission field, as were my grandparents, all with the International Mission Board.” Then her family moved to Virginia for her dad to work for IMB’s home office staff. As a middle schooler and high schooler, every time Lizzy heard about the need for the gospel to go forth, she felt a burden, a “burning” in her heart. She didn’t know what God would do with that, but she had a feeling she would see one day. Now, years later, she and Jason spend their time trying to find as many opportunities as they can to invite people into their home so they can share the hope of Jesus with them. That can mean Bible study or simply sharing a meal. ‘Completely lost’ Jason has been surprised by just how often people are willing to talk about faith. “You can get into spiritual conversations very quickly with people, especially if you’re just open and honest with them.” Lizzy shared that one of the easiest ways to do this is to be willing to let your day be interrupted. “That’s something I’ve seen Jason do firsthand in our neighborhood. He walks down the street, and everybody knows him because he stops and takes the time to ask them questions about their families, gets to know people, gets to know the newspaper stand guy and the guy at the fruit stand and the grocery store ladies.” She emphasized that caring about people is “what Christ would do.” The Davises, whose previous mission service prevents their photos from being published, live in a neighborhood of about 130,000 people. Their church of 15 people is the only evangelical congregation there. Lizzy said the area is “truly a lost, completely lost, dark neighborhood” with people who have never heard the gospel. Thousands more come to their area on a religious quest. The Davis family’s neighborhood is home to the Basilica Papale di San Paolo (the Papal Basilica of Saint Paul), one of the city’s four major basilicas. “So we get a lot of people coming on spiritual journeys, visiting our neighborhood, seeking some sort of spiritual experience. And oftentimes it’s just trying to earn their salvation,” she added. Jason described this environment as “a genuine need for people to actually hear the gospel and know that their sins can be forgiven and they can have an assurance of that.” IMB missionaries Jason and Liz

title_zh: 全球传教士合作伙伴通过IMB团队扩展福音工作
content: Rebeca Couto poses with her IMB teammates. Couto is a global missionary partner serving alongside IMB missionaries in Japan. IMB Photo Rebeca Couto poses with her violin. Couto is a professional violinist who is serving as a global missionary partner with the IMB in Japan. Doors have opened for her to use her skills with evangel ical Japanese musicians who perform. IMB Photo Rebeca Couto moved from one volcanic archipelago to another, leaving Portugal’s Azores islands to anchor her life in Japan. The percentage of evangelical Christians in the Azores and Japan is similar, with both populations under 1%. Couto is a fourth-generation Christian, a rarity on the small islands. She is one of few, if any, believers in the Azores with such a long spiritual lineage. This rich legacy shaped her and prepared her for ministry. “I’ve always understood the Great Commission as a call for all believers and all disciples of Christ to be missionaries, wherever they are, whatever they’re doing, and whatever God has equipped them with,” Couto said. Couto’s great-grandfather became a Christian through the witness of missionaries from the United Kingdom. Later, missionaries from the Foreign Mission Board, now the International Mission Board, started the first Baptist work in the Azores by planting an English-speaking church near an American military base. A Baptist Brazilian couple planted a Portuguese-speaking church, which became the congregation where Couto grew up and was commissioned as a missionary. Ministry has been passed down through the generations of her family. Couto’s father has pastored for 20 years, and both of her parents have been involved in ministry for most of their lives. Couto now serves in Japan as a global missionary partner, a missionary who is financially supported by a sending church or organization in their home country and serves with IMB teams. Close to 400 GMPs currently serve on IMB teams around the world. Language learning Couto is immersed in language study in Yokohama, Japan. She had a head start before she even arrived. After graduating from high school, Couto moved from the Azores to Lisbon to pursue a degree in music. She spent hours on public transportation and wanted a challenge to pass the time. She decided to study Japanese because she thought it sounded beautiful. At the time, she had no intention of becoming a missionary in the traditional sense. However, the more she learned about the language and the culture, her burden for the lost grew. She began researching Christianity in Japan. “I understood how bleak the scenario was, and how much the country needed Jesus. I struggled with that calling because the doors were closed, and it didn’t seem possible to come to Japan for a myriad of reasons,” Couto said. After finishing master’s degrees in music and violin performance, along with a seminary degree, Couto was considering pursuing a Ph.D. or returning to seminary when her seminary professors, IMB missionaries Jonathan and Bethany Sharp, contacted her about serving as a missionary in Japan. They introduced her to the GMP program and invited her to attend a missions immersion school they piloted . Rebeca Couto (far right) poses with her IMB teammates. Couto is a global missionary partner serving alongside IMB missionaries in Japan. IMB Photo Music to their ears As a professional violinist, Couto brought her violin to Japan, unsure of what opportunities existed, but she knew her call to the mission field somehow involved her gifting. “I see myself as having been called to serve through music. I never even conceived doing missions while excluding the violin entirely,” Couto said. She continued, “Music is such a universal way to connect with people, and it’s so intuitive to pair that with the gospel and with God’s message to people’s hearts.” While she knew the Lord would somehow open a door for her to use the violin for kingdom work, she was at peace with the possibility that, for a season, she may not be as

title_zh: IMB传教士使用家庭、咖啡馆、应用程序为西班牙的福音对话敞开大门
content: Men and women gather to discuss spiritual topics with Caleb and Carina Beaty, International Mission Board missionaries who serve in Madrid. IMB Photo Across Spain, people looking for connection and meaningful conversation turn to the internet to find groups where they can meet others. At a café by the river, Caleb and Carina Beaty engage in conversations about finding purpose, beauty and “what’s wrong with the world.” A website called Meetup allows people to search for groups to meet in person. The description of the Beatys’ group indicates that it discusses spiritual topics. People come expecting to talk about faith, so it’s not a surprise when they arrive. Caleb said he always has a list of questions that begin broadly and funnel into questions such as, “If there were a God …” or “What do you think Christians believe about that?” or “Why do you think religions have such different perspectives?” The Beatys’ goal in these conversations is to work toward deeper worldview questions within 45 minutes to an hour. Most of the people who attend their Meetup group are from Madrid, but they also have conversations with people from other countries. During one Meetup, Caleb and Carina shared how creation was perfect, but sin led to a world separated from the Father. God offers salvation through the death and resurrection of Jesus, they explained. “There are times we’re able to get to a clear gospel presentation with a group of people, and sometimes we’re doing pre-evangelism.” Caleb said. Some repeat attendees who have been attending for more than a year quickly jump to the heart of the discussion. “All right, Caleb, what’s the Bible say about suffering?” they’ll ask. Caleb and Carina then have the opportunity to share the Christian perspective. IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty and their children pose for a photo in a park in Madrid, Spain.  IMB Photo Spain has secularized rapidly since the 1990s, Caleb said. While many may think of it as a Catholic nation, many people do not know the basic tenets of Christianity. “We’ve got all the churches, we’ve got the cathedrals, and they do processions, but the average person on the street does not know anything about the gospel and does not know anything about Jesus,” Caleb said. Younger Spaniards are drawn to their group and are receptive to the gospel because they don’t have a spiritual foundation or know anyone who does. “There’s just this curiosity because, for a lot of them, they’ve never met someone who actually believes that God exists, and that changes your life,” Carina said. “I’ve had people completely shocked that we believe in God. ‘You really believe that God exists?’ They can’t wrap their mind around that.” During one Meetup, a man contrasted Protestant and Catholic beliefs by saying Protestants focus on Jesus’ suffering and Catholics on Mary’s grief. Caleb responded that evangelicals focus on the resurrection. When Caleb said Jesus rose from the dead, the man replied that he needed to look into that. Caleb said encounters like that reveal how little many Spaniards know about the gospel. Caleb noted the irony of the man’s sharing the Catholic perspective without truly understanding it. He is not the only person the Beatys have met who has missed the heart of the gospel. A friend of the Beatys told them she’d heard Jesus died, but she hadn’t heard he rose from the dead. A man reads a passage of Scripture during a Bible study hosted by IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty at their family’s apartment in Madrid, Spain. Five atheists began attending their Bible study after attending the couple’s Meetup group. IMB Photo The Beatys also host seasonal outreach events through the Meetup. Members from their church in Madrid have started attending the Meetup to learn how the Beatys lead discussions. Their group has become so popular, a waitlist has formed. Caleb and Carina host a small-group Bible study in their home. Five atheists who joined their Meetup now attend the Bible study.

IMB President Paul Chitwood said he celebrates what God did in the 2025-26 season and what He is doing now to lead Southern Baptists toward historic generosity. “I thank God for Southern Baptists! With giving through the Lottie Moon offering at an all-time high, churches and individual givers continue to display a heart for the gospel to be proclaimed to every nation, all tribes, peoples and languages,” Chitwood said. The Annie total marked the second highest in NAMB’s history. The record Lottie Moon offering total surpassed last year’s total by more than $5 million and is the best offering in IMB history. “God is giving our generation unprecedented opportunity to send missionaries to the most unreached peoples and places,” Chitwood continued. “Though the challenges faced by our missionaries are enormous, the generosity of Southern Baptists ensures they have what they need to face those challenges and continue in the work while we hold the ropes with our support.” IMB missionary Landon Williams (center) walks with a Chilean pastor and a U.S. pastor on a remote island in Chile. Cooperation and generosity among Southern Baptists fuels the work to reach the uttermost parts of the world with the gospel. IMB Photo National goals for both offerings are set in partnership with Woman’s Missionary Union (WMU) each year. In response to the offering totals, Sandy Wisdom-Martin, executive director-treasurer of WMU, said: “As Southern Baptists, we are all in for His mission. When we give sacrificially, we prioritize the mission of God. Together our fervent prayers, our faithful generosity and our wholehearted obedience become channels for the gospel to reach our neighbors as well as the nations.” For the last 10 years, Southern Baptists have increasingly supported the Annie offering, setting records in seven of the last 10 years. Totals in each of the last four years have surpassed $70 million. “I am so grateful to the pastors and churches for the faithfulness and generosity they have demonstrated through this offering,” said NAMB president Kevin Ezell. “As I travel and speak in churches of all sizes, I love seeing the posters in the hallways showing their offering goals. Including church plants and replants, Southern Baptists have surpassed 700 new churches in four of the last five years. More than 12,000 churches have been planted since 2010.
